सोमप्रवहणे सोम यास्त इति तृचोऽनुवक्तव्यः । सूत्रितं च । सोम यास्ते मयोभुव इति तिस्रः । आ. ४-४ [?] इति ॥ आग्रयणे सौम्यस्य सोम यास्त इत्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । सोम यास्ते मयोभुवो या ते धामानि दिवि या पृथिव्याम् । २-९ [?] इति ॥ अश्वमेधेऽपि पौष्णमिष्ट्वा द्वितीयस्याज्यभागस्यैषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि सोम यास्ते मयोभुव इति सद्वंतौ । आ. १०-६ [?] इति ॥ हे सोम ते तव संबन्धिन्यो दाशुषे चरुपुरोडाशादीनि दत्तवते यजमानाय मयोभुवो मयसः सुखस्य भावयित्र्यो या ऊतयो रक्षाः संति विद्यन्ते ताभी रक्षाभिर्नोऽस्माकमविता रक्षिता भव ॥ मयोभुवः । अस्या ऊतिविशेषणत्वेन स्त्रीलिंगत्वे भुवश्च । पा. ४-१-४२ [?] इति ङीष् प्राप्नोति । तद्वोतो गुणवचनादित्यस्मादुत इति तपरकरणस्यानुवर्तनान्न भवति ॥

somapravahaṇe soma yās ta iti tṛco 'nuvaktavyaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | soma yās te mayobhuva iti tisraḥ | Ā. 4-4 [?] iti ‖ āgrayaṇe saumyasya soma yās ta ity eṣānuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | soma yās te mayobhuvo yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyām | 2-9 [?] iti ‖ aśvamedhe 'pi pauṣṇam iṣṭvā dvitīyasyājyabhāgasyaiṣānuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | tvam agne saprathā asi soma yās te mayobhuva iti sadvaṃtau | Ā. 10-6 [?] iti ‖ he soma te tava saṃbandhinyo dāśuṣe carupuroḍāśādīni dattavate yajamānāya mayobhuvo mayasaḥ sukhasya bhāvayitryo yā ūtayo rakṣāḥ saṃti vidyante tābhī rakṣābhir no 'smākam avitā rakṣitā bhava ‖ mayobhuvaḥ | asyā ūtiviśeṣaṇatvena strīliṃgatve bhuvaś ca | Pā. 4-1-42 [?] iti ṅīṣ prāpnoti | tadvoto guṇavacanād ity asmād uta iti taparakaraṇasyānuvartanān na bhavati ‖

Translation: "In the somapravahaṇa (conveying of Soma) the three Ṛks beginning soma yās te are to be recited; it is prescribed: 'soma yās te mayobhuva iti tisraḥ' (Ā. 4-4 [?]). In the Āgrayaṇa offering, for the Saumya, soma yās te is the anuvākyā; prescribed: 'soma yās te mayobhuvo yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyām' (2-9 [?]). In the Aśvamedha too, after the offering to Pūṣan, this is the anuvākyā for the second ājyabhāga; prescribed: 'tvam agne saprathā asi soma yās te mayobhuva', a pair [sadvantau] (Ā. 10-6 [?]). — O Soma, whichever ūtayaḥ (helps, protections) of yours, mayobhuvaḥ — producers of mayas, of happiness — exist for the sacrificer who gives oblations (dāśuṣe), such as the caru and puroḍāśa: with those protections be our avitā, our protector."

Grammar tail: mayobhuvaḥ — since it is an attribute of ūtayaḥ and is feminine, by bhuvaś ca (Pā. 4-1-42 [?]) the feminine suffix ṅīṣ would be obtained; but since in vāto guṇavacanāt the ta-restricted ut ["of a stem ending in u"] continues, it does not occur.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.9)

Soma — O Soma-deity; te — belonging to you; dāśuṣe — to the sacrificer who offers oblations; mayobhuvaḥ — which are causes of happiness; yāḥ ūtayaḥ — whichever means of protection; santi — there are; tābhiḥ — with those means of protection; naḥ — our; avitā — protector; bhava — be.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.9

"O Soma-deity, the sacrificer who offers you oblations, your devotee, trusts only in you for his protection. With whatever means of protection that are causes of happiness for him, be our protector too with all of them."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.9

"Soma, be our protector with these assistances which are sources of happiness to the offerer of oblations." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.9)

"In the somapravahaṇa the three Ṛks beginning soma yās te are the puronuvākyā mantras; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows this by the sūtra 'soma yās te mayobhuva iti tisraḥ'. And in the Āgrayaṇeṣṭi, in the offering to the Soma deity, soma —

original p. 357

"— yās te is to be used as the puronuvākyā mantra; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows this by the sūtra 'soma yās te mayobhuvo yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyām' (Ā. 2-9 [?]). And in the Aśvamedha sacrifice too, in the offering to the Pūṣan deity, this Ṛk is to be used as the puronuvākyā mantra for the second ājyabhāga oblation; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains it by the sūtra 'tvam agne saprathā asi soma yās te mayobhuva iti sadvantau' (Ā. 10-6 [?])."

dāśuṣe — dāśṛ dāne | "To the sacrificer who offers oblations."

ūtayaḥ — ūtir avanāt (Ni. 5-3 [?]) | "The author of the Nirukta explains that the word ūti is derived from the root av, which gives the sense 'protection', and cites the Ṛk ā tvā rathaṃ yatho-ūtaye (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-68-1 [?]) [as read; the citation is cut short in the print]. ūtayaḥ means 'protections'. What sort of protections? —"

mayobhuvaḥ — mayasaḥ sukhasya bhāvayitryaḥ | "Protections that are causes of happiness: this is the meaning. The nature of the happiness obtained from Soma is described in the Ṛks from Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-[?] to [?]. In general all the prayers that are made in the Ṛksaṃhitā to the deities, even though they proceed looking to happiness, are described in the prayer to the deity Soma as of a very high order of happiness:"

यत्र ज्योतिरजस्रं यस्मिँल्लोके स्वर्हितम् । तस्मिन्मां धेहि पवमानामृते लोके अक्षित इन्द्रायेन्दो परि स्रव ॥

yatra jyotir ajasraṃ yasmiṃl loke svarhitam | tasmin māṃ dhehi pavamānāmṛte loke akṣita indrāyendo pari srava ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-7 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Where there is unceasing light, in the world in which the sun is set — in that place put me, O purifying one, in the immortal, imperishable world; flow clear for Indra, O Indu."

यत्र कामा निकामाश्च यत्र ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् । स्वधा च यत्र तृप्तिश्च तत्र मामृतं कृधीन्द्रायेन्दो परि स्रव ॥

yatra kāmā nikāmāś ca yatra bradhnasya viṣṭapam | svadhā ca yatra tṛptiś ca tatra māmṛtaṃ kṛdhīndrāyendo pari srava ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-10 [?]; the print reads māmamṛtaṃ with an apparent extra ma [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Where there are desires and fulfilments, where is the vault of the sun, where is svadhā [the ancestral offering-food] and satisfaction — there make me immortal; flow clear for Indra, O Indu."

यत्रानन्दाश्च मोदाश्च मुदः प्रमुद आसते । कामस्य यत्राप्ताः कामास्तत्र मामृतं कृधीन्द्रायेन्दो परि स्रव ॥

yatrānandāś ca modāś ca mudaḥ pramuda āsate | kāmasya yatrāptāḥ kāmās tatra māmṛtaṃ kṛdhīndrāyendo pari srava ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-113-11 [?]; the same note on māmamṛtaṃ [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Where delights and joys, pleasures and ecstasies abide, where the desires of desire are attained — there make me immortal; flow clear for Indra, O Indu."

"The nature of the happiness described in these Ṛks surpasses even the happiness of heaven as it is ordinarily described: a happiness of the highest order, with joy, delight and ecstasy of the kind that has no craving left [nikāma]."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.9)

soma — vocative singular; since it stands at the head of the pāda, the āmantrita-nighāta does not occur; by āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198 [?]) the initial-acute accent.

original p. 358

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.9, continued (grammar page, noted briefly):

mayobhuvaḥ — mayasaḥ bhāvayitryaḥ mayobhuvaḥ; when mayas is the upapada, kvip after the root bhū. Though ūti here is feminine and the word is its attribute, so that by bhuvaś ca (Pā. 4-1-42 [?]) ṅīṣ would have to come, by vāto guṇavacanāt (वा तो गुणवचनात्, Pā. 4-1-44 [?]) the restriction to ut [a stem ending in u] continues, and it does not come; as it is lengthened, there is no ṅīṣ here. By aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ… (अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां…, Pā. 6-4-77 [?]), since jas follows, the uvaṅ replacement. santi — root as bhuvi; laṭ, third person plural; by śnasor allopaḥ (श्नसोरल्लोपः, Pā. 6-4-111 [?]) the a of the root as is elided; since yāḥ ("which") in the earlier part is related, the nighāta of the finite verb does not occur; by the suffix accent the initial acute. dāśuṣe — root ḍudāñ dāne; kvasu, as an irregular formation, by dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca (दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्च, Pā. 6-1-12 [?]); in the dative singular, by vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (वसोः संप्रसारणम्, Pā. 6-4-131 [?]) saṃprasāraṇa; by saṃprasāraṇāc ca (संप्रसारणाच्च) the preceding form; by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (शासिवसिघसीनां च, Pā. 8-3-60 [?]) the ṣatva of the s of vasu: dāśuṣe. avitā — root av rakṣaṇe; tṛc in the agent sense; by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः) the augment iṭ: avitṛ; the nominative singular, su following: an -an- replacement [the print names it anaṅ/ānaṅ, read doubtfully [?]]; by aptṛntṛcsvasṛ… (अप्तृन्तृच्स्वसृ…, the sūtra begins thus; the number not legible [?]) the lengthening of the penultimate; su-elision; n-elision; by cit (चितः, Pā. 6-1-163 [?]) the final syllable takes the acute. ‖ 9 ‖

Rik 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.10)

इमं यज्ञमिदं वचो जुजुषाण उपागहि । सोम त्वं नो वृधे भव ॥ १० ॥

imaṃ yajñam idaṃ vaco jujuṣāṇa upāgahi | soma tvaṃ no vṛdhe bhava ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.10)

इमम् । यज्ञम् । इदम् । वचः । जुजुषाणः । उपऽआगहि । सोम । त्वम् । नः । वृधे । भव ॥ १० ॥

imam | yajñam | idam | vacaḥ | jujuṣāṇaḥ | upa-āgahi | soma | tvam | naḥ | vṛdhe | bhava ‖ 10 ‖

original p. 359

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.10)

हे सोम त्वमिममस्माभिः क्रियमाणं यज्ञमिदं वच इदानीं क्रियमाणं स्तुतिलक्षणं वचनं जुजुषाणः सेवमानः सन् उपागहि । उपागच्छ । प्राचीनवंशलक्षणं गृहं प्राप्नुहि । प्राप्य च नोऽस्माकं वृधे यज्ञस्य वर्धनाय भव ॥ जुजुषाणः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । छन्दसि लिट् । लिटः कानच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । उपागहि । गमेर्लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना मकारलोपः । असिद्धवदत्रा भादित्यस्यासिद्धत्वाद्धेर्लुगभावः । गतिर्गतौ । पा. ८-१-७० [?] इति पूर्वस्य गतेर्निघातः ॥

he soma tvam imam asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇaṃ yajñam idaṃ vaca idānīṃ kriyamāṇaṃ stutilakṣaṇaṃ vacanaṃ jujuṣāṇaḥ sevamānaḥ san upāgahi | upāgaccha | prācīnavaṃśalakṣaṇaṃ gṛhaṃ prāpnuhi | prāpya ca no 'smākaṃ vṛdhe yajñasya vardhanāya bhava ‖ jujuṣāṇaḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | chandasi liṭ | liṭaḥ kānac | cita ity antodāttatvaṃ | upāgahi | gamer loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | anudāttopadeśety ādinā makāralopaḥ | asiddhavadatrā bhād ity asiddhatvād dher lugabhāvaḥ | gatir gatau | Pā. 8-1-70 [?] iti pūrvasya gater nighātaḥ ‖

Translation: "O Soma, accepting (jujuṣāṇaḥ) this sacrifice that is being performed by us and this word, the praise now being uttered, approach (upāgahi): come, attain the house, the prācīnavaṃśa [the hall with the eastward-facing roof-beam]. And having come, be for our vṛdhe, for the growth of the sacrifice."

Grammar tail: jujuṣāṇaḥ — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the liṭ in Chandas; the suffix kānac for the liṭ; by cit the final-acute. upāgahi — in the loṭ of gam, by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; by anudāttopadeśa… the loss of the m; by asiddhavad atrābhāt the m-loss counts as not having occurred, so that the elision of hi does not take place; by gatir gatau (Pā. 8-1-70 [?]) the nighāta of the preceding preverb.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.10)

Soma — O Soma-deity; tvam — you; imaṃ yajñam — this sacrifice (that we are bringing to fulfilment); idaṃ vacaḥ — this speech in the form of praise; jujuṣāṇaḥ — accepting and enjoying; upāgahi — come graciously (to this house of sacrifice of ours); naḥ — our; vṛdhe — for the growth (of the sacrifice); bhava — be (gracious).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.10

"O Soma-deity, come graciously to this house of sacrifice of ours, accepting and enjoying this sacrifice that we bring to fulfilment and this speech in the form of praise. And be a helper in the growth of our sacrifice."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.10

"O Soma, accepting this our sacrifice, and this our praise, approach us and be to us as the angmenter [sic] of our rite." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.10)

jujuṣāṇaḥ — juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | "One who enjoys: that is, one who graciously enjoys our sacrifice and our praise-speech with regard."

vṛdhe — vṛdhu vṛddhau | "For the growth, for the increase of our sacrifice."

मक्षि सोम वरुणं मक्षि मित्रं मक्षीन्द्रमिन्दो पवमान विष्णुम् । मक्षि शर्धो मारुतं मक्षि देवान्मक्षि महामिन्द्रमिन्दो मदाय ॥

makṣi soma varuṇaṃ makṣi mitraṃ makṣīndram indo pavamāna viṣṇum | makṣi śardho mārutaṃ makṣi devān makṣi mahām indram indo madāya ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-80-3 [?]; the Saṃhitā text as read, makṣi as printed [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Quickly [bring] Varuṇa, O Soma; quickly Mitra; quickly Indra, O Indu, and the purifying Viṣṇu; quickly the host of the Maruts; quickly the gods; quickly great Indra, O Indu, for exhilaration."

original p. 360

"As said in Ṛks such as these, the satisfaction of all the deities, which is the means to the final end of the sacrifice, arises from the drinking of Soma; so Soma himself is the chief cause of the growth of our sacrifice. Therefore there is the prayer 'cause our sacrifice to grow'. Moreover, as described in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-2-10 [?], 9-6-8 [?] and the like, Soma himself is yajñātmā, the self of the sacrifice; therefore he is the cause of the growth of the sacrifice."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.10)

jujuṣāṇaḥ — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; in the present sense, by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, Pā. 3-4-6 [?]) the liṭ; by liṭaḥ kānajvā (लिटः कानज्वा, Pā. 3-2-106 [?]) kānac for the liṭ; the root is doubled, the reduplicative keeps halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; by aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi [the sūtra read as "āṭkupvāj…", partial] the ṇatva of the n; by cit (चितः, Pā. 6-1-163 [?]) the final-acute. upāgahi — upa + ā, the preverbs (gatiś ca); root gam gatau; loṭ, second person singular, sip; by serhy apicca (सेर्ह्यपिच्च) hi is the replacement; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; since by the prescription of non-pit the hi is ṅit, by anudāttopadeśa… (अनुदात्तोपदेश…, Pā. 6-4-37 [?]) the nasal m of the root is elided; by asiddhavad atrābhāt (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, Pā. 6-4-22 [?]) the m-elision counts as not having occurred, so the elision of hi by ato heḥ (अतो हेः) does not come; since upa is a gati and ā [a preverb with the same name] follows, by gatir gatau (Pā. 8-1-70 [?]) the preceding preverb (upa) takes the nighāta accent. vṛdhe — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; after the suffix kvip the word is vṛdh; the dative singular; by sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः, Pā. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the acute. ‖ 10 ‖

Rik 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.11)

सोम गीर्भिष्ट्वा वयं वर्धयामो वचोविदः । सुमृळीको न आ विश ॥ ११ ॥

soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayaṃ vardhayāmo vacovidaḥ | sumṛḷīko na ā viśa ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 361

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.11)

सोम । गीःऽभिः । त्वा । वयम् । वर्धयामः । वचःऽविदः । सुऽमृळीकः । नः । आ । विश ॥ ११ ॥

soma | gīḥ-bhiḥ | tvā | vayam | vardhayāmaḥ | vacaḥ-vidaḥ | su-mṛḷīkaḥ | naḥ | ā | viśa ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.11)

दर्शयागे सौम्यस्याज्यभागस्य सोम गीर्भिरित्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । अग्निः प्रत्नेन मन्मना सोम गीर्भिष्ट्वा वयं । आ. १-३ [?] इति । अन्यत्रापि यत्र वृधन्वन्तावाज्यभागौ तत्रैषा द्वितीयाज्यभागानुवाक्या ॥ हे सोम त्वा त्वां वचोविदः स्तुतिलक्षणानां वचसां वेदितारो वयमनुष्ठातारो गीर्भिः स्तुतिलक्षणैर्वचोभिर्वर्धयामः । प्रवृद्धं कुर्मः । तादृक्त्वं च नोऽस्माकं सुमृळीकः शोभनं सुखं कुर्वन्सन् आ विश । आगच्छ ॥ सुमृळीकः । मृड सुखने । मृडेः कीकनकनौ । उ. ४-२४ [?] इति भावे कीकन्प्रत्ययः । शोभनं मृडीकं यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं ॥

darśayāge saumyasyājyabhāgasya soma gīrbhir ity eṣānuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | agniḥ pratnena manmanā soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayaṃ | Ā. 1-3 [?] iti | anyatrāpi yatra vṛdhanvantāv ājyabhāgau tatraiṣā dvitīyājyabhāgānuvākyā ‖ he soma tvā tvāṃ vacovidaḥ stutilakṣaṇānāṃ vacasāṃ veditāro vayam anuṣṭhātāro gīrbhiḥ stutilakṣaṇair vacobhir vardhayāmaḥ | pravṛddhaṃ kurmaḥ | tādṛk tvaṃ ca no 'smākaṃ sumṛḷīkaḥ śobhanaṃ sukhaṃ kurvan san ā viśa | āgaccha ‖ sumṛḷīkaḥ | mṛḍa sukhane | mṛḍeḥ kīkanakanau | U. 4-24 [?] iti bhāve kīkanpratyayaḥ | śobhanaṃ mṛḍīkaṃ yasyeti bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ ‖

Translation: "At the Darśa (new-moon) sacrifice, for the ājyabhāga of the Saumya, soma gīrbhiḥ is the anuvākyā; prescribed: 'agniḥ pratnena manmanā soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayam' (Ā. 1-3 [?]); and elsewhere too, wherever there are ājyabhāga oblations with the vṛdhanvat Ṛks, this is the anuvākyā of the second ājyabhāga. — O Soma, we, vacovidaḥ — the knowers of the words of praise, the performers — gīrbhiḥ, with words of praise, vardhayāmaḥ tvā — we make you grow, we render you exalted. And you, such as you are, sumṛḷīkaḥ — making good happiness for us — ā viśa, come."

Grammar tail: sumṛḷīkaḥ — root mṛḍa sukhane; the Uṇādi kīkan (mṛḍeḥ kīkanakanau, U. 4-24 [?]) in the abstract sense; śobhanaṃ mṛḍīkaṃ yasya — a bahuvrīhi; by nañsubhyām the final-member final-acute.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.11)

Soma — O Soma-deity; tvā — you; vacovidaḥ — familiar with praise-words; vayam — we; gīrbhiḥ — by the praise-words; vardhayāmaḥ — cause to grow (exalt); naḥ — to us; sumṛḷīkaḥ — an excellent bringer of happiness; ā viśa — be gracious.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.11

"O Soma-deity, the way of praising you is well known to us. With pure praise-words we praise you and cause you to grow. Come here as the maker of the most excellent happiness for us."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.11

"Acquainted with hymns we elevate you with praises ; do you who are benignant approach." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.11) Kannada; begins at the foot of p. 361

"In the Darśayāga, when the ājyabhāga oblation is offered to the Soma deity, the mantra soma gīrbhiḥ is the puronuvākyā mantra, says the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: 'agniḥ pratnena manmanā soma

original p. 362

Special Topics of Rik 91.11, continued from p. 361 (Kannada): "— gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayam' (Ā. 1-3 [?]). In other places too — that is, wherever the ājyabhāga oblations with the vṛdhanvatī Ṛks occur — it should be understood that this mantra is the puronuvākyā of the second ājyabhāga."

vacovidaḥ — vacasāṃ stutīnāṃ jñātāraḥ | "That is, those who know well the nature of the words of praise and so praise the deities. The word vacas here means 'praise'. For instance, in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?] [?]; 8-[?]-[?] [?] and the like, and in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-31-10 [?] cited by the author of the Nirukta (Ni. 10-31 [?]), the word vacas has the sense of 'praise' too. Therefore vacovidaḥ means those who, knowing well the nature of praise, praise the deities in the proper order."

gīrbhiḥ — stutayo giraḥ | "The author of the Nirukta explains gir as derived from the root gṝ (gṛṇāteḥ, Ni. 1-11 [?]), which gives the sense 'to speak', and says that the word giraḥ in the Ṛk tam id vardhantu no giraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-8 [?]) means 'praises'. Since the same sense is found in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?] [?]; 8-[?]-[?] [?] and other Ṛks, gīrbhiḥ here too means 'by praises'. Because all deities are fond of praise, and because they attain growth by praises given with satisfaction, here too it is 'by speech in the form of praise'."

vardhayāmaḥ — pravṛddhaṃ kurmaḥ | "We make you grow, that is, we praise so that you may grow — this is the meaning, as in the Ṛk tam id vardhantu no giraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-8 [?])."

sumṛḷīkaḥ — mṛḷa sukhane | śobhanaṃ sukhaṃ kurvan san | "Be gracious, making the most excellent happiness for us. The nature of the happiness described in the eleven Ṛks of the 113th sūkta of Ṛ. Saṃ. 9 [as read, doubtful [?]] has been explained in the commentary on the Ṛk 9-[?]-[?] [?]."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.11)

gīrbhiḥ — the word gir; the instrumental plural, bhis following; by r-vor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ (र्वोरुपधाया दीर्घ इकः, Pā. 8-2-76 [?]; printed "वोरुपधाया दीर्घः…") the penultimate i is lengthened. vardhayāmaḥ — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; in the causative sense ṇic; by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च, Pā. 7-3-86 [?]) the guṇa of the light penultimate; by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ the ṇic-ending stem is a root; then laṭ; in the first person plural mas; śap; the guṇa of ṇic because of it; the ay replacement; by ato dīrgho yañi (अतो दीर्घो यञि) the lengthening of the stem-final a; since at the head of the pāda, no nighāta; the accent of ṇic appears.

original p. 363

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.11, continued (grammar page, noted briefly):

vacovidaḥ — vacāṃsi vidanti iti vacovidaḥ; root vida jñāne; the suffix kvip; the nominative plural; by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्) the kṛdanta final member keeps its natural accent. sumṛḷīkaḥ — root mṛḍa sukhane; by mṛḍeḥ kīkankakanau (मृडेः कीकन्कनौ [?], U. 4-46 [?] — the figure is read "४-४६" here, whereas p. 361 gave "४-२४" [?]) the suffix kīkan in the abstract sense; the stem mṛḍīka; śobhanaṃ mṛḍīkaṃ yasya sa sumṛḷīkaḥ — in the bahuvrīhi compound, by nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्, Pā. 6-2-172 [?]) the final syllable of the final member is acute. viśa — root viśa praveśane; loṭ, second person singular; by the nighāta of a finite verb following. ‖ 11 ‖

Rik 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.12)

गयस्फानो अमीवहा वसुवित्पुष्टिवर्धनः । सुमित्रः सोम नो भव ॥ १२ ॥

gayasphāno amīvahā vasuvit puṣṭivardhanaḥ | sumitraḥ soma no bhava ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.12)

गयऽस्फानः । अमीवऽहा । वसुऽवित् । पुष्टिऽवर्धनः । सुऽमित्रः । सोम । नः । भव ॥ १२ ॥

gaya-sphānaḥ | amīva-hā | vasu-vit | puṣṭi-vardhanaḥ | su-mitraḥ | soma | naḥ | bhava ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.12) begins on p. 363

संति पवमानेष्टयस्तिस्रः । तत्र तृतीयस्यामिष्टावुत्तरस्याज्यभागस्य गयस्फान इत्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । पुष्टिमंतावग्निना रयिमश्नवद्गयस्फानो अमीवहा । आ. २-१ [?] इति ॥ एषैव प्रातःकालीनोपसदि सौम्ययागस्य याज्या सायंकालीनायां त्वनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं चाथोपसदिति खण्डे । त्वं सोमासि सत्पतिर्गयस्फानो अमीवहा । आ. ४-८ [?] इति ॥

santi pavamāneṣṭayas tisraḥ | tatra tṛtīyasyām iṣṭāv uttarasyājyabhāgasya gayasphāna ity eṣānuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | puṣṭimantāv agninā rayim aśnavad gayasphāno amīvahā | Ā. 2-1 [?] iti ‖ eṣaiva prātaḥkālīnopasadi saumyayāgasya yājyā sāyaṃkālīnāyāṃ tvanuvākyā | sūtritaṃ cāthopasad iti khaṇḍe | tvaṃ somāsi satpatir gayasphāno amīvahā | Ā. 4-8 [?] iti ‖

original p. 364

गयस्फानः । गये इति धननाम । धनस्य वर्धयिता अमीवहा अमीवानां रोगाणां हन्ता वसुवित् स्तोतॄणां धनस्य लम्भयिता प्रापयिता पुष्टिवर्धनः पुष्टेः संपदो वर्धयिता सुमित्रः शोभनानि मित्राणि सखायो यस्य स तथोक्तः । हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्माकमेवंगुणविशिष्टो भव ॥ गयस्फानः । स्फायी वृद्धौ । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात् ल्युटि व्यत्ययेन यलोपः । इदमादिषु चतुर्षु पदेषु कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सुमित्रः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

gayasphānaḥ | gaye iti dhananāma | dhanasya vardhayitā amīvahā amīvānāṃ rogāṇāṃ hantā vasuvit stotṝṇāṃ dhanasya lambhayitā prāpayitā puṣṭivardhanaḥ puṣṭeḥ saṃpado vardhayitā sumitraḥ śobhanāni mitrāṇi sakhāyo yasya sa tathoktaḥ | he soma tvaṃ no 'smākam evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭo bhava ‖ gayasphānaḥ | sphāyī vṛddhau | antarbhāvitaṇyarthāt lyuṭi vyatyayena yalopaḥ | idamādiṣu caturṣu padeṣu kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | sumitraḥ | nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam ‖

Translation: "There are three Pavamāneṣṭis. In the third of these, the iṣṭi, this Ṛk gayasphānaḥ is the anuvākyā of the latter ājyabhāga; it is prescribed: 'puṣṭimantāv agninā rayim aśnavad gayasphāno amīvahā' (Ā. 2-1 [?]). This same Ṛk is the yājyā of the Soma-offering at the morning upasad, and the anuvākyā at the evening one; it is prescribed in the section athopasad: 'tvaṃ somāsi satpatir gayasphāno amīvahā' (Ā. 4-8 [?]). — Gayasphānaḥ — gaya is a name for wealth: the augmenter of wealth. Amīvahā — the slayer of diseases (amīvā). Vasuvit — he who obtains for the praisers, who causes them to reach, wealth. Puṣṭivardhanaḥ — the augmenter of nourishment, of prosperity. Sumitraḥ — he who has good friends, good companions. O Soma, be for us endowed with these qualities."

Grammar tail: gayasphānaḥ — root sphāyī vṛddhau; from the root with the causative sense included, the suffix lyuṭ, by vyatyaya the y is dropped; in these four words beginning with this, the final member, a kṛdanta, keeps its natural accent. sumitraḥ — by nañsubhyām the final-member final-acute.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.12)

Soma — O Soma-deity; naḥ — to us; gayasphānaḥ — one who makes wealth grow; amīvahā — a destroyer of diseases; vasuvit — one who obtains (for the praisers) wealth; puṣṭivardhanaḥ — one who makes the wealth of nourishment grow; sumitraḥ — an excellent friend; bhava — be.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.12

"O Soma-deity, be for us one who makes our wealth grow, a destroyer of disease, a giver of wealth, a maker of the wealth of nourishment to grow, and an excellent friend."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.12

"O Soma, be unto us, the bestower of wealth, the remover of desease [sic], the cognizant of riches, the augmenter of nourishment and an excellent friend." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.12)

"There are three iṣṭis named Pavamāneṣṭi. In the third of these, for the final ājyabhāga oblation, the Ṛk gayasphānaḥ is to be used as the puronuvākyā mantra; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows this by the sūtra 'puṣṭimantāv agninā rayim aśnavad gayasphāno amīvahā' (Ā. 2-1 [?]). And in the upasad iṣṭi performed in the morning, in the sacrifice belonging to Soma, this mantra is the puronuvākyā in the evening; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section athopasad, makes it clear by the sūtra 'tvaṃ somāsi satpatir gayasphāno amīvahā' (Ā. 4-8 [?])."

gayasphānaḥ — gaye iti dhananāma | dhanasya vardhayitā | "The meaning is the one who makes wealth grow. The word gaya has three meanings: progeny, house and wealth. tuk, tokaṃ, —

original p. 365

Special Topics of Rik 91.12, continued from p. 364 (Kannada) — the sentence broken at the foot of p. 364 continues: "tuk, tokaṃ, tanayaḥ and the like, since the word gayaḥ is read among the names for offspring (apatya) (Ni. 3-2 [?]), gayaḥ may mean offspring; since it is read among the names for wealth, such as mīḷhaṃ, rekṇaḥ (Ni. 2-10 [?]), it may mean wealth; and since it is read among the names for house, such as gayaḥ, kṛvaraṃ, harmyam (Ni. 3-4 [?]), it may mean house. Sāyaṇācārya, in explaining the Ṛk 3-10-3 [?] of the Ṛksaṃhitā, says 'gamyate nivāsāya iti gayaṃ gṛhaṃ, gīyate stūyate iti vā gayaṃ dhanam' ['that to which one goes for dwelling is gaya, the house; or that which is sung, praised, is gaya, wealth']. Besides, he explains gaye in the Ṛk 6-24-2 [?] as 'gṛhaṃ gṛhagataṃ prāṇijātaṃ vā' ['the house, or the creatures belonging to the house']. Of these three meanings here, any one may be taken. In Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya too: 'sphāyir vṛddhyarthaḥ | apatyasya dhanasya gṛhasya vā vardhayitā gayasphānaḥ' ['sphāyī has the sense of growth; gayasphānaḥ is the one who makes grow offspring, wealth or house']. Soma too has the epithet gayasādhana, as in —"

समी वत्सं न मातृभिः सृजता गयसाधनम् ।

samī vatsaṃ na mātṛbhiḥ sṛjatā gayasādhanam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-104-2 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Release him [Soma] like a calf with the mothers [the waters], the accomplisher of the house [or wealth]."

"— and in this Ṛk too all three meanings may be given."

amīvahā — amu rogeḥ [as read] | "From the word amu that gives the sense 'disease', the word amīva is derived; he who destroys it is well known as amīvahā. Prayers to Soma for the destruction of disease are found in many places, for example —"

इन्द्राय सोम सुषुतः परि स्रवापामीवा भवतु रक्षसा सह ।

indrāya soma suṣutaḥ pari sravāpāmīvā bhavatu rakṣasā saha | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-85-1 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Well pressed, O Soma, flow clear for Indra; let disease be driven off together with the Rakṣas."

सोमारुद्रा वि वृहतं विषूचीममीवा या नो गयमाविवेश ।

somārudrā vi vṛhataṃ viṣūcīm amīvā yā no gayam āvivesa | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-74-2 [?]; the final word of the citation is printed āveśa, read as āviveśa [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "O Soma and Rudra, tear apart the spreading disease that has entered our house [or wealth]."

"— in these Ṛks Soma is prayed to for help in destroying disease. Amīvahā also means the destroyer of harmful enemies."

vasuvit — dhanasya prāpayitā | "One who brings wealth together. The word vasu also means food (Ni. 2-9 [?]); therefore he may also be the giver of food. The names vasuvit, hiraṇyavit, govit are well known of Soma, for example —"

गोवित्पवस्व वसुविद्धिरण्यविद्रेतोधा इन्दो भुवनेष्वर्पितः ।

govit pavasva vasuvid dhiraṇyavid retodhā indo bhuvaneṣv arpitaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-39 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Flow clear, finder of cows, finder of wealth, finder of gold, bearer of seed, O Indu, placed in the worlds."

"— in this Ṛk all three of these epithets occur. In the Ṛk 3-40-6 [?] he is called rayipatiḥ ('lord of wealth')."

original p. 366

puṣṭivardhanaḥ — puṣṭeḥ saṃpado vardhayitā | "Because he destroys all diseases and grants wealth and prosperity, 'he who increases nourishment of every kind' is the meaning."

sumitraḥ — śobhanāni mitrāṇi yasya saḥ | "One who has excellent friends: this is the meaning. Or śobhanānāṃ mitrāṇāṃ kartā: one who provides good friends."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.12)

gayasphānaḥ — root sphāyī vṛddhau, a root with the causative sense included (the sense of impelling is contained in it); the suffix lyuṭ; when a y is intended, by vyatyayo bahulam (व्यत्ययो बहुलम्) the y of the root is elided; gayasya sphānaḥ; by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 [?]) the final member, a kṛdanta, keeps its natural accent. Since in this mantra the four words beginning with this one all have a kṛdanta final member, the same sūtra gives the natural accent of the final member everywhere. amīvahā — amīvānāṃ hantā; root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate (अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते, Pā. 3-2-178 [?]) the suffix kvip; the stem amīvahan; the nominative singular. vasuvit — root vidḷ lābhe; this too has the causative sense included; the suffix kvip. puṣṭivardhanaḥ — puṣṭeḥ vardhayitā; root vṛdhu vṛddhau; the sense of the causative included; then lyuṭ; by yuvor anākau (युवोरनाकौ, Pā. 7-1-1 [?]) ana for yu. sumitraḥ — śobhanāni mitrāṇi yasya saḥ; by nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्, Pā. 6-2-172 [?]) the final syllable of the final member is acute. ‖ 12 ‖

Rik 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.13)

सोम रारन्धि नो हृदि गावो न यवसेष्वा । मर्य इव स्व ओक्ये ॥ १३ ॥

soma rārandhi no hṛdi gāvo na yavaseṣv ā | marya iva sva okye ‖ 13 ‖

original p. 367

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.13)

सोम । ररन्धि । नः । हृदि । गावः । न । यवसेषु । आ । मर्यःऽइव । स्वे । ओक्ये ॥ १३ ॥

soma | rarandhi | naḥ | hṛdi | gāvaḥ | na | yavaseṣu | ā | maryaḥ-iva | sve | okye ‖ 13 ‖

(The Saṃhitā prints rārandhi, the Pada rarandhi; the Saṃhitā's lengthening is treated in the grammar tail below. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.13)

हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्माकं हृदि हृदये रारन्धि रमस्व । तत्र निदर्शनमुच्यते । गावो न । यथा गावो यवसेषु शोभनतृणेष्वाभिमुख्येन रमन्ते । मर्य इव । यथा वा मर्यो मरणधर्मा मनुष्यः स्व ओक्ये स्वकीये ओकसि गृहे पुत्रादिभिः सह रमते तद्वदस्माभिर्दत्तेन हविषा तृप्तः सन् अस्मास्वेवावतिष्ठस्व । नान्यत्र गच्छेति निदर्शनद्वयस्य तात्पर्यार्थः ॥ ररन्धि । रमु क्रीडायां । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । छन्दस्युभयथेति हेरार्धधातुकत्वेन ङित्त्वाभावादङित्केति [?] हेर्धिः । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हेरपित्त्वात्तस्यैव स्वरः शिष्यते । छान्दसमभ्यासदीर्घत्वं । आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वात्पदादपरत्वेन निघाताभावः । मर्य इव । छन्दसि निष्कर्क्येत्यादौ मर्यशब्दो यत्प्रत्ययान्तो निपात्यते । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । ओक्ये । उच समवाये । उच्यते समवेयते प्राप्यत इत्योक्यं गृहं । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । चजोः कु घिण्यतोरिति कुत्वं । तित्स्वरितः ॥

he soma tvaṃ no 'smākaṃ hṛdi hṛdaye rārandhi ramasva | tatra nidarśanam ucyate | gāvo na | yathā gāvo yavaseṣu śobhanatṛṇeṣv ābhimukhyena ramante | marya iva | yathā vā maryo maraṇadharmā manuṣyaḥ sva okye svakīye okasi gṛhe putrādibhiḥ saha ramate tadvad asmābhir dattena haviṣā tṛptaḥ san asmāsv evāvatiṣṭhasva | nānyatra gaccheti nidarśanadvayasya tātparyārthaḥ ‖ rarandhi | ramu krīḍāyāṃ | vyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | chandasy ubhayatheti herārdhadhātukatvena ṅittvābhāvād aṅitketi [?] her dhiḥ | ser hy apicceti herapittvāt tasyaiva svaraḥ śiṣyate | chāndasam abhyāsadīrghatvaṃ | āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavad iti pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvāt padād aparatvena nighātābhāvaḥ | marya iva | chandasi niṣkarkyety ādau maryaśabdo yatpratyayānto nipātyate | yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | okye | uca samavāye | ucyate samaveyate prāpyata ity okyaṃ gṛhaṃ | ṛhaloṇ yat | cajoḥ ku ghiṇyator iti kutvaṃ | titsvaritaḥ ‖

Translation: "O Soma, in our hṛdi — our heart — rārandhi, delight; here the comparison is given: gāvo na — as cows delight, facing [the food], in the yavaseṣu, the good pastures; marya iva — or as a mortal man, one subject to death, delights in his own okye, his own house, with his sons and others: so, satisfied with the oblation we give, abide with us alone, and go nowhere else — this is the intention of the two comparisons."

Grammar tail (clotted in the print; characterized, not transcribed): rarandhi — root ramu krīḍāyām; the parasmaipada by vyatyaya; bahulaṃ chandasi — ślu for śap; by chandasy ubhayathā the hi is ārdhadhātuka, and not being ṅit, hi becomes dhi [the cited rule aṅitka… partly read [?]]; by ser hy apicca, since hi is non-pit, its own accent remains; the lengthening of the reduplicative is Vedic. āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat — the preceding vocative counts as non-existent, so the nighāta, which presupposes a preceding word, does not occur. marya iva — the word marya, ending in the suffix yat, is irregularly formed [in the section beginning chandasi niṣkarkya…]; by yato 'nāvaḥ the initial-acute. okye — root uca samavāye; "ucyate samaveyate prāpyata ity okyaṃ gṛhaṃ"; the suffix ṇyat by ṛhaloṇ yat; the ku substitution by cajoḥ ku ghiṇyatoḥ; tit — svarita.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.13)

Soma — O Soma-deity; yavaseṣu — in green pastures; ā — all around; gāvo na — like cows who delight; sve okye — in his own house; marya iva — like a man (with his sons and others), in contentment delighting; tvam — you; naḥ — our; hṛdi — in the heart; rarandhi (rārandhi) — delight.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.13

"O Soma-deity, as cows, entering the rich green pastures, without going out, delight there; and as a man in his own house, with his sons, grandsons and the rest, delights in contentment without wishing to go elsewhere: so you, abiding in our heart, with no other going, delight in contentment." The English translation and Special Topics of 91.13 begin on p. 368.

original p. 368

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.13

"Soma, dwell happy in our hearts, like cattle in fresh pastures, like men in their own abodes." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.13)

okye — oka iti nivāsanāmocyate [as read] (Ni. 3-3 [?]) | "A dwelling-place is called oka. sve okye means 'in one's own house'. To show that a man has complete self-regard (abhimāna) in his own house, the author of the Nirukta gives an example (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-4-8 [?]): 'atha sa okaḥ punar eva tad eti yata āgato bhavati' (Ni. 3-3 [?]) [as read]. Even if one has gone abroad, one's self-regard is in the house; one returns there; so one's own house is the object of complete self-regard. In this Ṛk the ṛṣi prays to Soma to keep that very self-regard and independence in our heart and to show affection."

maryaḥ — martyo manuṣyo maraṇadharmā (Ni. 2-[?] [?]) | "One whose nature is to die: hence the name marya."

rarandhi (rārandhi) — ramu krīḍāyām | "'Sport and experience delight' is the meaning: as delight is obtained by cattle in green pastures, and by a man in his own house, so may you obtain that very delight in our heart."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.13)

rarandhi — root ramu krīḍāyām; by vyatyayo bahulam (व्यत्ययो बहुलम्) the parasmaipada; loṭ, second person singular, sip; hi for it; by bahulaṃ chandasi ślu for śap; by ślau (श्लौ, Pā. 6-1-10 [?]) the root is doubled; in the reduplicative halādiḥ śeṣaḥ. When rarama + hi has come, by chandasy ubhayathā (छन्दस्युभयथा, Pā. 3-4-117 [?]) hi has the name ārdhadhātuka, and, not being ṅit [print: "jit"?], by ajantāc ca (as read, Pā. 6-4-103 [?]) hi has dhi as its replacement; on this account, because it is not ṅit, the nasal m of the root is not elided by anudāttopadeśa…; by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि) the m becomes anusvāra [i.e. n]: hence rarandhi. As soma, a vocative, stands before, by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat (Pā. 8-1-72 [?]) it counts as non-existent, and by tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. 8-1-28 [?]) there is no nighāta. Since the non-pit (apit) was prescribed, the suffix accent comes; then the final syllable of rarandhi is acute. In the Saṃhitā, the lengthening of the reduplicative is Vedic.

original p. 369

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.13, continued (grammar page, noted briefly):

hṛdi — the word hṛdaya; the locative singular follows; by padd annomās hṛn… (पद्दन्नोमास्हृन्…, as printed, Pā. 6-1-63 [?]) the replacement hṛd; by ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171, numerals read "६-१-१७१" in the print) the case-ending takes the acute. This clears the doubt recorded on p. 343 over the number of the same sūtra. marya iva — by chandasi niṣkarkyadeva… (as printed, Pā. 3-1-123 [?]) the word marya is formed irregularly, ending in the suffix yat; by yato 'nāvaḥ (यतोऽनावः, Pā. 6-1-213 [?]) the svarita is set aside and the initial-acute accent comes. okye — root uca samavāye; "ucyate samaveyate prāpyate iti okyaṃ gṛham" (the house, a dwelling-place); by ṛhaloṇ yat (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्, Pā. 3-1-124 [?]) the suffix ṇyat; by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca the guṇa of the light penultimate before the suffix; by cajoḥ ku ghiṇyatoḥ (चजोः कु घिण्यतोः, Pā. 7-3-52 [?]) the ku substitution of the root's c, caused by the ṇit suffix: hence okya. As the suffix is tit, by tit svaritam (तित्स्वरितम्, Pā. 6-1-185 [?]) the svarita accent. The locative singular. ‖ 13 ‖

Rik 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.14)

यः सोम सख्ये तव रारणद्देव मर्त्यः । तं दक्षः सचते कविः ॥ १४ ॥

yaḥ soma sakhye tava rāraṇad deva martyaḥ | taṃ dakṣaḥ sacate kaviḥ ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.14)

यः । सोम । सख्ये । तव । ररणत् । देव । मर्त्यः । तम् । दक्षः । सचते । कविः ॥ १४ ॥

yaḥ | soma | sakhye | tava | raraṇat | deva | martyaḥ | tam | dakṣaḥ | sacate | kaviḥ ‖ 14 ‖

(The Saṃhitā prints rāraṇat, the Pada raraṇat. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.14) begins at the foot of p. 369

हे देव द्योतमान सोम तव सख्ये त्वदीये सखित्वे निमित्तभूते सति यो मर्त्यो मरणधर्मा यजमानो रारणत् रणति एतत्सूक्तरूपेण त्वां

he deva dyotamāna soma tava sakhye tvadīye sakhitve nimittabhūte sati yo martyo maraṇadharmā yajamāno rāraṇat raṇati etatsūktarūpeṇa tvāṃ

original p. 370

स्तौति तं यजमानं कविः क्रान्तदर्शी दक्षः सर्वकार्यसमर्थस्त्वं सचते । सेवसे । अनुगृह्णासीत्यर्थः ॥ रारणत् । रण शब्दार्थः । लेटि अडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । छन्दस्युभयथेत्यार्धधातुकत्वाद्[clotted — the phrase dyanniṭi lasārvadhātuke vidhīyamānasyābhyastād yudāttatvasyābhāve, as read [?]] धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । सचते । षच समवाये । पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥

stauti taṃ yajamānaṃ kaviḥ krāntadarśī dakṣaḥ sarvakāryasamarthas tvaṃ sacate | sevase | anugṛhṇāsīty arthaḥ ‖ rāraṇat | raṇa śabdārthaḥ | leṭi aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | chandasy ubhayathety ārdhadhātukatvād [clotted [?]] dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | sacate | ṣaca samavāye | puruṣavyatyayaḥ ‖

Translation: "O Deva, shining Soma, in your friendship — you being the cause of that friendship — the mortal, the dying sacrificer who rāraṇat, 'sounds forth', praises you in the form of this sūkta: that sacrificer, you, the kavi, the far-seeing, dakṣa, capable of every task, sacate, serve — you favour him: this is the meaning."

Grammar tail (partly clotted; characterized): rāraṇat — the root raṇa, in the sense of sound; in the leṭ the augment aṭ; by bahulaṃ chandasi ślu for śap; by itaś ca lopaḥ the elision of the i; by chandasy ubhayathā, as the suffix is ārdhadhātuka, [the following clause, on the abhyasta-accent in the sārvadhātuka, is clotted in the print [?]] the accent of the root remains. sacate — root ṣaca samavāye; the change of person (puruṣavyatyaya): the middle form for the second person.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.14)

deva — O shining one; Soma — O Soma-deity; tava — your; sakhye — in friendship [as its cause]; yaḥ martyaḥ — whichever sacrificer; rāraṇat — praises you with a hymn in the form of the sūkta; tam — that sacrificer; kaviḥ — one of divine sight; dakṣaḥ — you, capable of every task; sacate — you serve (you favour).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.14

"O shining Soma-deity, the service one does for you is never in vain. For the sacrificer who, for the sake of friendship with you, praises you with a hymn in the form of a sūkta, you, who have divine sight and are capable of every task, show favour without fail."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.14

"The experienced sage commends the mortal who, divine Soma, praises you through affection." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.14)

rāraṇat — raṇati etatsūktarūpeṇa tvāṃ stauti | "Sāyaṇa gives the meaning 'he praises you in the form of this sūkta'. From the root raṇa śabde, which gives the sense of sound, he shows this form's derivation and takes the word to be 'a sound in the form of a hymn'. But Skandasvāmin's meaning seems more apt than this: 'rāraṇat — atyantaṃ ramate', 'he delights exceedingly'. If one looks at the context, the sense that 'we experience the happiness that is the fruit of friendship with you' is natural. Such senses of delight are found in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?], and also —"

नाहमिन्द्राणि रारण सख्युर्वृषाकपेरृते ।

nāham indrāṇi rāraṇa sakhyur vṛṣākaper ṛte | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-13 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "I, O Indrāṇī, take no delight without my friend Vṛṣākapi."

original p. 371

Special Topics of Rik 91.14, continued from p. 370 (Kannada): "— on this Ṛk the bhāṣya-writers explain 'na rarāṇa na rame' [as read, doubtful [?]]."

kaviḥ — "It has been said many times before that this word has the senses 'far-seeing' and 'intelligent', and what is distinctive in it."

martyaḥ — "Like the word marya: 'one subject to death, a human being'."

sacate — "He serves."

taṃ dakṣaḥ sacate kaviḥ — "For this latter half of the Ṛk, Sāyaṇa's construction is one way, and Skandasvāmin's is another. kaviḥ — the wise, or far-seeing; dakṣaḥ — you, capable of every task; taṃ — that sacrificer; sacate — you serve, that is, you favour: so Sāyaṇa. Skandasvāmin explains: kaviḥ — the sacrificer, the intelligent one; taṃ dakṣaḥ — that strength, or that growth; sacate — he enjoys, that is, he experiences."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.14)

sakhye — sakhyuḥ bhāvaḥ sakhyam; by sakhyur yaḥ (सख्युर्यः, Pā. 5-1-126 [?]) the suffix ya; by the suffix accent the final syllable is acute. raraṇat — root raṇa śabde; leṭ, third person singular, tip; by itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97 [?]) the i is elided; by bahulaṃ chandasi ślu for śap; by ślau the doubling of the root; the reduplicative keeps its first consonant and vowel (ādir halaḥ śeṣaḥ); by leṭo 'ḍāṭau the augment aṭ for the suffix. Since yaḥ ("who") precedes and is related, by yadvṛttān nityam (यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम्, Pā. 8-1-66 [?]) the nighāta is prohibited; by chandasy ubhayathā the suffix has the name ārdhadhātuka, so that for the non-iṭ sārvadhātuka beginning with a vowel the initial-acute that abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189 [?]) would give does not come; the accent of the root remains; the reduplicative is short in the Pada by Vedic usage [the Saṃhitā prints it long]. sacate — root ṣaca samavāye; by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ the initial ṣ becomes s; by vyatyayo bahulam the third-person singular suffix replaces the second-person singular; by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e the final e; by kartari śap the śap; the nighāta since a finite verb follows a word. ‖ 14 ‖

Rik 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.15) printed on p. 372

original p. 372

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.15)

उरुष्या णो अभिशस्तेः सोम नि पाह्यंहसः । सखा सुशेव एधि नः ॥ १५ ॥

uruṣyā ṇo abhiśasteḥ soma ni pāhy aṃhasaḥ | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ ‖ 15 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.15)

उरुष्य । नः । अभिऽशस्तेः । सोम । नि । पाहि । अंहसः । सखा । सुऽशेवः । एधि । नः ॥ १५ ॥

uruṣya | naḥ | abhi-śasteḥ | soma | ni | pāhi | aṃhasaḥ | sakhā | su-śevaḥ | edhi | naḥ ‖ 15 ‖

(The Saṃhitā prints uruṣyā, the Pada uruṣya. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.15)

हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्मानभिशस्तेरभिशंसनादभिशापरूपान्निन्दनादुरुष्य । रक्ष । उरुष्यतीं रक्षाकर्मेति यास्कः । नि. ५-२३ [?] । तथांहसोऽस्मत्कृतात्पापाच्च नि पाहि । नितरां पालय । एवमस्मदीयं पापं परिहृत्य सुशेवोऽस्मभ्यं दातव्येन शोभनेन सुखेन युक्तः सन्नेधि । हितकारी भव ॥ अभिशस्तेः । शंसु स्तुतौ । अस्माद्भावे क्तिन् । तादौ चेति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । एधि । अस भुवि । लोटि सेर्हिः । तस्य जित्त्वात् श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । घ्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्चेति सकारस्यैत्वं । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वात् हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिरिति हेर्धिरादेशः ॥

he soma tvaṃ no 'smān abhiśaster abhiśaṃsanād abhiśāparūpān nindanād uruṣya | rakṣa | uruṣyatī rakṣākarmeti yāskaḥ | Ni. 5-23 [?] | tathāṃhaso 'smatkṛtāt pāpāc ca ni pāhi | nitarāṃ pālaya | evam asmadīyaṃ pāpaṃ parihṛtya suśevo 'smabhyaṃ dātavyena śobhanena sukhena yuktaḥ sann edhi | hitakārī bhava ‖ abhiśasteḥ | śaṃsu stutau | asmād bhāve ktin | tādau ceti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | edhi | asa bhuvi | loṭi ser hiḥ | tasya jittvāt śnasor allopa ity akāralopaḥ | ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ceti sakārasyaitvaṃ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhād ity asiddhatvāt hujhalbhyo her dhir iti her dhir ādeśaḥ ‖

Translation: "O Soma, protect us from abhiśasti — from reproach, from censure in the form of curses: uruṣya, guard. 'The root uruṣya is a verb of protecting', says Yāska (Ni. 5-23 [?]). And from aṃhas, the sin committed by us, ni pāhi — guard us thoroughly. Having thus removed our sin, be, suśevaḥ, endowed with the excellent happiness that is to be given to us; edhi, be a well-wisher."

Grammar tail: abhiśasteḥ — root śaṃsu stutau; the suffix ktin in the abstract sense; tādau ca — the preverb keeps its natural accent. edhi — root asa bhuvi; the hi replaces sip in the loṭ; since it is a jit [as read], by śnasor allopaḥ the a is elided; by ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca the s becomes e; by asiddhavad atrābhāt that [elision] counts as not having occurred, and by hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ the replacement dhi for hi.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.15)

Soma — O Soma-deity; naḥ — us; abhiśasteḥ — from the blemish in the form of calumny; uruṣya — protect; aṃhasaḥ — from sin (that we may commit or have committed); ni pāhi — protect completely; suśevaḥ — together with the happiness offered by us; naḥ — to us; sakhā edhi — be, like a friend, a bringer of happiness.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.15

"O Soma-deity, protect us from blemish in the form of calumny. Protect us completely from sin that we have committed or may commit. Come together with the means of happiness offered by us, and be a bringer of happiness to us, like a friend."

original p. 373

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.15

"Soma, protect us from calumny, preserve us from Sin ; pleased with our service, be our friend." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.15)

abhiśasteḥ — "The word abhiśasti has many meanings, such as curse, calamity (āpatti), reproach. Here the bhāṣya-writer says 'abhiśāparūpān nindanāt' — 'from calumny, in the form of a curse', that is, from blame."

uruṣya — uruṣyatī rakṣākarmā (Ni. 5-23 [?]) | "uruṣya means 'protect'. In many Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-3 [?]; 8-[?]-[?] [?] this word occurs in the sense of 'protect'."

aṃhasaḥ — aṃhatiś cāṃhaś cāṃhuś ca hanteḥ [as read; the print's first word is doubtful [?]] (Ni. 4-23 [?]) | "Though the word aṃhas is formed from the root han, which gives the sense of killing, the sense of sin is more common for this word than the general sense of violence. Here it means 'from sin'."

suśevaḥ — "Being the giver of the most excellent happiness: this is the meaning."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.15)

uruṣyā — uruṣya is a root with the sense of protecting; loṭ, second person singular; by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (अन्येषामपि दृश्यते, Pā. 6-3-137 [?]) the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. abhiśasteḥ — root śaṃsu stutau; in the abstract sense, by striyāṃ ktin (स्त्रियां क्तिन्, Pā. 3-3-94 [?]) the suffix ktin; by anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति, Pā. 6-4-24 [?]) the nasal of the penultimate is elided: śasti; since it follows abhi, by tādau ca niti (Pā. 6-2-50 [?]) the preverb, as the suffix beginning with t and being nit, keeps its natural accent; the ablative singular. pāhi — root pā rakṣaṇe, of the adādi class; loṭ, second person singular; as a finite verb it has the nighāta. edhi — root as bhuvi, of the adādi class; loṭ, second person singular, sip; by ser hy apicca (Pā. 3-4-87 [?]) hi; since it is [taken as] jit, then by śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-111 [?]) the a of as is elided; by ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca (घ्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्च, Pā. 6-4-119 [?]) e for the s before hi (ddhi); by asiddhavad atrābhāt the e-change is treated as not having occurred, so that —

original p. 374

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.15, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly): [edhi, continued —] "…so that the s comes as if it had not been lost; and, by hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ (हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः, Pā. 6-4-101 [?]), because it follows a jhal-ending stem, hi becomes dhi; the form is edhi. As a finite verb following a word, the nighāta accent." ‖ 15 ‖

Rik 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.16)

आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते विश्वतः सोम वृष्ण्यम् । भवा वाजस्य संगथे ॥ १६ ॥

ā pyāyasva sam etu te viśvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam | bhavā vājasya saṃgathe ‖ 16 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.16)

आ । प्यायस्व । सम् । एतु । ते । विश्वतः । सोम । वृष्ण्यम् । भव । वाजस्य । सम्ऽगथे ॥ १६ ॥

ā | pyāyasva | sam | etu | te | viśvataḥ | soma | vṛṣṇyam | bhava | vājasya | saṃ-gathe ‖ 16 ‖

(The Saṃhitā prints bhavā, the Pada bhava. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.16)

ग्रावस्तोत्रे आ प्यायस्व समेतु त इति तृचो विनियुक्तः । सूत्रितं च । आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते इति तिस्रो मृजन्ति त्वा दश क्षिपः । आ. ५-१२ [?] इति ॥ पत्नीसंयाजेषु सौम्यस्याप्यायस्वेत्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजाः । आ. १-१० [?] इति ॥ चमसाप्यायनेऽप्येषा विनियुक्ता । सूत्रितं च । आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजा इति चमसानाद्योपाद्यान् । आ. ५-६ [?] इति ॥ हे सोम त्वमा प्यायस्व । वर्धयस्व । ते तव वृष्ण्यं वृषत्वं वीर्यं सामर्थ्यं विश्वतः सर्वतः समेतु । संगच्छताम् । त्वया संयुक्तं भवतु । एवंभूतस्त्वं वाजस्यान्नस्य संगथे संगमने भव । अस्माकमन्नप्रदो भवेत्यर्थः ॥ वृष्ण्यं । वृष सेचने । कनिन्युवृषीत्यादिना कनिन् । वृष्णि भवं वृष्ण्यम् । भवे छन्दसि । यत् । अल्लोपोऽनः इत्यकारलोपः । येचाभावकर्मणोरिति प्रकृतिभावस्तु व्यत्ययेन न प्रवर्तते । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । भव । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । संगथे । पात्कृतुदिवचीत्यादिना [?] विधीयमानस्थक्प्रत्ययो बहुलवचनाद्गमेरपि भवति । थाथादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं ॥

grāvastotre ā pyāyasva sametu ta iti tṛco viniyuktaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | ā pyāyasva sametu te iti tisro mṛjanti tvā daśa kṣipaḥ | Ā. 5-12 [?] iti ‖ patnīsaṃyājeṣu saumyasyāpyāyasvety eṣānuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājāḥ | Ā. 1-10 [?] iti ‖ camasāpyāyane 'py eṣā viniyuktā | sūtritaṃ ca | ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasānādyopādyān | Ā. 5-6 [?] iti ‖ he soma tvam ā pyāyasva | vardhayasva | te tava vṛṣṇyaṃ vṛṣatvaṃ vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ viśvataḥ sarvataḥ sametu | saṃgacchatām | tvayā saṃyuktaṃ bhavatu | evaṃbhūtas tvaṃ vājasyānnasya saṃgathe saṃgamane bhava | asmākam annaprado bhavety arthaḥ ‖ vṛṣṇyaṃ | vṛṣa secane | kanin yuvṛṣītakṣīty ādinā kanin | vṛṣṇi bhavaṃ vṛṣṇyam | bhave chandasi | yat | allopo 'naḥ ity akāralopaḥ | ye cābhāvakarmaṇor iti prakṛtibhāvas tu vyatyayena na pravartate | yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | bhava | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | saṃgathe | pātkṛtudivacītyādinā [?] vidhīyamānathakpratyayo bahulavacanād gamer api bhavati | thāthādinottarapadāntodāttatvaṃ ‖

Translation: "In the grāvastotra (the praising of the pressing-stones), the three Ṛks ā pyāyasva sametu te are applied; prescribed: 'ā pyāyasva sametu te iti tisro mṛjanti tvā daśa kṣipaḥ' (Ā. 5-12 [?]). In the patnīsaṃyājas, for the Saumya, āpyāyasva is the anuvākyā; prescribed: 'ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājāḥ' (Ā. 1-10 [?]). It is also applied at the camasāpyāyana (the swelling of the cups); prescribed: 'ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasān ādyopādyān' (Ā. 5-6 [?]). — O Soma, ā pyāyasva: swell, increase. Let your vṛṣṇya, your virility, your valour and capacity, from every side (viśvataḥ) sametu, come together; let it be joined with you. Being thus, in the saṃgathe, in the coming-together, of vāja, food, be: this is the meaning — be the giver of food to us."

Grammar tail: vṛṣṇyam — root vṛṣa secane; the suffix kanin by kanin yuvṛṣitakṣi…; "vṛṣṇi bhavam" — vṛṣṇya; by bhave chandasi the suffix yat; by allopo 'naḥ the elision of the a; the prakṛtibhāva by ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ does not apply, by vyatyaya; by yato 'nāvaḥ the initial-acute. bhava — by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. saṃgathe — the suffix thak prescribed in the Uṇādi (pātkṛtudivaci… as read [?]) comes after gam also, by "bahulam"; by thāthādi… the final-member final-acute.

original p. 375

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.16)

Soma — O Soma-deity; ā pyāyasva — obtain full growth; te — your; vṛṣṇyam — valour; viśvataḥ — from all sides; sametu — come and fill [you]; vājasya — of the food (which is to be divided for us); saṃgathe — in the gathering; bhava — be eager.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.16

"O Soma-deity, obtain full growth. May your valour come and fill you from all sides. Be eager in the gathering of the food that is to be divided for us."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.16

"Increase Soma ; may vigour come to you from every side ; be deligent [sic] in the supply of food to us." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.16)

"The three Ṛks beginning ā pyāyasva sametu te are used at the grāvastotra, that is, when the pressing stones that crush the Soma-creeper are praised; so says the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra 'ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā' (Ā. 1-10 [?]). Also, at the filling of the camasa vessel with Soma-juice, there is application for this Ṛk; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra makes it clear in the sūtra 'ā pyāyasva sametu te saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasānādyopādyān'."

vṛṣṇyam — "Strength that is to be shown, or valour."

vājasya — "The word vāja is read in the Nirukta among the names of food and among the names of battle. The distinctive feature of this word has been told earlier. Here vājasya means 'of food'."

saṃgathe — "This word is read in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-[?] [?]) among the names of battle. The meaning 'coming together', i.e. 'joining', beyond that 'battle', is one view. But here saṃgathe means 'in the gathering', or 'in the bringing and joining together for us'."

original p. 376

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.16)

pyāyasva — root ohpyāyī vṛddhau of the bhvādi class; ātmanepada; loṭ, second person singular, thās; by thāsaḥ se (थासः से, Pā. 3-4-80 [?]) se for thās; by savābhyāṃ vāmau (सवाभ्यां वामौ, Pā. 3-4-91 [?]) va for the e; śap; the nighāta accent. etu — root iṅ gatau; loṭ, third person singular; the tiṅ-nighāta. vṛṣṇyam — root vṛṣa secane; by kanin yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyutyupatāpibhyaḥ (the Uṇādi sūtra as printed, U. 1-154 [?]) the suffix kanin: vṛṣan; vṛṣṇi bhavaṃ vṛṣṇyam; by bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110 [?]) the suffix yat; since the suffix begins with y, the stem has the name bha, and by allopo 'naḥ (अल्लोपोऽनः) the a of an in vṛṣan is elided; in fact here the prakṛtibhāva by ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 6-4-168 [?]) ought to occur, but by vyatyayo bahulam it does not occur here; by yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 [?]), the suffix being yat, the initial-acute accent comes. bhava — root bhū sattāyām; loṭ, second person singular; since it has two vowels, by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ (द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः, Pā. 6-3-135 [?]) the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. saṃgathe — root gam gatau; the suffix thak prescribed in the Uṇādi by pātṛtudivaci… (पात्कृतुदिवचि…, U. 3-164 [?], as printed) — by bahulam it comes after the root gam as well; because it is kit, by anudāttopadeśa… (Pā. 6-4-37 [?]) the nasal m of the root is elided; by thāthaghañ… (थाथघञ्…, Pā. 6-2-144 [?]) in the compound with sam the final syllable of the final member is acute; the locative singular. ‖ 16 ‖

Rik 17

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 91.17) Uṣṇih

आ प्यायस्व मदिन्तम सोम विश्वेभिरंशुभिः । भवा नः सुश्रवस्तमः सखा वृधे ॥ १७ ॥

ā pyāyasva madintama soma viśvebhir aṃśubhiḥ | bhavā naḥ suśravastamaḥ sakhā vṛdhe ‖ 17 ‖

original p. 377

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 91.17)

आ । प्यायस्व । मदिन्ऽतम । सोम । विश्वेभिः । अंशुऽभिः । भव । नः । सुश्रवःऽतमः । सखा । वृधे ॥ १७ ॥

ā | pyāyasva | madin-tama | soma | viśvebhiḥ | aṃśu-bhiḥ | bhava | naḥ | suśravaḥ-tamaḥ | sakhā | vṛdhe ‖ 17 ‖

(The Pada prints madin-tama with the vocative ending as in the Saṃhitā and suśravaḥ-tamaḥ for the Saṃhitā's suśravastamaḥ; the Saṃhitā prints bhavā, the Pada bhava. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 91.17)

हे मदिन्तम अतिशयेन मदवन् सोम विश्वेभिः सर्वैरंशुभिर्लतावयवैः समन्तादा प्यायस्व । आ समन्ताद्वृद्धो भव । स त्वं सुश्रवस्तमोऽतिशयेन शोभनान्नैर्युक्तः सन् नोऽस्माकं वृधे वर्धनाय सखा भव । मित्रोभव ॥ मदिन्तम । मदो हर्षः । तद्वान् मदी । अतिशयेन मदी मदिन्तमः । नाद्घस्य । पा. ८-२-१७ [?] इति तमपो नुट् । सुश्रवस्तमः । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । श्रूयत इति श्रवः । नि. १०-३ [?] इति यास्कः । शोभनं श्रवो यस्य स तथोक्तः । अतिशयेन सुश्रवाः सुश्रवस्तमः । तमपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वमेव शिष्यते ॥

he madintama atiśayena madavan soma viśvebhiḥ sarvair aṃśubhir latāvayavaiḥ samantād ā pyāyasva | ā samantād vṛddho bhava | sa tvaṃ suśravastamo 'tiśayena śobhanānnair yuktaḥ san no 'smākaṃ vṛdhe vardhanāya sakhā bhava | mitrobhava ‖ madintama | mado harṣaḥ | tadvān madī | atiśayena madī madintamaḥ | nādghasya | Pā. 8-2-17 [?] iti tamapo nuṭ | suśravastamaḥ | srava ity annanāma | śrūyata iti śravaḥ | Ni. 10-3 [?] iti yāskaḥ | śobhanaṃ śravo yasya sa tathoktaḥ | atiśayena suśravāḥ suśravastamaḥ | tamapaḥ pittvād anudāttatve sor manasī alomoṣasī ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam eva śiṣyate ‖

Translation: "O Soma, exceedingly joyful (madintama) one: with all your aṃśubhiḥ, the parts of the creeper, grow full on every side. Such as you are — endowed in the highest degree (suśravastamaḥ) with excellent food — be a friend for the growth (vṛdhe) of us. Madintama — mada is joy; he who has it is madī; he who is exceedingly madī is madintama; by nādghasya (Pā. 8-2-17 [?]) the augment nuṭ for the suffix tamap. Suśravastamaḥ — śravaḥ is a name for food: 'that which is heard (śrūyate) is śravaḥ', says Yāska (Ni. 10-3 [?]); he whose śravaḥ is excellent is suśravāḥ; in the superlative, suśravastamaḥ. Since tamap is pit and unaccented, the initial-acute of the final member given by sor manasī alomoṣasī alone remains."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.17)

madintama — O exceedingly joyful one; Soma — O Soma-deity; viśvebhiḥ — all; aṃśubhiḥ — with the tendrils (of the creeper); ā pyāyasva — obtain growth on all sides; suśravastamaḥ — being united exceedingly with excellent food; naḥ — our; vṛdhe — [being the cause] of growth; sakhā bhava — be a friend.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.17

"O Soma-deity, you are always filled with exceeding joy. Obtain growth on all sides, with all the tendrils of the creeper that are around you. Being united, in the highest degree, with excellent food, be our friend, the cause of our growth."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.17; the last line of the print is smudged

"Exulting Soma, increase with all twining plants ; be a frie[nd — smudged] well supplied with food we may prosper." — as printed (the words after "a frie" are blotted in the scan; the closing clause is read "…well supplied with food we may prosper").

original p. 378

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.17)

madintama — "Sāyaṇa explains it as 'one who has exceeding gladness, very joyful'; Skandasvāmin as 'one who creates exceeding intoxication [or joy] in others'. As said in the Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā 9-80-3 [?]"

मक्षि शर्धो मारुतं मक्षि देवान्मक्षि महामिन्द्रमिन्दो मदाय ।

makṣi śardho mārutaṃ makṣi devān makṣi mahām indram indo madāya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-80-3 [?]; the same Ṛk as cited on p. 359)

"— because Soma causes intoxication [joy] in all the deities, the meaning 'cause of delight' is the right one."

aṃśubhiḥ — "aṃśu means 'ray'. But here the parts of the Soma-creeper, bright and fine, spreading in all directions like rays, are called aṃśu."

suśravastamaḥ — "The word śravas is read in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-9 [?]) among the names of strength, of wealth and of food. Here the meaning given is 'food': one possessed of the most excellent food. Skandasvāmin explains 'sudhanatamaḥ sukīrtitamo vā' ['one with the best wealth, or of the best fame']."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.17)

madintama — mada + ini: madī; by ata ini-ṭhanau (अत इनिठनौ, Pā. 5-2-115 [?]) the suffix ini; in the sense of excess, by atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, Pā. 5-3-55 [?]) tamap; by nādghasya (Pā. 8-2-17 [?]) nuṭ is the augment of the tarap/tamap suffixes standing after a stem ending in n, here in Chandas; the n becomes anusvāra by parasavarṇa; as madintama is a vocative, by āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]) the nighāta accent comes. viśvebhiḥ — the word viśva; bhis following; by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 7-1-10 [?]) ais does not occur; by bahuvacane jhaly et (Pā. 7-3-103 [?]) the e; the s becomes ru, visarga. bhava — since it stands at the head of the pāda, no nighāta; since śap is unaccented, the root's accent remains. suśravastamaḥ — "śravaḥ iti annanāma śrūyate iti śravaḥ" (Nirukta 10-3 [?], Yāska): the knowers say śravaḥ is a name of food. śobhanaṃ śravo yasya sa suśravāḥ; the atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau suffix tamap — continued on p. 379

original p. 379

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.17, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly): [suśravastamaḥ, continued —] "since tamap is pit, it is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau (अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ, Pā. 3-1-4 [?]). Then, by sor manasī alomoṣasī the final-member initial-acute: as śravas ends in as, the initial-acute accent already obtained for the final member remains." ‖ 17 ‖

पत्नीसंयाजेषु सौम्यस्य सं ते पयांसीति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजा इह त्वष्टारमग्रियम् । आ. १-१० [?] इति ॥ चमसाप्याय-

patnīsaṃyājeṣu saumyasya saṃ te payāṃsīti yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam | Ā. 1-10 [?] iti ‖ camasāpyāya-

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 91.18, continued from p. 379:

-नेऽप्येषा । सूत्रितं च । सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजा इति चमसानाद्योपाद्यान् । आ. ५-६ [?] इति ॥ हे सोम अभिमातिषाहोऽभिमातीनां शत्रूणां हन्तुस्ते तव एवंभूतं त्वां पयांसि श्रयणार्थानि क्षीराणि सं यन्तु । संगच्छन्ताम् । तथा वाजा उ हविर्लक्षणान्यन्नानि च त्वां संगच्छन्ताम् । वृष्ण्यानि वीर्याणि च संगच्छन्ताम् । हे सोम । त्वमप्यमृतायास्माकममृतत्वायामरत्वायाप्यायमान आ समन्ताद्वर्धमानः सन् दिवि नभसि स्वर्गे उत्तमान्युद्गततमानि उत्कृष्टानि श्रवांस्यन्नान्यस्माभिर्भोक्तव्यानि हविर्लक्षणानि वा धिष्व । धारय ॥ ते । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी । अभिमातिषाहः । षह अभिभवने । छन्दसि सह इति ण्विप्रत्ययः । सुषामादित्वात् षत्वम् । अमृताय । नञो जरमरमित्रमृता इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । उत्तमानि । उच्चैःशब्दसाधनक्रियावचनादतिशायनिकस्तमप् । उत्तमशश्वत्तमौ सर्वत्र । पा. ६-१-१६० [?] इत्युञ्छादिषु पाठादन्तोदात्तत्वं । धिष्व । सुधित वसुधित नेमधित धिष्व धिषीय च । पा. ७-४-४५ [?] इति धिभावो निपात्यते ॥

-ne 'py eṣā | sūtritaṃ ca | saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasān ādyopādyān | Ā. 5-6 [?] iti ‖ he soma abhimātiṣāho 'bhimātīnāṃ śatrūṇāṃ hantus te tava evaṃbhūtaṃ tvāṃ payāṃsi śrayaṇārthāni kṣīrāṇi saṃ yantu | saṃgacchantām | tathā vājā u havirlakṣaṇāny annāni ca tvāṃ saṃgacchantām | vṛṣṇyāni vīryāṇi ca saṃgacchantām | he soma | tvam apy amṛtāyāsmākam amṛtatvāyāmaratvāyāpyāyamāna ā samantād vardhamānaḥ san divi nabhasi svarge uttamāny udgatatamāni utkṛṣṭāni śravāṃsy annāny asmābhir bhoktavyāni havirlakṣaṇāni vā dhiṣva | dhāraya ‖ te | kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam iti karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāc caturthyarthe ṣaṣṭhī | abhimātiṣāhaḥ | ṣaha abhibhavane | chandasi saha iti ṇvipratyayaḥ | suṣāmāditvāt ṣatvam | amṛtāya | nañ jaramaramitramṛtā ity uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | uttamāni | uccaiḥśabdasādhanakriyāvacanād atiśāyanikas tamap | uttamaśaśvattamau sarvatra | Pā. 6-1-160 [?] ity uñchādiṣu pāṭhād antodāttatvaṃ | dhiṣva | sudhita vasudhita nemadhita dhiṣva dhiṣīya ca | Pā. 7-4-45 [?] iti dhibhāvo nipātyate ‖

Translation: "…this Ṛk is also applied at the [swelling] of the camasa cups; it is prescribed: 'saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasān ādyopādyān' (Ā. 5-6 [?]). — O Soma, abhimātiṣāhaḥ, the slayer of the abhimātis, the enemies: let the payāṃsi, the milks that serve to feed, saṃ yantu, come together to you who are such. And let vājāḥ, the foods in the form of oblations, come together to you. And let vṛṣṇyāni, the potencies, come together. O Soma, being āpyāyamānaḥ, growing on every side, for our immortality, for our undying, dhiṣva — hold, in heaven (divi, in the sky, in svarga), the uttamāni śravāṃsi, the highest, the choicest foods that are to be enjoyed by us, or the foods in the form of oblations."

Grammar tail: te — "the mention of the action should be made [by vārttika]"; since the object is a recipient (saṃpradāna), the genitive stands in the sense of the dative. abhimātiṣāhaḥ — root ṣaha abhibhavane; in Chandas the suffix ṇvi (by chandasi sahaḥ); ṣatva because it belongs to the suṣāmādi group. amṛtāya — by nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ the final member's initial-acute. uttamāni — tamap in the superlative sense, after the word ut, expressing the means of 'highest' action; by uttamaśaśvattamau sarvatra (Pā. 6-1-160 [?]) the final-acute, since it is listed in the uñchādi group. dhiṣva — by sudhita vasudhita nemadhita dhiṣva dhiṣīya ca (Pā. 7-4-45 [?]) the dhi formation is irregular.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 91.18)

abhimātiṣāhaḥ — O Soma-deity, destroyer of enemies; te — to you (towards you); payāṃsi — (protective) milks; saṃ yantu — flow all around and come together; vājāḥ u saṃ — may the foods in the form of oblations also come together to you; vṛṣṇyāni saṃ — may potencies also fill you; Soma — O Soma-deity; amṛtāya — so that there may be no death for (us); āpyāyamānaḥ — growing all around; divi — in heaven; uttamāni — excellent; śravāṃsi — foods; dhiṣva — obtain.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 91.18

"O Soma-deity, may protective streams of milk flow all around to you who destroy your enemies. May the foods in the form of oblations and the potencies also come and fill you. So that we may be free from death, growing all around, obtain for us excellent foods in heaven."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 91.18

"May the milky [printed "milky uices", the j of "juices" lost] flow around you ; may sacrificial offerings and vigour be concentrated in the destroyer of foes ; and, being fully nourished, Soma, provide excellent foods in heaven for our immortality." — as printed (the first line is rendered "may the milky uices flow around you"; the missing j is a misprint [sic]).

original p. 381

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 91.18)

"When the offering to the Soma deity is made in the homas called patnīsaṃyāja, this Ṛk, saṃ te payāṃsi, is to be used as the yājyā mantra; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains it by the sūtra 'saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam' (Ā. 1-10 [?]). The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows the application of this Ṛk in the camasāpyāyana as well, by the sūtra 'saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā iti camasān ādyopādyān' (Ā. 5-6 [?])."

abhimātiṣāhaḥ — abhitaḥ hiṃsantīty abhimātayaḥ | teṣām abhibhavitā | "Those who harm on every side are abhimātis, enemies; their conqueror: the destroyer of enemies who injure from every side — this is the meaning."

पाप्मा वा अभिमातिः ।

pāpmā vā abhimātiḥ | (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-3-5 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Sin indeed is the enemy [abhimāti]."

"— by such śruti-sentences the sinner, too, is abhimāti. The enemy too, who does not perform sacrifice and the like, is a sinner."

payāṃsi — "Protective milks, or waters in the form of rain."

amṛtāya — "So that there may be no death. Or the word amṛta is the name of the deities: 'devatārtham' (Ska. Bhā.) — 'for the sake of the deities' — is the meaning he gives."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 91.18)

te — in the sūtra that lays down the name saṃpradāna, from the statement "kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam" (the mention of the action must be made) the name saṃpradāna arises here, and so the genitive stands in the sense of the dative; by te mayāvekavacanasya (ते मयावेकवचनस्य, Pā. 8-1-22 [?]) te is the replacement for the singular of yuṣmad. yantu — root iṇ gatau; loṭ, third person plural; anta for jhi; utva; by iko yaṇ the yaṇ replacement; the tiṅ-nighāta. vṛṣṇyāni — explained in the sixteenth Ṛk of this very sūkta. abhimātiṣāhaḥ — root saha abhibhave; by chandasi sahaḥ (Pā. 3-2-63 [?]) the suffix ṇvi; in ṇvi, the whole of the suffix is elided (sarvalopa); since it is ṇit, by ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 [?]) the penultimate a of the root is lengthened [vṛddhi]: sāh; abhimātīnāṃ sāṭ — abhimātiṣāṭ; since it is read in the suṣāmādi list, the s takes ṣatva; the plural [form] … the last line of the page is blotted in the scan; the print continues on p. 382

original p. 382

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 91.18, continued (grammar page, noted briefly):

āpyāyamānaḥ — root ohpyāyī vṛddhau; in the present sense śānac; śap; by āne muk (आने मुक्, Pā. 7-2-82 [?]) the augment muk for the stem ending in a before āna; as the replacement ends the word, the lasārvadhātuka suffix follows, and by tāsyanudāttet (तास्यनुदात्तेत्, Pā. 6-1-186 [?]) it is unaccented; śap, being pit, is unaccented; then the accent of the root remains. amṛtāya — root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; the suffix kta; na mṛtam amṛtam; by nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ (नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः, Pā. 6-2-116 [?]) the final member's initial-acute. divi — by ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171) the locative singular takes the acute. uttamāni — ut is a word expressing the means of an action; after it, in the superlative sense, the suffix tamap; with tamap unaccented, the accent would be unobtained, but by uttamaśaśvattamau sarvatra (Pā. 6-1-160 [?]), since it is listed in the uñchādi group, the final syllable takes the acute; the accusative plural. dhiṣva — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; loṭ, second person singular; by sudhita vasudhita nemadhita dhiṣva dhiṣīya ca (Pā. 7-4-45 [?]) the dhi formation is irregular; since it follows a word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 18 ‖
