Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 92.4, concluded:

षाः शास्त्रोक्तमन्धकारं [clotted [?]] व्यावः । विवृतमपश्लिष्टमकरोत् ॥ नृतूरिव । तुर्वी हिंसार्थः । क्विप् इति क्विप् । रात्सस्य इति वलोपः । वोरुपधाया इति दीर्घत्वं । यद्वा । नृत्यतीति गात्रविनामे । नृतिशृधोः कूः । उ. १-९४ [?] इति कूप्रत्ययः । बर्जहं । वृज् संभक्तौ । वृणीते संभजते गामिति बः पयः । विच् । तज्जहातीति बर्जहः । ओहाङ् त्यागे । खत्करणे वातशुनीतिलगर्धेष्वजहेट्तुदजहातिभ्य उपसंख्यानं । पा. ३-२-५८ [?] इत्यर्घशब्दोपपदादपि कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनात् खश् । तस्य सार्वधातुकत्वेन कर्तरि शपि जुहोत्यादित्वात् श्लुः । द्विर्वचनादि । बवयोरभेद इति बत्वं । दिवोदासादित्वात्पूर्वपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । आवः । वृञ् वरणे । लुङः मन्त्रे घसेति च्लेर्लुक् । गुणे हल्ङ्यादि इति लोपः । छन्दस्यपि दृश्यते । पा. ६-४-७३ [?] इत्यडागमः ॥

-ṣāḥ śāstroktam andhakāraṃ [clotted [?]] vy āvaḥ | vivṛtam apaśliṣṭam akarot ‖ nṛtūr iva | turvī hiṃsārthaḥ | kvip iti kvip | rātsasya iti valopaḥ | vor upadhāyā iti dīrghatvaṃ | yadvā | nṛtyatīti gātravināme | nṛtiśṛdhoḥ kūḥ | U. 1-94 [?] iti kūpratyayaḥ | barjahaṃ | vṛj saṃbhaktau | vṛṇīte saṃbhajate gām iti baḥ payaḥ | vic | taj jahātīti barjahaḥ | ohāṅ tyāge | khatkaraṇe vātaśunītilagardheṣv ajaheṭtudajahātibhya upasaṃkhyānaṃ | Pā. 3-2-58 [?] ity arghaśabdopapadād api kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti bahulavacanāt khaś | tasya sārvadhātukatvena kartari śapi juhotyāditvāt śluḥ | dvirvacanādi | bavayor abheda iti batvaṃ | divodāsāditvāt pūrvapadādyudāttatvaṃ | āvaḥ | vṛñ varaṇe | luṅaḥ mantre ghaseti cler luk | guṇe halṅyādi iti lopaḥ | chandasy api dṛśyate | Pā. 6-4-73 [?] ity aḍāgamaḥ ‖

Translation: "…the Uṣas, vy āvaḥ, opened out the darkness [the clause between 'uṣāḥ' and 'andhakāram' is clotted in the print [?]]: she made it uncovered, unattached. — Here nṛtūr iva — "like a nṛtū, a barber": he who with the hair makes men bare. As he cuts the hair completely, so the Uṣas too destroys the darkness down to the root. Or: nṛtor iva — like a dancing woman; peśāṃsi — a name for 'forms': the Uṣas adhi vapate, 'puts on', forms that all can see; she holds them in excess on her own self. So, first dispelling the darkness with her own rays, she apornute vakṣaḥ, uncovers her own breast, the region of the chest: she makes it uncovered by darkness; she herself becomes manifest. Barjaham — the 'udder', the place where milk is produced: as the cow usrā shows it at milking-time. What is she doing? Gāvo na vrajam — as cattle by themselves quickly occupy their pen, so by herself she, having reached the eastern quarter, makes jyotiḥ, light, for viśvasmai bhuvanāya, for the whole world."

Grammar tail (partly clotted; characterized): nṛtūḥ — tūrvī has the sense of harming; the suffix kvip; the elision of v, etc. Or from nṛtī ('to dance') — the suffix kū (U. 1-94 [?]). barjaham — root vṛj saṃbhaktau; ba, 'milk': vṛṇīte saṃbhajate gām iti baḥ payaḥ; the suffix vic; "that which gives it up (jahāti) is barjahaḥ", root ohāṅ tyāge; the suffix khaś by the upasaṃkhyāna with arghaśabda in the upapada (Pā. 3-2-58 [?]) and by kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam; śap elided (ślu) because the root is of the juhotyādi class; doubling etc.; b for v by bavayor abhedaḥ; since it belongs to the divodāsādi group, the first member's initial acute. āvaḥ — root vṛñ varaṇe; luṅ; the luk of cli by mantre ghasa…; the elision by guṇe halṅyādi…; the augment aṭ, seen in Chandas also (Pā. 6-4-73 [?])."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 92.4)

uṣāḥ — the deity Uṣas; nṛtoḥ iva — as a barber cuts the hair completely; peśāṃsi — (the ones clinging to the world) the darkness [as read]; vapate — cuts off (destroys). [nṛtoḥ iva — like a graceful dancing woman; peśāṃsi — (attractive) her beautiful forms; adhi vapate — (in herself) fully displays.] usrā — a cow; barjaham — (at the time of milking) the udder, showing [it]; vakṣaḥ — her breast; apornute — uncovers (shows, freeing it from the darkness); gāvaḥ — cattle; vrajaṃ na — as they go to the cow-pen (so Uṣas too, going to the eastern quarter); viśvasmai bhuvanāya — for the whole world; jyotiḥ — light; kṛṇvatī — making; tamaḥ — darkness; vi āvaḥ — destroyed completely.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 92.4

"As a barber cuts the hair, the Uṣas deity drives away the darkness. Like a dancing woman, the Uṣas deity fully displays her attractive forms. As a cow shows her udder at milking time, she shows her breast. As cows go to the cow-pen, Uṣas, going to the eastern quarter and making light for the whole world, destroys the darkness completely."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 92.4; the passage continues on p. 416

"Ushas cuts off the accumulated glooms as a barber cuts off the hair ; she bares her bosom as a cow yeilds [sic] her udder to the milker ; and as cattle —" continued on p. 416

original p. 416

English Translation of Rik 92.4, concluded printed in English in the source

"— hasten to their pastures, she speeds to the east, and, shedding light npon [sic] all the world dissipates the darkness." — as printed (so the whole reads: "Ushas cuts off the accumulated glooms as a barber cuts off the hair ; she bares her bosom as a cow yeilds her udder to the milker ; and as cattle hasten to their pastures, she speeds to the east, and, shedding light npon all the world dissipates the darkness.").

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 92.4)

nṛtoḥ iva — "In this simile two kinds of meaning arise: the removal of a blemish, and the display of beauty. The first: nṛtūḥ means nṝn tūrvati keśena riktīkarotīti nṛtūr nāpitaḥ [as read, doubtful [?]]: because he cuts all the hair of men completely, the barber is called nṛtū, nāpita."

vapate — chinatti | "She cuts off. As a barber cuts the hair of the head, so the Uṣas too peśāṃsi — the dark glooms that cover the world — adhi vapate, destroys completely. In this sense it is that she displays beauty through the removal of blemish."

"The second: nṛtoḥ iva — nṛtyantī yoṣid iva: as a beautiful woman who dances makes ready her peśāṃsi, her charming forms and graces, so the Uṣas too adhi vapate — acquires her charming beauty, spreading her radiance all around — this is the meaning."

usrā — "Since āhnayaḥ, usrā and the like are read among the names of the cow (Ni. 2-9 [?]), usrā means 'cow'. usrā viśo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ [as read, clotted [?]]: because they hold flowing milk that is a means of comfort, the cow has the name usriyā."

barjaham — prāṇināṃ bharaṇasamarthatvāt bas iti kṣīram ucyate | taj jahātīti barjaham ūdhaḥ | "Milk, which is able to nourish living beings, is called bas. The place that gives this milk is called barjaham: the udder."

"Here the simile has great propriety. As the cow shows her udder in order to give milk generously, so the Uṣas too shows her breast: that is, she spreads her radiance, generously, to the world, and creates light and awareness."

vrajam — vṛṇoter vrajaḥ (Ni. 6-[?] [?]) | "Because it is enclosed [by a fence], it is called vraja. vrajaṃ na — as a cow goes to the pen that is the place of her protection, out of her own pleasure, with no other compulsion, so the Uṣas too goes to her own place —

original p. 417

"— the eastern quarter — out of her own satisfaction, and spreads light over all the worlds. The Ṛk below conveys this same point:"

उदपप्तन्नरुणा भानवो वृथा स्वायुजो अरुषीर्गा अयुक्षत ।

udapaptann aruṇā bhānavo vṛthā svāyujo aruṣīr gā ayukṣata | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-2 [?]; this is the second Ṛk of the present sūkta, as translated on p. 407)

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 92.4)

vapate — root ḍuvap bījasantāne; this is also used in the sense of cutting (bhedana); laṭ, third person singular; the nighāta accent. nṛtūriva — root turvī hiṃsārthaḥ; by kvip ca the suffix kvip; by rālopa (रात्लोपः, Pā. 6-4-21 [?]) the v standing after r is elided; su following; by vor upadhāyā dīrghaḥ (Pā. 8-2-76 [?]) the penultimate vowel of the root ending in r is lengthened: tūḥ. Or from nṛtī gātravināme ('to dance, to move the limbs'); by nṛtiśṛdhyoḥ kūḥ (U. 1-91 [?]) the suffix kū; since it is kit, the guṇa of the light penultimate does not occur; by the suffix accent the final-acute. ūrṇute — root ūrṇuñ ācchādane of the adādi class; laṭ, third person singular; the tiṅ-nighāta. barjaham — root vṛj saṃbhaktau; "vṛṇīte saṃbhajate gām iti baḥ payaḥ"; the suffix vic; the guṇa of the root on that account; since r follows, the visarga is replaced by r. By the upasaṃkhyāna "khaś prakaraṇe vātaśunītilagardheṣv ajaheṭtudajahātibhya" (Pā. 3-2-28 [?], vārttika as printed) the suffix khaś: here, although the word gardha is not the upapada, the suffix khaś comes by the mention of bahulam in kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam; by tiṅ śit sārvadhātukam (Pā. 3-4-113 [?]) it takes the name sārvadhātuka; then śap by kartari śap; since the root belongs to the juhotyādi class, ślu replaces śap; by ślau the root is doubled; the reduplicative is shortened; by kuhoś cuḥ the cutva; by bavayor abhedaḥ the v becomes b; since it belongs to the divodāsādi list, the first member takes the initial-acute. āvaḥ — root vṛñ varaṇe; luṅ, third person singular, tip; by itaś ca the i is elided; by mantre ghasahvaraṇa… (Pā. 2-4-80 [?]) the luk of the cli obtained in the luṅ; because of tip the guṇa of the root; since tip [here] is apṛkta after the consonant-ending stem, by halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal (Pā. 6-1-68 [?]) [the consonant-elision] and the augment aṭ for the stem; since a finite verb follows a word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 4 ‖

Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 92.5) Triṣṭubh

प्रत्यर्ची रुशदस्या अदर्शि वि तिष्ठते बाधते कृष्णमभ्वम् । स्वरुं न पेशो विदथेष्वञ्जञ्चित्रं दिवो दुहिता भानुमश्रेत् ॥ ५ ॥

pratyarcī ruśadasyā adarśi vi tiṣṭhate bādhate kṛṣṇam abhvam | svaruṃ na peśo vidatheṣv añjañ citraṃ divo duhitā bhānum aśret ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 92.5)

प्रति । अर्चिः । रुशत् । अस्याः । अदर्शि । वि । तिष्ठते । बाधते । कृष्णम् । अभ्वम् । स्वरुम् । न । पेशः । विदथेषु । अञ्जन् । चित्रम् । दिवः । दुहिता । भानुम् । अश्रेत् ॥ ५ ॥

prati | arciḥ | ruśat | asyāḥ | adarśi | vi | tiṣṭhate | bādhate | kṛṣṇam | abhvam | svarum | na | peśaḥ | vidatheṣu | añjan | citram | divaḥ | duhitā | bhānum | aśret ‖ 5 ‖

(The Saṃhitā's pratyarcī ruśat is divided in the Pada as prati | arciḥ | ruśat. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 92.5)

प्रातरनुवाके उषस्ये क्रतौ प्रत्यर्चिरित्यष्टावनुवक्तव्याः । आश्विनशस्त्रे च । तथा च सूत्रितं । प्रत्यर्चिरित्यष्टौ वृषा आ वो दिविजा इति षळिति त्रैष्टुभं । आ. ४-१४ [?] इति ॥ अस्या उषसो रुशद्दीप्यमानमर्चिस्तेजः प्रत्यदर्शि । सर्वैः पूर्वस्यां दिशि प्रथमतो दृश्यते । वि तिष्ठते । सर्वासु दिक्षु विविधमवतिष्ठते । व्याप्नोतीत्यर्थः । सर्वा दिशो व्याप्य चाभ्वं । महन्नामैतत् । अतिशयेन विपुलं कृष्णं कृष्णवर्णमन्धकारं बाधते । अपसारयति । विदथेषु यज्ञेषु स्वरुं न स्वरुनाम्ना शकलेन युक्तं यूपं यथाज्येनाध्वर्यवो अञ्जन् अञ्जन्ति तद्वन्नभसि स्वकीयं पेशो रूपमुषा अनक्ति । संश्लिष्टं करोति । तदनन्तरं चित्रं चायनीयं भानुं

prātaranuvāke uṣasye kratau pratyarcir ity aṣṭāv anuvaktavyāḥ | āśvinaśastre ca | tathā ca sūtritaṃ | pratyarcir ity aṣṭau vṛṣā ā vo divijā iti ṣaḷ iti traiṣṭubhaṃ | Ā. 4-14 [?] iti ‖ asyā uṣaso ruśad dīpyamānam arcis tejaḥ pratyadarśi | sarvaiḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi prathamato dṛśyate | vi tiṣṭhate | sarvāsu dikṣu vividham avatiṣṭhate | vyāpnotīty arthaḥ | sarvā diśo vyāpya cābhvaṃ | mahannāmaitat | atiśayena vipulaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇam andhakāraṃ bādhate | apasārayati | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu svaruṃ na svarunāmnā śakalena yuktaṃ yūpaṃ yathājyenādhvaryavo añjan añjanti tadvan nabhasi svakīyaṃ peśo rūpam uṣā anakti | saṃśliṣṭaṃ karoti | tadanantaraṃ citraṃ cāyanīyaṃ bhānuṃ

original p. 419

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 92.5, concluded:

सूर्यं दिवो दुहिता द्युलोकादुत्पन्नोषा अश्रेत् । असेवत ॥ वि तिष्ठते । समवप्रविभ्य इत्यात्मनेपदं । अश्रेत् । श्रिञ् सेवायां । लङि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् ॥

sūryaṃ divo duhitā dyulokād utpannoṣā aśret | asevata ‖ vi tiṣṭhate | samavapravibhya ity ātmanepadaṃ | aśret | śriñ sevāyāṃ | laṅi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk ‖

Translation: "…the sun: divo duhitā, the daughter of heaven, Uṣas born of the heavenly world, aśret, served him [asevata]. — vi tiṣṭhate: the ātmanepada by samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ. aśret — root śriñ sevāyām; in the laṅ the luk of śap by bahulaṃ chandasi."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 92.5)

asyāḥ — of the Uṣas deity; ruśat — shining; arciḥ — radiance; prati adarśi — is seen first (in the eastern quarter); vi tiṣṭhate — (afterwards) spreads in all the quarters; abhvam — spreading widely; kṛṣṇam — blackness (darkness); bādhate — destroys; vidatheṣu — in sacrifices; svarum na añjan — as [the priests] anoint the sacrificial post with ghee, by means of a stick; peśaḥ — her own form (which Uṣas adorns with collyrium and the like); citram — brilliant; bhānum — the sun; divaḥ duhitā — the daughter of heaven, Uṣas; aśret — served.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 92.5

"The radiance of the shining Uṣas deity is first seen in the eastern quarter. Then it destroys the darkness that spreads widely in all quarters. As priests in the sacrifices anoint the sacrificial post with ghee, using a stick, so the Uṣas deity too adorns her form. And the daughter of heaven, Uṣas, serves the radiant sun."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 92.5

"Her brilliant light is first seen towards the east ; it spreads and disperses the thick darkness ; she anoints her body as the priests anoint the sacrificial post in sacrifices ; the daughter of the sky awaits the glorious Sun." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 92.5)

"At the time of reciting the prātaranuvāka mantras, for the mantras connected with the Uṣasya sacrifice, the eight Ṛks beginning pratyarciḥ, and also for the mantras of the Āśvina-śastra, the application of these mantras is shown by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra 'pratyarcir ity aṣṭau vṛṣā ā vo divijā iti ṣaḍ iti traiṣṭubhaṃ' (Ā. 4-14 [?])."

svaruṃ na — "svaru means 'a stick, a rod', the stick with which collyrium is applied to the eye. As ghee is smeared with it on the sacrificial post, so the Uṣas deity adorns herself with collyrium, or with a stick applied to the eye: this is the idea.

original p. 420

"Besides, svaru means 'sacrificial post' too. In the Ṛk 7-35-7 [?] the word svarūṇām is explained 'svarūṇāṃ yūpānām', and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-4 [?] 'svarur na yūpaśakalavājī' — 'svarur atra yūpaṃ lakṣayati' ['here svaru indicates the sacrificial post']: so the bhāṣya-writers explain it. In general the meaning of the word svaru is 'sacrificial post'. Some Ṛks in which this word occurs, for example —"

उदु स्वरुर्नवजा नाक्रः पेशो वे अनक्ति सुधितिः सुमेकः ।

ud u svarur navajā nākraḥ peśo ve anakti sudhitiḥ sumekaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-4 [?]; the Saṃhitā text as read from the print, doubtful [?])

शं नः स्वरूणां मितयो भवन्तु शं नः प्रस्वः शम्वस्तु वेदिः ।

śaṃ naḥ svarūṇāṃ mitayo bhavantu śaṃ naḥ prasvaḥ śam v astu vediḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-7 [?])

बृहन्निदिध्म एषां भूरि शस्तं पृथुः स्वरुः ।

bṛhann ididdhma eṣāṃ bhūri śastaṃ pṛthuḥ svaruḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-3 [?]; read as printed, nidhma [?])

ते देवासः स्वरवस्तस्थिवांसः प्रजावदस्मे दिधिषन्तु रत्नम् ।

te devāsaḥ svaravas tasthivāṃsaḥ prajāvad asme didhiṣantu ratnam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-6 [?])

हंसा इव श्रेणिशो यतानाः शुक्रा वसानाः स्वरवो न आगुः ।

haṃsā iva śreṇiśo yatānāḥ śukrā vasānāḥ svarāvo na āguḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-9 [?])

शृङ्गाणीवेच्छृङ्गिणां सं ददृश्रे चषालवन्तः स्वरवः पृथिव्याम् ।

śṛṅgāṇīvec chṛṅgiṇāṃ saṃ dadṛśre caṣālavantaḥ svaravaḥ pṛthivyām | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-10 [?])

अस्थुरु चित्रा उषसः पुरस्तान्मिता इव स्वरवोऽध्वरेषु ।

asthur u citrā uṣasaḥ purastān mitā iva svaravo 'dhvareṣu | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-2 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative (for the group): "…the measures of the svarus be peace for us; may the vedi be peace for us. — Those gods who stood as svarus [sacrificial posts], may they bestow upon us wealth with offspring. — Like geese in rows, bright, clothed [?], the svarus came to us. — Like horns of the horned, the svarus with their ring-heads were seen on the earth. — The bright Uṣases have stood forth in the east like measured svarus at the sacrifices." The Saṃhitā texts above are read from the print and each is doubtful in places [?].

"The word svaru in these Ṛks indicates the sense 'sacrificial post'. Yāska has given no explanation of this word."

ruśat — "From 'auspicious colour', 'shining' is the meaning. The order of its derivation has been told in the commentary on the Ṛk 1-92-2 [p. 409]."

arciḥ — arciḥ, śociḥ, tapaḥ and the like being read among the names of blazing (Ni. 1-[?] [?]), 'light' is the meaning.

vi tiṣṭhate — "'She spreads in various ways in the three worlds' is the meaning."

vidatheṣu — "yajñaḥ, venaḥ, adhvaraḥ and the like are read among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-17 [?]). vidathāni are vedanāni, 'knowledges'. Explaining this meaning, the author of the Nirukta cites the Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā —

original p. 421

होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥

hotā devo amartyaḥ purastād eti māyayā | vidathāni pracodayan ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "The immortal god, the Hotṛ, goes in front by his power, urging the vidathas."

"— so here too: 'in the sacrifices that are means of knowledge'."

divo duhitā — "'Born from the heavenly world': Uṣas is meant. For the Uṣas the epithet divo duhitā, or duhitar divaḥ, in the vocative, comes in many places; for example —"

त्वं त्र्यभिरागहि वाजेभिर्दुहितर्दिवः ।

tvaṃ try-abhir āgahi vājebhir duhitar divaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-20 [?]; read as printed)

सह वामेन न उषो व्युच्छा दुहितर्दिवः ।

saha vāmena na uṣo vy uchā duhitar divaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-1 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Come to us with your three-fold [gifts], with strengths, O daughter of heaven. — Dawn forth with good things for us, O Uṣas, daughter of heaven."

"— so in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-30-5 [?]; 7-42-15 [?] and many other Ṛks this word is used."

abhvam — mahat, bṛhat, ukṣitaḥ and the like being read among the names of the great (Ni. 3-3 [?]) | "The extremely great, deep darkness too the Uṣas destroys."

bhānum aśret — "One meaning: 'she served the sun'; or 'she obtained radiance'; and there is another meaning: 'she, who at every moment is blazing, assumes another form' — so Skandasvāmin says: 'pratikṣaṇaṃ dīptā rūpāntarībhavatīty arthaḥ'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 92.5)

adarśi — root dṛśir prekṣaṇe; in the passive luṅ, third person singular, the suffix ta; by ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 3-1-66 [?]) ciṇ for the cli; by ciṇo luk (Pā. 6-4-104 [?]) the elision of the ta that follows ciṇ; the guṇa of the light penultimate of the root on account of ciṇ; the augment aṭ for the stem; since it follows a word, the nighāta accent. vi tiṣṭhate — root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; parasmaipada; since the preverb vi is joined, the ātmanepada by samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ (Pā. 1-3-22 [?]); laṭ, third person singular; by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e the final e; śap; by pāghrādhmāsthā… (Pā. 7-3-78 [?]) the replacement tiṣṭha for the stem; the tiṅ-nighāta. bādhate — root bādhṛ viloḍane, the ātmanepada in the laṭ; since it follows a finite verb, the nighāta accent does not occur; since śap and the lasārvadhātuka suffix are unaccented, the accent of the root remains.

original p. 422

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 92.5, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly):

divaḥ — by ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171) the case-ending takes the acute. aśret — root śriñ sevāyām; laṅ, third person singular, tip, the elision of its i [by itaś ca lopaḥ]; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ the guṇa of the ik vowel of the root because of the suffix; the augment aṭ for the stem: aśret; since it follows a word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 92.6)

अतारिष्म तमसस्पारमस्योषा उच्छन्ती वयुना कृणोति । श्रिये छन्दो न स्मयते विभाती सुप्रतीका सौमनसायाजीगः ॥ ६ ॥

atāriṣma tamasas pāram asyoṣā ucchantī vayunā kṛṇoti | śriye chando na smayate vibhātī supratīkā saumanasāyājīgaḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 92.6)

अतारिष्म । तमसः । पारम् । अस्य । उषाः । उच्छन्ती । वयुना । कृणोति । श्रिये । छन्दः । न । स्मयते । विऽभाती । सुऽप्रतीका । सौमनसाय । अजीगरिति ॥ ६ ॥

atāriṣma | tamasaḥ | pāram | asya | uṣāḥ | ucchantī | vayunā | kṛṇoti | śriye | chandaḥ | na | smayate | vi-bhātī | su-pratīkā | saumanasāya | ajīgar iti ‖ 6 ‖

(The Pada's ajīgar iti stands for the Saṃhitā's ājīgaḥ, as in 92.4 āvar iti; the Saṃhitā's ucchantī is printed with a double cch. Accent marks not reproduced.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 92.6) begins at the foot of p. 422

अस्य नैशस्य तमसोऽन्धकारस्य पारं समाप्तिप्रदेशमतारिष्म । उत्तीर्णा आभूम । आनन्तरमुच्छन्ती नैशं तमो वर्जयन्त्युषा वयुना वयुनानि

asya naiśasya tamaso 'ndhakārasya pāraṃ samāptipradeśam atāriṣma | uttīrṇā ābhūma | ānantaram ucchantī naiśaṃ tamo varjayanty uṣā vayunā vayunāni

original p. 423

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 92.6, continued:

सर्वेषां प्राणिनां ज्ञानानि कृणोति । निर्मिमीते । श्रिये संपदर्थं छन्दो न स्मयते । यथोपच्छन्दयिता वशीकरणे समर्थः पुरुष आर्थ्यसमीपं [?] प्राप्य तत्प्रीत्यर्थं स्मयते हसति एवं विभाती विशिष्टप्रकाशं कुर्वत्युषाः स्वकीययां निर्मलदन्तपङ्क्त्या हसन्तीव दृश्यते । एवं सुप्रतीका विशिष्टप्रकाशरूपत्वेन शोभनाङ्गी सती सौमनसाय सर्वेषां सौमनस्यायाजीगः । अन्धकारं भक्षितवती ॥ अतारिष्म । तॄ प्लवनतरणयोः । लुङः सिचि वृद्धिः । तमसः । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति विसर्जनीयस्य संहितायां सत्वं । स्मयते । स्मिङ् ईषद्धसने । भौवादिकः । अजीगः । गॄ निगरणे । लङि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्येत्वं । तुजादित्वाद्दीर्घः ॥

sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ jñānāni kṛṇoti | nirmimīte | śriye saṃpadarthaṃ chando na smayate | yathopacchandayitā vaśīkaraṇe samarthaḥ puruṣa ārthya-samīpaṃ [?] prāpya tatprītyarthaṃ smayate hasati evaṃ vibhātī viśiṣṭaprakāśaṃ kurvaty uṣāḥ svakīyayā nirmaladantapaṅktyā hasantīva dṛśyate | evaṃ supratīkā viśiṣṭaprakāśarūpatvena śobhanāṅgī satī saumanasāya sarveṣāṃ saumanasyāyājīgaḥ | andhakāraṃ bhakṣitavatī ‖ atāriṣma | tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ | luṅaḥ sici vṛddhiḥ | tamasaḥ | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti visarjanīyasya saṃhitāyāṃ satvaṃ | smayate | smiṅ īṣaddhasane | bhauvādikaḥ | ajīgaḥ | gṝ nigaraṇe | laṅi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīty abhyāsasyetvaṃ | tujāditvād dīrghaḥ ‖

Translation: "…produces vayunā, the knowledges (consciousness), in all living beings. Śriye chando na smayate: as a man who is skilful in winning over by flattery (upacchandayitā) goes near the one from whom he wants something and smayate, smiles, in order to please him, so the Uṣas vibhātī — making a special light — is seen as if smiling with her own bright rows of teeth. So supratīkā, of beautiful limbs through her special form of light, for saumanasāya, the good-heartedness of all, ajīgaḥ — she has devoured the darkness. — atāriṣma — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; the vṛddhi before sic in the luṅ. tamasaḥ — the visarga of the genitive becomes s in the Saṃhitā by ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…. smayate — root smiṅ īṣaddhasane, of the bhvādi class. ajīgaḥ — root gṝ nigaraṇe; in the laṅ the ślu for śap by bahulaṃ chandasi; the i-vowel of the reduplicative by bahulaṃ chandasi; the lengthening because it belongs to the tujādi group."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 92.6)

asya tamasaḥ — of this darkness of night-time; pāram — the end; atāriṣma — we have crossed; ucchantī — (removing the darkness) appearing; uṣāḥ — the deity Uṣas; vayunā — (of all beings) the consciousness; kṛṇoti — creates; śriye — for wealth; chandaḥ — one who is able to flatter by praise; smayate na — as he goes to the wealthy and smiles to please him; vibhātī — shining, with the laughter of her radiance; supratīkā — beautifully shining in radiance, or one with an attractive face; saumanasāya — for the delight (of the beings); ajīgaḥ — swallowed (the darkness).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 92.6

"With the help of the Uṣas deity we have crossed to the end of the darkness of night. The Uṣas deity, appearing by driving away the darkness, creates consciousness in all beings. And as a man able to praise [and so win over], for the acquisition of wealth goes to the wealthy and, to please him, smiles broadly, so she too shines, smiling with the laughter of her radiance, and, beautifully lit and attractive in her radiance, she has swallowed the darkness for the delight of all beings."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 92.6

"We have crossed over the boundary of darkness. Ushas restores the consciousness of living beings ; bright-shining, she smiles, like a flatterer, to obtain favour, and lovely in all her radiance, she has swallowed the darkness for our delight." — as printed.

original p. 424

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 92.6)

ucchantī — "For this word one meaning is 'removing, destroying'; another meaning may be given: 'shining, appearing with radiance'. The derivation of the word uṣā too comes from ucchati (Ni. 2-18 [?]). But the word ucchati may be derived from the root uchī vivāse, or from vaś kāntau; the author of the Nirukta also dealt with this matter in section 2-[?]. In the present context either meaning may be taken. ucchantī uṣāḥ may also mean 'the Uṣas who appears, driving away the darkness', or 'the Uṣas who shines'."

chandaḥ — "rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ and the like are read among the names of the praiser (Ni. 3-16 [?]). The meaning here is 'the praiser, who goes to a wealthy man and flatters him to win him over, and in the course of this praise smiles at him: as this praiser becomes smiling-faced, so the Uṣas too, with her radiance, smiles': this is one meaning. Besides, as Skandasvāmin says: 'chandas iti kāntikarmasu pāṭhāt chandaśśabdo 'tra kāmivacanaḥ' [as read, partly clotted [?]] — since 'chandas' is read among the names of loveliness (Ni. 3-[?] [?]), the word chandaḥ here may be said to mean a lover (kāmin) — a woman in love, who, smiling a little, with her tooth-rays flashing, shows [them]: yathā kāminī īṣat smayantī sphuraddantakiraṇā prakāśayati evam uṣāḥ svakiraṇān āviṣkaroti: as a lovely woman, smiling gently, displays the rays of her teeth, so the Uṣas also displays her rays."

supratīkā — pratīkaśabdo mukhavacanaḥ darśanaparyāyo vā | sumukhā sudarśanā vā | "pratīka means 'face', or 'seeing, appearance'. Therefore here it means 'one who has a beautiful face' or 'one who has a charming appearance'. In the Ṛksaṃhitā:"

यावन्मात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुपर्ण्यो वसते मातरिश्वः ।

yāvan mātram uṣaso na pratīkaṃ suparṇyo vasate mātariśvaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-19 [?]; the print has suparṇyo 3 vasate, a mark of protraction)

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "As much as the [bright] face of the Uṣases, the well-winged [?] wind dwells [in it]." Reading of the whole citation doubtful [?].

"— in this Ṛk too the word pratīka is explained in such a way."

ājīgaḥ — "In explaining the derivation of this word the author of the Nirukta cites a Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā —"

यदा ते मर्तो अनु भोगमानळादिद्ग्रसिष्ठ ओषधीरजीगः ।

yadā te marto anu bhogam ānaḷ ād id grasiṣṭha oṣadhīr ajīgaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-58-2 [?]; the numerals as read, doubtful)

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "When the mortal has attained your enjoyment, then you, the devourer, have swallowed the plants."

original p. 425

Special Topics of Rik 92.6, continued from p. 424 (Kannada): "— citing this Ṛk [yadā te marto anu bhogam ānaḍ…], the author of the Nirukta gives three meanings: 'jigarṣtir gīratikarmā vā gṛṇātikarmā vā gṛhṇātikarmā vā' (Ni. 6-[?] [?]): that is, 'eating', or 'praising', or 'seizing' — any of these may do. But in the Ṛk now in hand too, for ājīgaḥ Sāyaṇa explains 'andhakāraṃ bhakṣitavatī' — 'she swallowed the darkness'; and Skandasvāmin explains 'trīn api lokān prati gacchati' [as read [?]] — 'she goes over the three worlds, pervading them'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 92.6)

atāriṣma — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; luṅ, first person plural, mas; by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ (Pā. 3-4-99 [?]) the s of the suffix is elided; for the cli of the luṅ, by cleḥ sic the replacement sic; by sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 7-2-1 [?]) the vṛddhi of the root; the augment aṭ; since it stands at the head of the pāda no nighāta; since the augment is acute, the word is initial-acute. tamasaḥ — in tamasaḥ pāram, by ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspoṣeṣu (Pā. 8-3-53 [?]) the visarga takes s. kṛṇoti — root kṛvi hiṃsāyām; laṭ, third person singular; by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (Pā. 3-1-80 [?]) the u-suffix in place of śap, with the replacement of the stem-final a; because it is idit, the root takes num; when kṛn-u-ti has been formed, by ato lopaḥ [as read, doubtful [?]] the a is elided because of the u; since the ṛ precedes, ṇatva of the n; the guṇa of the u because of tip; the tiṅ-nighāta. śriye — the dative singular; by sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the acute. smayate — root smiṅ īṣaddhasane, of the bhvādi class; laṭ, third person singular; by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e the final e; śap; because of it, the guṇa of the root's i, and ay; the tiṅ-nighāta. ajīgaḥ — root gṝ nigaraṇe; laṅ, second person singular, sip [as printed; the form is that of the second-person suffix for a third-person sense by vyatyaya [?]], the i elided; by bahulaṃ chandasi ślu for śap; by ślau the root is doubled; by kuhoś cuḥ the g of the reduplicative becomes j; by bahulaṃ chandasi the reduplicative takes i; —

original p. 426

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 92.6, concluded: [ajīgaḥ, continued —] "since it is listed among the tujādi words, by tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya (Pā. 6-1-7 [?]) the reduplicative is lengthened; the augment aṭ for the stem; since it follows a word, the nighāta accent." ‖ 6 ‖

भास्वती नेत्री सूनृतानां दिवः स्तवे दुहिता गोतमेभिः । प्रजावतो नृवतो अश्वबुध्यानुषो गोअग्रानुप मासि वाजान् ॥ ७ ॥

bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānāṃ divaḥ stave duhitā gotamebhiḥ | prajāvato nṛvato aśvabudhyān uṣo goagrān upa māsi vājān ‖ 7 ‖

भास्वती । नेत्री । सूनृतानाम् । दिवः । स्तवे । दुहिता । गोतमेभिः । प्रजाऽवतः । नृऽवतः । अश्वऽबुध्यान् । उषः । गोऽअग्रान् । उप । मासि । वाजान् ॥ ७ ॥

bhāsvatī | netrī | sūnṛtānām | divaḥ | stave | duhitā | gotamebhiḥ | prajā-vataḥ | nṛ-vataḥ | aśva-budhyān | uṣaḥ | go-agrān | upa | māsi | vājān ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 92.7)

भास्वती तेजस्विनी । सूनृतेति वाङ्नाम । सूनृतानां प्रियसत्यात्मिकानां नेत्री प्रेरयित्री कारयित्री । उषसि हि जातायां मनुष्यप्रमुखाः प्राणिनः स्वस्वव्यापारायेतस्ततः शब्दं कुर्वन्ति । एवंभूता दिवो दुहिता द्युलोकसकाशादुत्पन्नोषा गोतमेभिर्गोतमवंशजैरस्माभिः स्तवे । स्तूयते । हे उष आस्माभिः स्तुता त्वं वाजानन्नान्युप मासि । प्रयच्छ । कीदृशान्वाजान् । प्रजावतः प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिर्युक्तान्

bhāsvatī tejasvinī | sūnṛteti vāṅnāma | sūnṛtānāṃ priyasatyātmikānāṃ netrī preyitrī kārayitrī | uṣasi hi jātāyāṃ manuṣyapramukhāḥ prāṇinaḥ svasvavyāpārāyetas tataḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti | evaṃbhūtā divo duhitā dyulokasakāśād utpannoṣā gotamebhir gotamavaṃśajair asmābhiḥ stave | stūyate | he uṣa āsmābhiḥ stutā tvaṃ vājānn annāny upa māsi | prayaccha | kīdṛśān vājān | prajāvataḥ prajābhiḥ putrapautrādibhir yuktān

original p. 427

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 92.7, concluded:

नृवतो दासलक्षणैर्नृभिरुपेतान् अश्वबुध्यान् । अश्वा बुध्ना विद्यमानत्वेन बोद्धव्या येषु वाजेषु तान् । यद्वा । अश्वबुध्यान् । वर्णव्यापत्त्या यकारः । अश्वमूलान् । अश्वैर्हि राजानो धनान्यन्नानि च लभन्ते । अतोऽन्नानां तन्मूलत्वं । गोअग्रान् । गावोऽग्रे प्रमुखे येषां तादृशान् ॥ भास्वती । भा दीप्तौ । असुन् । ततो मतुप् । मादुपधायाः इति मतुपो वत्वं । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । नेत्री । ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति ङीप उदात्तत्वं । स्तवे । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । कर्मणि लट् बहुलं छन्दसीति बहुलग्रहणाद्ये को ऽपि लुक् [?] । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः । छन्दस्युभयथेत्येकारस्यार्धधातुकत्वेन ङित्त्वाभावाद्गुणावादेशौ । नृवतः । व्यत्ययेन मतोर्वत्वं । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं । मासि । मा माने । आदादिकः ॥

nṛvato dāsalakṣaṇair nṛbhir upetān aśvabudhyān | aśvā budhnā vidyamānatvena boddhavyā yeṣu vājeṣu tān | yadvā | aśvabudhyān | varṇavyāpattyā yakāraḥ | aśvamūlān | aśvair hi rājāno dhanāny annāni ca labhante | ato 'nnānāṃ tanmūlatvaṃ | goagrān | gāvo 'gre pramukhe yeṣāṃ tādṛśān ‖ bhāsvatī | bhā dīptau | asun | tato matup | mādupadhāyāḥ iti matupo vatvaṃ | ugitaś ceti ṅīp | netrī | ṛnnebhyo ṅīp | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ | stave | ṣṭuñ stutau | karmaṇi laṭ bahulaṃ chandasīti bahulagrahaṇād ye ko 'pi luk [?] | lopas ta ātmanepadeṣv iti talopaḥ | chandasy ubhayathety ekārasyārdhadhātukatvena ṅittvābhāvād guṇāvādeśau | nṛvataḥ | vyatyayena matorvatvaṃ | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub iti matupa udāttatvaṃ | māsi | mā māne | ādādikaḥ ‖

Translation (bhāṣya, concluded): "…prajāvataḥ, possessed of progeny, sons, grandsons and so on; nṛvataḥ, endowed with men, with servants; aśvabudhyān — those vājas, foods, in which horses are to be known as existing as the budhna, the foundation [of wealth]; or aśvabudhyān, with y by a change of letter: 'having horses as their root': for by horses kings obtain wealth and food; therefore foods have horses as their root. Goagrān — those in which cows stand in front, as the chief. — bhāsvatī — root bhā dīptau, the suffix asun, then matup; by mādupadhāyāś ca… the v of matup; ṅīp by ugitaś ca. netrī — ṅīp after a stem in ṛ (ṛnnebhyo ṅīp); by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt the ṅīp takes the acute. stave — root ṣṭuñ stutau; the laṭ in the passive; the elision of the ta by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu; guṇa and av since the e is ārdhadhātuka and not ṅit by chandasy ubhayathā. nṛvataḥ — the v of matup by vyatyaya; by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub the matup takes the acute. māsi — root mā māne of the ādādika class."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 92.7)

bhāsvatī — the radiant one; sūnṛtānām — of speech pleasing and true; netrī — the cause; divaḥ duhitā — Uṣas deity, the daughter of the heavenly world; gotamebhiḥ — by us, born in the line of Gotama; stave — is praised; uṣaḥ — O Uṣas deity; prajāvataḥ — endowed with offspring; nṛvataḥ — with servants and other people; aśvabudhyān — distinguished by horses; goagrān — filled with cows; vājān — foods; upa māsi — graciously give.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 92.7

"We, born in the line of Gotama, praise the Uṣas deity, who is radiant, the cause of speech that is pleasing and true, and born of the heavenly world. O Uṣas deity, graciously give us the foods that are endowed with offspring, with servants and other people, distinguished by horses and filled with cows."

English Translation printed in English in the source; Rik 92.7

"The brilliant daughter of the sky, the exciter of pleasant voices, is praised by the descendants of Gotama. Ushas, grant us food associated with progeny and dependants and distinguished by horses and cattle." — as printed.

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 92.7) Kannada; begins at the foot of p. 427

sūnṛtānāṃ netrī — "sūnṛtā, sūnṛtāvatī, sūnṛtāvarī and the like are all epithets, or synonymous words, of the Uṣas (Ni. 3-[?] [?]). sūnṛteti vāṅnāma ['sūnṛtā is a name of speech']; netrī utpāda-

original p. 428

Special Topics of Rik 92.7, continued from p. 427 (Kannada): "— netrī utpādayitrī: uṣasaḥ prādurbhāvānantaraṃ hi paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ sarve śabdaṃ kurvanti | ata eva tāsāṃ vācāṃ pravartayiteti ucyate ['for after the appearance of Uṣas all animals, birds, deer and so on make their sounds; therefore she is called the originator of those voices'] — that is, the word sūnṛtānām is connected with all dealings in speech. Since after Uṣas rises the speech-dealings of all animals, birds and the rest begin, the meaning is that the Uṣases are the originators of all these. Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha and others use this epithet especially in their own hymns. For example —"

भास्वती नेत्री सूनृतानामचेति चित्रा वि दुरो न आवः ।

bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānām aceti citrā vi duro na āvaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-4 [?])

एषा नेत्री राधसः सूनृतानामुषा उच्छन्ती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः ।

eṣā netrī rādhasaḥ sūnṛtānām uṣā ucchantī ribhyate vasiṣṭhaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76-7 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative (both): "The radiant leader of pleasant words has been noticed; she, the wonderful, has opened our doors. — This leader of bounty and of pleasant words, the Uṣas, shining forth, is praised by the Vasiṣṭhas."

"In some places Sāyaṇa explains the word sūnṛtānām as stutīnām, 'of praises': 'the leader of the praises'."

gotamebhiḥ — "For this word Sāyaṇa says 'ṛṣibhir asmābhiḥ', 'by us, the seers'; and Skandasvāmin says 'ekasminn eva bahuvacanaṃ | gotamena mayā' — the plural is used for the singular: 'by me, Gotama'."

aśvabudhyān — "Two kinds of meaning are given for this attribute. 'aśvair yo [yeṣu] boddhavyas te aśvabudhyāḥ tān' [as read, clotted [?]]: wealth, or food, that is to be known by the existence of horses, that is, [wealth] with abundant horses. Or, as Sāyaṇa says, since the word aśvabudhyān [stands] with y by a change of letter in place of the n, it is aśvabudhnān, from which the sense 'foods that have horses as their root' also arises. If the second meaning is given, since kings get wealth and foods by the help of horses, it is called aśvabudhya. In the 8th Ṛk of the same sūkta [1-92-8 [?]] the same word occurs; for that too these two meanings are given."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 92.7)

bhāsvatī — root bhā dīptau; the suffix asun, which is obtained after all roots (U. 4-189 [?]); bhāḥ asyāḥ asti iti bhāsvatī; by tad asyāstyasmin… (Pā. 5-2-94 [?]) the suffix matup; by mādupadhāyāś ca… (Pā. 8-2-9 [?]) the m of matup becomes v; by ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6 [?]) the ṅīp in the feminine. netrī — root nīñ prāpaṇe; in the agent sense the suffix tṛc; the word netṛ; in the feminine, because the stem ends in ṛ, by ṛnnebhyo ṅīp (Pā. 4-1-5 [?]) the suffix ṅīp; the ṛ is replaced by y (yaṇ). —

original p. 429

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 92.7, continued (grammar page, noted briefly):

[netrī, continued —] "the ṛ, being acute by cit (Pā. 6-1-163 [?]), takes the replacement yaṇ, and the ṅīp that follows it, by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt (Pā. 6-1-174 [?]), takes the acute." stave — root ṣṭuñ stutau; in the passive laṭ, third person singular, the suffix ta; by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 [?]), through the mention of bahulam there, the luk of yak, which is obtained in the passive; by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41 [?]) the t of the suffix is elided; the e remains; by chandasy ubhayathā the e has the name ārdhadhātuka, and by sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. 1-2-4 [?]) it does not become ṅit; because of the suffix the guṇa of the root and the replacement āv; since it follows a word, the nighāta accent. gotamebhiḥ — the word gotama; the instrumental plural, bhis following; by bahulaṃ chandasi there is no ais; by bahuvacane jhaly et the e. nṛvataḥ — in the sense 'he has nṛ', the suffix matup after the word nṛ; though there is no cause, by vyatyaya the m of matup becomes v; the accusative plural; by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup (Pā. 6-1-176 [?]) the matup takes the acute. māsi — root mā māne, of the adādi class; laṭ, second person singular; the luk of śap; the tiṅ-nighāta. ‖ 7 ‖
