वधैः । दुःऽशंसान् । अप । दुःऽध्यः । जहि । दूरे । वा । ये । अन्ति । वा । के । चित् । अत्रिणः । अथ । यज्ञाय । गृणते । सुऽगम् । कृधि । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ९ ॥

vadhaiḥ | duḥ-śaṃsān | apa | duḥ-dhyaḥ | jahi | dūre | vā | ye | anti | vā | ke | cit | atriṇaḥ | atha | yajñāya | gṛṇate | su-gam | kṛdhi | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 9 ‖ Reading note: Saṃhitā dūḍhyaḥ, Pada duḥ-dhyaḥ as printed, as in 94.8; Saṃhitā athā, Pada atha and Saṃhitā kṛdhy agne, Pada kṛdhi agne, by sandhi; Saṃhitā duḥśaṃsām̐, Pada duḥ-śaṃsān.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.9)

हे अग्ने त्वं वधैर्हननसाधनैरायुधैर्दुःशंसान् दुःखेन कीर्तनीयान् दूढ्यो दुर्धियः पापबुद्धीनपि जहि । वधं प्रापय । ये केचित् ये के चन दूरे विप्रकृष्टदेशे वान्तिके समीपदेशे वा वर्तमाना अत्रिणोऽत्तारो राक्षसादयो विद्यन्ते तान् स्पर्धियोऽपि [?] जहीत्यर्थः ॥ अथानन्तरं यज्ञाय यज्ञपतये गृणते त्वां स्तुवते यजमानाय सुगं शोभनं मार्गं कृधि । कुरु । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ वधैः । हनश्च वध इति हन्तेः करणेऽप् वधादेशश्च । स चादन्तोऽन्तोदात्तः । तस्यातो लोपे सत्यपि निवृत्तिस्वरेण [?] प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वं । दुःशंसान् । ईषद्दुःसुष्विति कर्मणि खल् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । जहि । लोटि हिः । हन्तेर्ज इति जादेशः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वाद्धेर्लुग्भावः [?] । अन्ति । अन्तिकस्य कादिलोपो बहुलमिति कलोपः । अत्रिणः । आदेस्त्रिनि चेति त्रिनिप्रत्ययः । इकारो नकारपरित्राणार्थः । गृणते । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । सुगं । सुदुरोरधिकरणे । पा. ३-२-४८ [?] इति गमेर्डः । कृधि । श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसीति हेर्धिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् ॥

he agne tvaṃ vadhair hananasādhanair āyudhair duḥśaṃsān duḥkhena kīrtanīyān dūḍhyo durdhiyaḥ pāpabuddhīn api jahi | vadhaṃ prāpaya | ye kecit ye ke cana dūre viprakṛṣṭadeśe vāntike samīpadeśe vā vartamānā atriṇo 'ttāro rākṣasādayo vidyante tān spardhiyo 'pi [?] jahīty arthaḥ ‖ athānantaraṃ yajñāya yajñapataye gṛṇate tvāṃ stuvate yajamānāya sugaṃ śobhanaṃ mārgaṃ kṛdhi | kuru | anyat pūrvavat ‖ vadhaiḥ | hanaś ca vadha iti hanteḥ karaṇe 'p vadhādeśaś ca | sa cādanto 'ntodāttaḥ | tasyāto lope saty api nivṛttisvareṇa [?] pratyayasyodāttatvaṃ | duḥśaṃsān | īṣadduḥsuṣv iti karmaṇi khal | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | jahi | loṭi hiḥ | hanter ja iti jādeśaḥ | tasyāsiddhavad atrābhād ity asiddhatvād dher lugbhāvaḥ [?] | anti | antikasya kādilopo bahulam iti kalopaḥ | atriṇaḥ | ādes trini ceti trinipratyayaḥ | ikāro nakāraparitrāṇārthaḥ | gṛṇate | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | sugaṃ | sudurorādhikaraṇe | pā. 3-2-48 [?] iti gamer ḍaḥ | kṛdhi | śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasīti her dhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O Agni, with your death-dealing weapons strike the evil-speaking ones (those who are hard to speak of), the evil-minded: bring them to death. Whichever eaters (atriṇaḥ — ogres and the like) there are, far off or near at hand, strike those as well. Then, for the sacrificer who praises you, the master of the sacrifice, make a fair path. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: vadhaiḥ — from han in the instrumental sense with ap and substitution of vadha, ending in a, final-acute; duḥśaṃsān — khal in the passive; jahi — loṭ, hi, ja for han, with the loss of the hi as treated as non-operating [?]; anti — from antika by loss of ka; atriṇaḥ — the suffix trin, whose i is for the preservation of the n; gṛṇate — case-ending acute; sugam — gam with ḍa after su/dur in a locative sense; kṛdhi — hi → dhi in the Veda after kṛ (the rule on śru, śṛṇu, pṛ, kṛ, vṛ), with elision of the vikaraṇa (u) by bahulaṃ chandasi. The grammatical tail is clotted at nivṛttisvareṇa and lugbhāvaḥ; the sūtra numeral is as read, doubtful [?].

original p. 540

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"agne — O Agni; vadhaiḥ — with the weapons that cause death; duḥśaṃsān — those known as evil-speaking ones (wicked ones); dūḍhyaḥ — the enemies of sinful mind; apa jahi — destroy; ye kecit — whichever enemies; dūre — far off; vā — or near at hand; vā — whether; atriṇaḥ — such rākṣasa-like, evil enemies (destroy); atha — then; yajñāya — to the sacrificer; gṛṇate — (who praises you) the praising one; sugaṃ — a lovely path; kṛdhi — make; agne — O Agni; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, destroy with your death-dealing weapons the evil-minded enemies, known as wicked ones, whether they are far off or near. Destroy our wicked enemies, the ogres. Make a lovely path for the sacrificer, the praiser of you. Through friendship with you, favour us so that we suffer no harm of any kind."

English Translation (as printed)

Overcome with your fatal (weapons) the wicked and the impicus [sic], all who are enemies whether distant or near, and then provide an easy ( path ) for the sacrificer who praises you ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Kannada)

vadhaiḥ — hananasādhanair āyudhaiḥ: "with weapons that are the means of killing, that is the sense. In the Ṛksaṃhitā in general the word vadhaiḥ is used in the sense vadhasādhanair āyudhaiḥ. For example —" Gloss, editorial and tentative: "when, much-invoked one, for Kutsa you go about, smiting Śuṣṇa with unending blows". Gloss, editorial and tentative: "may he himself drive from us, with blows, the reviling and the ill-intentioned".

कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वञ्छुष्णमनन्तैः परियासि वधैः । kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvañ chuṣṇam anantaiḥ pariyāsi vadhaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-9 as read [?])

स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वधैरजेत दुर्मतिम् । svayaṃ so asmad ā nido vadhair ajeta durmatim | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-6 as read [?])

"Likewise in 1-133-6; 2-31-2; 6-20-4 [all as read, doubtful [?]] and other Ṛks, the word vadhaiḥ is used throughout in the sense of 'means of killing'."

original p. 541

atriṇaḥ — "attāraḥ, bhakṣitāraś ca: the devourers, who eat men, or the rākṣasas who rend bellies (the Kannada word as read, doubtful [?])."

sugaṃ — śobhanaṃ mārgaṃ: "a lovely path. From the point of view of travel, it means a path that is easily passed along; from the moral point of view, it means the best, the most glorious path. The word is used in both senses. For example —"

देवयानान् सुगान् पथः कुरुष्व सुमनाः स्वयम् । devayānān sugān pathaḥ kuruṣva sumanāḥ svayam | (Bṛhaddevatā 7-6-5 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "make the god-travelled paths easy to go, yourself of good mind". "In this verse the sense is of paths along which the gods travel easily. In the same sense in the Ṛksaṃhitā also:" Gloss, editorial and tentative: "may he make welfare and an easy path for our horse, for the ram and the ewe, for men, for women, for the cow".

शं नः करत्यर्वते सुगं मेषाय मेष्ये । नृभ्यो नारिभ्यो गवे ॥ śaṃ naḥ karaty arvate sugaṃ meṣāya meṣye | nṛbhyo nāribhyo gave ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-43-6 as read [?])

"In this Ṛk, and in Ṛks such as 9-63-10 [?] and 10-?-5 [?], it is said to be an easily traversed path; and in the sense of the moral view —" Gloss, editorial and tentative: "Bṛhaspati, turn that path away; make for us an easy way for this divine feast".

बृहस्पते अप तं वर्तया पथः सुगं नो अस्यै देववीतये कृधि ॥ bṛhaspate apa taṃ vartayā pathaḥ sugaṃ no asyai devavītaye kṛdhi ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?] [?], as read "२-३३-२" [?])

"— in Ṛks such as this, the word sugaṃ, from the moral standpoint, means 'what is to be gone to well' (suṣṭhu gantavyaṃ): 'yajñānuṣṭhānāya sumatiṃ dehi', 'give a good mind for the performance of sacrifice'; it is also understood as the good sense that performs sacrifice and the like. Moreover, in places such as 1-103-4 [?]; 6-109-2 [?], the word sugaṃ is explained as 'happiness'."

"Skandasvāmin explains this last sense as to be taken in this Ṛk also, saying āsetitam api sukhanāmaitat; iha draṣṭavyaṃ [read as printed, doubtful [?]; gloss, editorial and tentative: 'this too is a name for happiness; to be seen here'], and cites the Ṛk —"

अस्मभ्यमिन्द्र वरिवः सुगं कृधि प्र शत्रूणां मघवन् वृष्ण्या रुज । asmabhyam indra varivaḥ sugaṃ kṛdhi pra śatrūṇāṃ maghavan vṛṣṇyā ruja | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-102-4 [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "for us, Indra, make wide room and an easy way; break the vigour of the foes, bounteous one". "Having cited this Ṛk, they explain that, just as the sense is there, so here too the word suga, though not read among the names of happiness (sukha), has the meaning 'happiness'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 542

vadhaiḥ — root han (to strike, go); ap in the instrumental sense by hanaś ca vadhaḥ (Pā. 3-3-76 [?]); vadha as substitute for the root; the word ends in a and has the final acute; ato lopaḥ (as read) elides the a for the suffix ap…

original p. 542

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.9, continued from p. 541

vadhaiḥ, concluded: the suffix ap being pit is unaccented, and with the unaccented suffix's acute vowel dropped, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161 [?]) gives the acute to the suffix. — duḥśaṃsān — root śaṃsu (praise); with the word duḥ as upapada (in the sense of 'with difficulty'), khal in the passive by īṣaddussuṣu (Pā. 3-3-126 [?]); stem duḥśaṃsa; liti (Pā. 6-1-193 [?]): the syllable before the suffix, being lit, takes the acute; accusative plural duḥśaṃsān; with āṭ-type vowel following, dīrghād aṭi samānapāde (as read) gives ru for the n, and āto 'ṭi nityam (as read) gives nasalization of the preceding ā. — jahi — root han (striking, going); loṭ, second person singular, sip → hi; hanter jaḥ (Pā. 6-4-36 [?]) gives ja; because of asiddhavad atrābhāt (Pā. 6-4-22 [?]) the substitute is treated as not effected, so the elision of hi by ato heḥ does not take place; nighāta accent (following a tiṅanta, the verb as read). — anti — the word antika, with loss of the final ka by kādilopo bahulam. — atriṇaḥ — root ad (eating); trin by ādeś ca ni ca (Uṇ. 4-[?] [?], as read "४-५३७" [?]); the i after n is read in the suffix to prevent loss of the n (it would be elided as final by halantyam [as read]), so the stem atrin; nominative plural atriṇaḥ; the i acute by the suffix accent. — gṛṇate — root gṝ here in the sense of praise; śatṛ in the present sense; śnā by kryādibhyaḥ śnā; sārvadhātukam apit makes the suffix ṅit-like; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112 [?]) elides the ā of śnā; gṛṇat; dative singular; with no num, the case-ending is acute by śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 [?]). — sugam — root gam (going), with su as upapada, ḍa in the locative-type sense by sudurorādhikaraṇe (Pā. 3-2-48 [?]); ḍit-ness elides the ṭi of the root; stem suga; suffix accent; accusative singular. — kṛdhi — root ḍukṛñ (making); loṭ second person singular, sip → hi; dhi by śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi (Pā. 6-4-102 [?]); the vikaraṇa elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; nighāta accent. ‖ 9 ‖ Grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numerals small and doubtful [?]. The grammar of Rik 94.9 ended on p. 542 with kṛdhi and its ‖ 9 ‖; on p. 543 only the closing words of the entry on sugam and the entry on kṛdhi remain, as above: after nighāta in the last line, the stem suga takes final acute by the suffix accent, and the accusative singular ending is the second-case singular form.

original p. 543

Rik 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.10)

यदयुक्था अरुषा रोहिता रथे वातजूता वृषभस्येव ते रवः । आदिन्वसि वनिनो धूमकेतुनाग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ १० ॥

yad ayukthā aruṣā rohitā rathe vātajūtā vṛṣabhasyeva te ravaḥ | ād invasi vanino dhūmaketunāgne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.10)

यत् । अयुक्थाः । अरुषा । रोहिता । रथे । वातऽजूता । वृषभस्यऽइव । ते । रवः । आत् । इन्वसि । वनिनः । धूमऽकेतुना । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ १० ॥

yat | ayukthāḥ | aruṣā | rohitā | rathe | vāta-jūtā | vṛṣabhasya-iva | te | ravaḥ | āt | invasi | vaninaḥ | dhūma-ketunā | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 10 ‖ Reading note: the Pada, as printed, has ād invasi as āt | invasi, and the Saṃhitā ayukthā for the Pada's ayukthāḥ by sandhi, and aruṣā rohitā as printed in the dual.

original p. 544

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.10)

हे अग्ने अरुषा आरोचमानौ रोहिता लोहितवर्णौ । रोहिते इत्यग्नेरश्वस्याख्या । रोहितोऽग्नेरिति दर्शनात् । रोहितेन त्वाग्निर्देवताां गमयेतु [?] । तै. सं. १-६-४-३ [?] इति मन्त्रवर्णात् । एते वै देवाश्वाः । तै. सं. १-६-४-३ [?] इति हि तत्र व्याख्यातं । वातजूता वातस्य वायोर्जूतं जवो वेग इव वेगो ययोस्तौ । ईदृशावश्वौ रथे यद्यदायुक्थाः अयोजयः तदानीं वनानि दहतस्ते तव रवः शब्दो वृषभस्येव दृप्तस्य महोक्षस्य शब्द इव गम्भीरो भवति । आदनन्तरं वनिनो वनसंबद्धान् वृक्षान् धूमकेतुना धूमः केतुः प्रज्ञापको यस्य तादृशेन रश्मिनेन्वसि [?] व्याप्नोषि । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ अयुक्थाः । युजिर् योगे । लुङि रुलो रुलीति सकारलोपः [?] । अरुषेत्यादिद्विवचनेषु सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । रवः । रु शब्दे । ऋदोरबिति भावेऽप् । इन्वसि । इवि व्याप्तौ । भ्वादिकः । इदित्त्वान्नुम् ॥

he agne aruṣā ārocamānau rohitā lohitavarṇau | rohite ity agner aśvasyākhyā | rohito 'gner iti darśanāt | rohitena tvāgnir devatāṃ gamayetu [?] | tai. saṃ. 1-6-4-3 [?] iti mantravarṇāt | ete vai devāśvāḥ | tai. saṃ. 1-6-4-3 [?] iti hi tatra vyākhyātaṃ | vātajūtā vātasya vāyor jūtaṃ javo vega iva vego yayos tau | īdṛśāv aśvau rathe yad yad āyukthāḥ ayojayaḥ tadānīṃ vanāni dahatas te tava ravaḥ śabdo vṛṣabhasyeva dṛptasya mahokṣasya śabda iva gambhīro bhavati | ād anantaraṃ vanino vanasaṃbaddhān vṛkṣān dhūmaketunā dhūmaḥ ketuḥ prajñāpako yasya tādṛśena raśminenvasi [?] vyāpnoṣi | anyat pūrvavat ‖ ayukthāḥ | yujir yoge | luṅi rulo rulīti sakāralopaḥ [?] | aruṣety ādidvivaceṣu supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | ravaḥ | ru śabde | ṛdor ap iti bhāve 'p | invasi | ivi vyāptau | bhvādikaḥ | idittvān num ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O Agni, the two shining (aruṣā), red (rohitā, 'red-coloured') [horses]. Rohitā is a name of the horses of Agni, as seen in the saying 'the rohita of Agni'; and in the mantra-wording 'Agni, with the rohita, may he bring you to the deity' (Taittirīya Saṃhitā, as read 1-6-4-3 [?]); 'these are the gods' horses' — so it is explained there. vātajūtā — those two whose speed (jūta) is like the speed (vega) of the wind. When you have yoked such a pair to your chariot, then, burning the forests, your roar is deep like the roar of a proud great bull. And after that, with a banner of smoke — that is, the smoke is the ketu (the sign) of him — you pervade the trees that belong to the forest. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: ayukthāḥ — yuj (joining) in the aorist, with elision of the s as printed [?]; aruṣā — the dual case-ending is replaced by ā by supāṃ suluk…; ravaḥ — root ru (sound), ap in the sense of the action by ṛdor ap; invasi — root ivi (pervading), class bhvādi, the i-marker gives num. The bhāṣya is clotted at the Taittirīya Saṃhitā quotation rohitena tvāgnir devatāṃ gamayetu and its two numerals; at raśminenvasi; and at the aorist elision clause; marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"agne — O Agni; aruṣā — shining; rohitā — golden-coloured; vātajūtā — wind-swift; (your) horses [Kannada: kuduregaḷu]; rathe — to the chariot; yat — when; ayukthāḥ — are yoked (then); te — (forest-burning) your; ravaḥ — sound; vṛṣabhasyeva — like the bellow of a bull (is deep); āt — after that; vaninaḥ — all the trees in the forest; dhūmaketunā — with the flame made known by a banner-like smoke; invasi — you envelop; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, as soon as you yoke to your chariot your shining, golden-hued, wind-swift horses, your roar, as you burn the forest, is deep like the bellow of a bull. After that you envelop all the trees in the forest with a flame that has the smoke for its banner. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

English Translation (as printed)

When you have yoked the bright red horses, swift as the wind to your car, your roar is like that of a bull, and you envelope [sic] the forest trees with a banner of smoke ; Agni, let us not suffer injury, through your friendship.

original p. 545

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.10 (Kannada)

aruṣā — "Although the word aruṣa has the ordinary sense 'reddish-brown', here, since the epithet rohitā is also present, it has been explained as 'shining' (prakāśamāna)."

rohitā — "rohito 'gneḥ (Ni. 2-28 [?], as read) — the Nirukta-author thus gives the form of Agni's horse: 'golden-coloured', that is the sense."

vātajūtā — vātasya vāyoḥ jūtaṃ javaḥ vega iva vego yayoḥ tau: "'Horses whose speed is like the speed of the wind'; here the word vātajūta is an epithet of Agni's horses. In some places it is also used as an epithet of Agni himself:" The print's word before tiṣṭhate is read atiseṣu as printed, and is the Kannada-script reading of atasesu; doubtful [?]. Gloss, editorial and tentative: "wind-driven, he stands apart among the bushes, with ladles, with the sickle, loud in sound".

वि वातजूतो अतसेषु तिष्ठते वृथा जुहूभिः सृण्या तुविष्वणिः । vi vātajūto atiseṣu tiṣṭhate vṛthā juhūbhiḥ sṛṇyā tuviṣvaṇiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-58-5 as read [?])

यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः । yad vātajūto vanā vy asthād agnir ha dāti romā pṛthivyāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-4 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "when, wind-driven, he spread through the forests, Agni shears the hair of the earth". "In places such as these, the word is an epithet of Agni, meaning 'Agni urged on by the wind (vātena preritaḥ)'."

vaninaḥ — vanasaṃbaddhān vṛkṣān: "the trees belonging to the forest."

invasi — "invati, nakṣati and so on, ten [words] being read among the roots that mean 'pervasion' (Ni. 2-10 [?]); so invasi means 'you pervade'."

dhūmaketunā — "They explain the word dhūmaketu in two ways. Ketuḥ patākākāraḥ; ketuḥ patākāsthānīyo yasya saḥ: 'ketu means a standard (dhvaja); one whose banner is the smoke' — thus Agni, in one way; or, ketuḥ jñānaṃ vā: 'ketu means knowledge' — 'one who is known by the smoke' (dhūmena yaḥ jñāyate sa iti vā) — in another way. The commentators explain it thus."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.10 grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 546

ayukthāḥ — root yujir (joining), luṅ second person singular, thās; cleḥ siṅ/sic in place of cli; jhalo jhali (Pā. 8-2-26 [?]) elides the s; co kuḥ (Pā. 8-2-30 [?]) turns j to g by kutva; khari ca (Pā. 8-4-55 [?]) turns g to k …

original p. 546

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.10, continued : ayukthāḥ — … g turns to k; because the word is connected with yad, the nighāta accent does not arise; since the augment aṭ is acute, the word has acute on its first syllable. — aruṣā — aruṣā, rohitā, vātajūtā: these dual forms with the dual ending following, the case-ending becomes ā by supāṃ suluk…. — ravaḥ — root ru (sound); ap in the sense of the action by ṛdor ap; guṇa of the root by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ and av-substitution; since ap is pit, it is unaccented and the root's accent remains. — invasi — root ivi (pervading), bhvādi class; num augment by idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-58 [?]); śap as vikaraṇa; laṭ second person singular sip; nighāta accent, since it follows a tiṅanta (the printed atijanta, as read). — vaninaḥ — "that which has a forest (vana)": the suffix ini in the sense of possession by ato 'ni ṭhanau (as read); stem vanin; accusative plural vaninaḥ; the i acute by the suffix accent. ‖ 10 ‖ Grammar page, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals are small and doubtful [?].

Rik 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.11)

अध स्वनादुत बिभ्युः पतत्रिणो द्रप्सा यत्ते यवसादो व्यस्थिरन् । सुगं तत्ते तावकेभ्यो रथेभ्योऽग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ ११ ॥

adha svanād uta bibhyuḥ patatriṇo drapsā yat te yavasādo vy asthiran | sugaṃ tat te tāvakebhyo rathebhyo 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 547

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.11)

अध । स्वनात् । उत । बिभ्युः । पतत्रिणः । द्रप्साः । यत् । ते । यवसऽअदः । वि । अस्थिरन् । सुऽगम् । तत् । ते । तावकेभ्यः । रथेभ्यः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ११ ॥

adha | svanāt | uta | bibhyuḥ | patatriṇaḥ | drapsāḥ | yat | te | yavasa-adaḥ | vi | asthiran | su-gam | tat | te | tāvakebhyaḥ | rathebhyaḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 11 ‖ Reading note: Saṃhitā adha and Pada adha, Saṃhitā bibhyuḥ and Pada bibhyuḥ; the Saṃhitā's compound yavasādo is divided in the Pada as yavasa-adaḥ.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.11)

हे अग्ने अध दग्धुं वनप्रवेशानन्तरं स्वनात्त्वदीयोत्पूर्वोत्कृष्टगम्भीरशब्दात् । उतशब्दोऽप्यर्थः । पतत्रिणः पक्षिणोऽपि बिभ्युः । बिभ्यति भयं प्राप्नुवन्ति । उत्पतनेन देशान्तरं गन्तुं समर्थाः पक्षिणोऽपि यदा भयं प्राप्नुवन्ति किमु वक्तव्यमन्येषां तत्रत्यानां वृकादीनां भीतिर्जायत इति । अतस्त्वयि वनं प्रविशति सर्वे प्राणिनो भयं प्राप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः । तादृशस्य ते तव द्रप्साः ज्वालैकदेशा यवसादो यवसानामत्तारः संकोचयद्यदा [?] व्यस्थिरन् विविधमवतिष्ठन्ते तत्तदा ते तव सर्वमरण्यं सुगं सुखेन गन्तुं शक्यं । अतस्तावकेभ्यस्त्वदीयेभ्यो रथेभ्यश्च तदरण्यं सुगं भवति । पूर्वं प्रवृत्तैर्ज्वालाग्रैस्तृणादिषु दग्धेषु सत्सु त्वदीया रथाः प्रतिबन्धमन्तरेण पश्चाद्गच्छन्तीति भावः । अन्यत्समानं ॥ बिभ्युः । ञिभी भये । छान्दसो लिट् । एरनेकाच इति यण् । व्यस्थिरन् । समवप्रविभ्यः स्थ इति तिष्ठतेरात्मनेपदं । लुङः व्यत्ययेन झस्य रन् । स्थाघ्वोरिच्चेतीत्त्वं । प्रस्पादङ्गात् [?] । पा. ८-३-१२ [?] इति सलोपः । तावकेभ्यः । तवकममकावेकवचने । पा. सू. ४-३-३ [?] इति युष्मदस्तवकादेशः ॥

he agne adha dagdhuṃ vanapraveśānantaraṃ svanāt tvadīyotpūrvotkṛṣṭagambhīraśabdāt | utaśabdo 'py arthaḥ | patatriṇaḥ pakṣiṇo 'pi bibhyuḥ | bibhyati bhayaṃ prāpnuvanti | utpatanena deśāntaraṃ gantuṃ samarthāḥ pakṣiṇo 'pi yadā bhayaṃ prāpnuvanti kimu vaktavyam anyeṣāṃ tatratyānāṃ vṛkādīnāṃ bhītir jāyata iti | atas tvayi vanaṃ praviśati sarve prāṇino bhayaṃ prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ | tādṛśasya te tava drapsāḥ jvālaikadeśā yavasādo yavasānām attāraḥ saṃkocayad yadā [?] vyasthiran vividham avatiṣṭhante tat tadā te tava sarvam araṇyaṃ sugaṃ sukhena gantuṃ śakyaṃ | atas tāvakebhyas tvadīyebhyo rathebhyaś ca tad araṇyaṃ sugaṃ bhavati | pūrvaṃ pravṛttair jvālāgrais tṛṇādiṣu dagdheṣu satsu tvadīyā rathāḥ pratibandham antareṇa paścād gacchantīti bhāvaḥ | anyat samānaṃ ‖ bibhyuḥ | ñibhī bhaye | chāndaso liṭ | eranekāca iti yaṇ | vyasthiran | samavaprabhyaḥ stha iti tiṣṭhater ātmanepadaṃ | luṅaḥ vyatyayena jhasya ran | sthāghvor ic ceti ittvaṃ | prasvādaṅgāt [?] | pā. 8-3-12 [?] iti salopaḥ | tāvakebhyaḥ | tavakamamakāv ekavacane | pā. sū. 4-3-3 [?] iti yuṣmadas tavakādeśaḥ ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O Agni, adha — after your entering the forest to burn it — svanāt, from your loud, deep roar (uta here has the sense 'even'): the winged ones (patatriṇaḥ), the birds also, are afraid. If even birds, able to go to another place by flying up, are afraid, what is to be said of the fear that arises in the other creatures there, the wolves and the like? So the sense is that when you enter the forest, all creatures fall into fear. When your sparks (drapsāḥ — portions of flame), the eaters of grass (yavasādaḥ), spread out in many ways, then for you the whole forest is easy to travel (sugam): so that forest becomes easy for your chariots also. The sense is that when the grass and the like have been burned by the flame-tips that spread first, your chariots follow after without obstruction. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: bibhyuḥ — ñibhī (fear), the Vedic perfect, with y for the vowel by eranekāca…; vyasthiran — the ātmanepada of sthā after sam, ava, pra, vi by the rule on sthā; ran in place of jhi by the transposition of terms in the luṅ; i for the root vowel by sthāghvor ic ca; elision of s [clotted, the rule's wording and number doubtful [?]]; tāvakebhyaḥ — tavaka as substitute for yuṣmad in the singular (the rule number doubtful [?]). The bhāṣya is clotted at saṃkocayad yadā and at prasvādaṅgāt; marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 547; continues on p. 548

"agne — O Agni; atha — after you have entered the forest; svanāt — (by your) sound; patatriṇaḥ uta — even the birds; bibhyuḥ — are afraid; te — your; drapsāḥ — the parts of flame; yavasādaḥ — burning up all the grass; yat — when; vyasthiran — they spread in all directions; tat — then; te — to you; sugaṃ — (all the forest) it becomes possible to enter easily; tāvakebhyaḥ — your; rathebhyaḥ — for the chariots also (it is possible to enter easily…"

original p. 548

Pratipadārtha of Rik 94.11, concluded from p. 547: "…(it is possible to enter easily) — it becomes [so]; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer (any) harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, as soon as you have entered the forest, even the birds are afraid at your roar. When the portions of your flame, burning up all the grass, spread in all directions, the entry of the forest becomes very easy for you and for your chariots. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

English Translation (as printed)

At your roaring even the birds are terrified ; when your flames, consuming the grass, have spread in all directions, (the wood) is easy of access to you and to your chariots ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.11 (Kannada)

drapsāḥ — "The word drapsa ordinarily means 'that which flows' (dravaṇa-śīla), that is, 'what is to be run, flowing', or it has been used in the sense 'the drops of Soma-juice, like water-drops'. But in some contexts it means 'a ray of Agni', 'a banner', 'the moon'. For the word drapsāḥ in this Ṛk they explain jvālaikadeśāḥ, 'portions of the flame'. Skandasvāmin takes it as drapsaśabdaḥ kaṭhinavacanaḥ kaṭhināḥ bahularūpāḥ [as read, doubtful [?]]: 'the word drapsa gives the meaning "hard"', and says it is to be understood here as the hard and abundant flame of Agni."

vyasthiran — tiṣṭheḥ idaṃ rūpaṃ | vitiṣṭhante | sarvaṃ vyāpnuvantīty arthaḥ: "'this is a form of sthā: they stand in various ways, they pervade everything' — that is the sense: 'occupy all', or 'pervade'. The flame of Agni pervades everything and spreads."

sugaṃ — "The various senses of this word have been given already, in explaining the 9th Ṛk of this very Sūkta."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.11 grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 549

adha — in the word atha the tha becomes dha by Vedic variation. — bibhyuḥ — root ñibhī (fear); in the present sense, liṭ by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; reduplication of the root; the reduplicate takes jaś (the bh → b); third person plural jhi → us; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit… continues on p. 549

original p. 549

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.11, continued : bibhyuḥ — … by asaṃyogāl liṭ kit (Pā. 1-2-5 [?]) it is kit, so the root takes no guṇa; eranekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya (Pā. 6-4-82 [?]) turns the i to y; nighāta accent, following a tiṅanta. — vyasthiran — root ṣṭhā (cessation of motion), usually parasmaipada, but by samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ (Pā. 1-3-22 [?]) it takes the ātmanepada; luṅ, third person plural, jha; by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 [?]) ran replaces jha; sthāghvor ic ca (Pā. 1-2-17 [?]) gives i for the root's vowel in luṅ; then, the sic following a short vowel being elided by hrasvād aṅgāt (Pā. 8-2-27 [?]) — the print's clotted prasvādaṅgāt of the bhāṣya (p. 547) is to be read hrasvād aṅgāt, with the number as read here, not the 8-3-12 of the bhāṣya's tail [?]; the augment aṭ for the stem. Because the word yat stands before it, the nighāta accent is blocked by yadvṛttān nityam (as read); as the augment aṭ is acute, the first syllable is acute. — tāvakebhyaḥ — "these (are) yours": tava ime tāvakāḥ, in the sense of relationship; by yuṣmadasmador anyatarasyāṃ khañ ca (as read) the suffix aṇ follows; with that suffix following, tavakamamakāv ekavacane (Pā. 4-3-3 [?]) gives tavaka for yuṣmad; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ gives vṛddhi of the first vowel; the suffix accent falls on the last syllable; the form is the dative plural. ‖ 11 ‖

Rik 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.12)

अयं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धायसेऽवयातां मरुतां हेळो अद्भुतः । मृळा सु नो भूत्वेषां मनः पुनरग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ १२ ॥

ayaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya dhāyase 'vayātāṃ marutāṃ heḷo adbhutaḥ | mṛḷā su no bhūtv eṣāṃ manaḥ punar agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 12 ‖

original p. 550

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.12)

अयम् । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धायसे । अवऽयाताम् । मरुताम् । हेळः । अद्भुतः । मृळ । सु । नः । भूतु । एषाम् । मनः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ १२ ॥

ayam | mitrasya | varuṇasya | dhāyase | ava-yātām | marutām | heḷaḥ | adbhutaḥ | mṛḷa | su | naḥ | bhūtu | eṣām | manaḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 12 ‖ Reading note: the Pada line as printed, checked on an enlargement, has no punaḥ between manaḥ and agne, although the Saṃhitā has punar agne; the omission is the print's. The Saṃhitā's mṛḷā is the Pada's mṛḷa, and bhūtv eṣām is bhūtu | eṣām.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.12)

अयमग्नेः स्तोता मित्रस्याहरभिमानिनो देवस्य वरुणस्य रात्र्यभिमानिनश्च संबन्धिने धायसे धारणायोवस्थापनाय [?] भवतु । मित्रावरुणाविममग्नेः स्तोतारं धारयितामित्यर्थः । अवयातामवस्ताद् गच्छतां स्वर्गलोकस्याधस्तादन्तरिक्षे वर्तमानानां मरुतामेतन्नामकानां देवानां हेळः क्रोधो ऽद्भुतो महान् भवति । अद्भुत इत्येतन्महन्नाम । तस्मात्क्रोधादिममग्नेः स्तोतारं मित्रावरुणौ रक्षतामिति शेषः । असि च नोऽस्मान् हे अग्ने सु मृळ सुष्ठु मृडय । सुखय । एषां मरुतां मनश्च पुनर्भूतु । पुनरपि प्रसन्नं भवतु । अन्यत्समानं ॥ धायसे । वहिहाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसीति भावेऽसुन् । णिदित्यनुवृत्तेरातो युक् चिण्कृतोरिति युक् । अवयातां । या प्रापणे । अस्मादेवपूर्वाल्लटः शतृ । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । मृळ । मृड सुखने । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाज्ञेरनिटीति णिलोपः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । भूतु । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् ॥

ayam agneḥ stotā mitrasyāhar-abhimāninā devasya varuṇasya rātry-abhimāninaś ca saṃbandhine dhāyase dhāraṇāyovasthāpanāya [?] bhavatu | mitrāvaruṇāv imam agneḥ stotāraṃ dhārayitām ity arthaḥ | avayātām avastād gacchatāṃ svargalokasyādhastād antarikṣe vartamānānāṃ marutām etannāmakānāṃ devānāṃ heḷaḥ krodho 'dbhuto mahān bhavati | adbhuta ity etan mahannāma | tasmāt krodhād imam agneḥ stotāraṃ mitrāvaruṇau rakṣatām iti śeṣaḥ | asi ca no 'smān he agne su mṛḷa suṣṭhu mṛḍaya | sukhaya | eṣāṃ marutāṃ manaś ca punar bhūtu | punar api prasannaṃ bhavatu | anyat samānaṃ ‖ dhāyase | vahihādhāṅbhyaś chandasīti bhāve 'sun | ṇid ity anuvṛtter āto yuk ciṇkṛtor iti yuk | avayātāṃ | yā prāpaṇe | asmād eva pūrvāl laṭaḥ śatṛ | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | mṛḷa | mṛḍa sukhane | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāj ñer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | dvyaco 'tas tiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | bhūtu | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk ‖ The print's asi ca no 'smān is read as printed, where the sense requires kṛdhi or the like — it is presumably a misprint for asmān alone; also the opening clause asi ca nosmān [?]. The sūtras are named without numbers in this tail; none supplied.

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "May this praiser of Agni be [fit] for the support (dhāyase) belonging to Mitra, the god who presides over the day, and Varuṇa, who presides over the night: that is, may Mitra and Varuṇa sustain this praiser of Agni. The anger (heḷaḥ) of the Maruts, the gods so named, who dwell in the atmosphere below the world of heaven (avayātām — 'those who go below'), is adbhuta, great; (adbhuta is a word for 'great'); from that anger may Mitra and Varuṇa protect this praiser of Agni, so the sentence is completed. And, O Agni, su mṛḷa, make us well content; and let the mind of these Maruts be again [kindly], let it become gracious once more. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: dhāyase — the suffix asun in the sense of the action after the roots vah, hā, dhā and the like in the Veda, with the augment yuk; avayātām — yā (reaching), śatṛ in the present of that root with the prefix ava, with the case-ending acute by the rule on śatṛ; mṛḷa — mṛḍa (pleasing); śap taken as ārdhadhātuka, with ṇi-elision; lengthening in the Saṃhitā (mṛḷā); bhūtu — elision of śap by bahulaṃ chandasi. The bhāṣya is clotted at dhāraṇāyovasthāpanāya; marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 550; continues on p. 551

"ayaṃ — this sacrificer (who praises Agni); mitrasya — of Mitra (who presides over the day); varuṇasya — and of Varuṇa (who presides over the night); dhāyase — to obtain support (the Kannada word, as read, doubtful [?]) (fit); avayātāṃ — those who move below (in the lower region of the world of heaven); marutāṃ — of the Maruts; heḷaḥ — anger; adbhutaḥ — is great (may this sacrificer who praises Agni be protected by Mitra and Varuṇa from this anger); agne — O Agni; naḥ — us; sumṛḷa — make well content; eṣāṃ — of these Maruts; manaḥ — the mind; punaḥ — …"

original p. 551

Pratipadārtha of Rik 94.12, concluded from p. 550: "…punaḥ — again; bhūtu — (graciously) let it be; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer (any) harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"May this sacrificer who praises Agni be fit to obtain the support of Mitra and Varuṇa, and receive their protection. The anger of the Maruts, who move in the lower part of the world of heaven, is terrifying. May Mitra and Varuṇa protect the sacrificer from this anger. O Agni, make us thoroughly content; may the mind of these Maruts be gracious once more. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

English Translation (as printed)

May this (your adorer) enjoy the support of Mitra aud [sic] of Varuna ; wonderful is the fury of the Maruts ; (dwellers in the region) below (the heavens) encourage us ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.12 (Kannada)

dhāyase — "This word may be derived from the root dhā, which gives the sense 'hold, support' (dhāraṇa), or from the root dheṭ 'to drink' (dheṭ pāne, as read), which gives the sense 'drinking'. dhāyase here means either 'for the support of the sacrificers, by protection and so on' or 'for the drinking of the Soma-juice'. In other places also both senses are used. In places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?] [numerals illegible] they explain poṣaṇāya ('for nourishment') and jagataḥ dhāraṇāya ('for the support of the world'); in 1-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]-[?] [numerals illegible], somapānāya ('for the drinking of Soma'). So here also either of the two senses may be taken. Sāyaṇa explains dhāraṇāya, avasthāpanāya bhavatu ('may it be for support, for establishment'), and Skandasvāmin explains somapānāya."

"Skandasvāmin, to explain the setting of this Ṛk, cites a story. It is this:" continues on p. 552 Gloss, editorial and tentative, from the Kannada that follows: "Mitra, Varuṇa and the Maruts came to Kutsa's sacrifice; he, his mind absorbed in praising Agni, did not praise them [?]; the angry gods went away from the sacrifice; [for that reason] Kutsa spoke to Agni." Several words of the print are doubtful [?].

मित्रो वरुणो मरुतश्च कुत्सस्य यज्ञमाजग्मुः । सोऽग्निस्तुत्या क्षिप्तमनाः तान्न तुष्टाव [?] । तस्मै क्रुद्धा यज्ञाद्देवा जग्मुः । तत्प्रसक्तये [?] कुत्सोऽग्निमुवाच । mitro varuṇo marutaś ca kutsasya yajñam ājagmuḥ | so 'gnistutyā kṣiptamanāḥ tān na tuṣṭāva [?] | tasmai kruddhā yajñād devā jagmuḥ | tatprasaktaye [?] kutso 'gnim uvāca |

original p. 552

"Once Mitra, Varuṇa and the Maruts together came to Kutsa's sacrificial house; Kutsa, wholly absorbed in the praise of Agni, did not notice them, and they went away angry. Then he, in this Ṛk, prays to Agni. Its meaning is that the anger of the gods who departed in wrath is very strong, and that Agni should pacify them and bring them back for the drinking of Soma."

avayātām — apagacchatām: "those who go away, departing in anger."

heḷaḥ — krodhaḥ: "reḷate, heḷate, bhāmate and others are read among the ten roots in the sense of 'become angry' (Ni. 2-6 [?], as read), so the word means 'anger'. The word is used in the sense of anger in many Ṛks: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-1 [numerals illegible] and others."

sumṛḷa — "make us thoroughly content."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.12

dhāyase — root dhāñ (holding, nourishing); the suffix asun in the sense of the action by vahihāhādhāñbhyaś chandasi (Uṇ. 4-[?] [?], numeral as read doubtful); ṇit by vaser ṇit (Uṇ. [?]) carried forward, so that yuk is added to the root by āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (Pā. 7-3-33 [?]); the stem dhāyas, a word ending in a consonant; dative singular; the suffix being ṇit, the first syllable is acute by ñnityādir nityam. — avayātām — root yā (reaching), adādi class; the prefix ava before it; śatṛ in the present sense; avayāt; genitive plural; for the num-less śatṛ the case-ending takes the acute by śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 [?]). — mṛḷa — root mṛḍa (pleasing); ṇic by hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 [?]) since the causer's action is shown; after the ṇijanta, loṭ second person singular sip; hi by serhy apicca (Pā. 3-4-87 [?]); śap as vikaraṇa; by chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 [?]) śap is treated as ārdhadhātuka, so by ṇer aniṭi (Pā. 6-4-51 [?]) the ṇi is elided; ato heḥ (Pā. 6-4-105 [?]) elides hi; in the Saṃhitā the vowel is lengthened by dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ (Pā. 6-3-135 [?]), the word remaining of two syllables. — bhūtu — root bhū (being); loṭ third person singular; u for the ending by eruḥ (Pā. 3-4-86 [?]); śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; guṇa blocked by bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88 [?]); form bhūtu. ‖ 12 ‖

original p. 553

devo devānām asi mitro adbhuto vasur vasūnām asi cārur adhvare | śarman syāma tava saprathastame 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.13)

हे अग्ने देवो द्योतमानस्त्वं देवानां सर्वेषामद्भुतो महान् मित्रोऽसि प्रौढः [?] सखा भवसि । तथा चारुः शोभनस्त्वमध्वरे यज्ञे वसूनां सर्वेषां धनानां वसुः निवासयिता भवसि । अतोऽस्माकं वसूनि देहीत्यर्थः । किंच सप्रथस्तमे सर्वतः पृथुतमे अतिशयेन विस्तीर्णे तव त्वत्संबन्धिनि शर्मणि यज्ञगृहे स्याम । वर्तमाना भवेम । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ शर्मन् । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् ॥

he agne devo dyotamānas tvaṃ devānāṃ sarveṣām adbhuto mahān mitro 'si prauḍhaḥ [?] sakhā bhavasi | tathā cāruḥ śobhanas tvam adhvare yajñe vasūnāṃ sarveṣāṃ dhanānāṃ vasuḥ nivāsayitā bhavasi | ato 'smākaṃ vasūni dehīty arthaḥ | kiṃca saprathastame sarvataḥ pṛthutame atiśayena vistīrṇe tava tvatsaṃbandhini śarmaṇi yajñagṛhe syāma | vartamānā bhavema | anyat pūrvavat ‖ śarman | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā luk ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O Agni, you, the shining god, are to all the gods a wonderful, great Mitra, a friend [the print's word before* sakhā read as prauḍhaḥ*, doubtful [?]]. And you, the lovely one, are in the sacrifice the vasu — the establisher — of all the treasures (vasūnām): so give us treasures, is the sense. And may we be in your śarman — your sacrificial house, which is the widest and most extensive on every side. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: śarman — the locative ending is elided by supāṃ suluk.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 553; continues on p. 554

"agne — O Agni; devaḥ — you, shining; devānāṃ — to (all) the gods; adbhutaḥ — of great majesty; mitraḥ asi — you are a friend; cāruḥ — lovely…"

original p. 554

Pratipadārtha of Rik 94.13, concluded from p. 553: "…cāruḥ — you of lovely form; adhvare — in the sacrifice; vasūnāṃ — of (all) treasures; vasuḥ asi — you are the establisher; saprathastame — most extensively spread; tava — your; śarman — in the sacrificial house; syāma — may (we) be; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, you, the shining one, are the great friend of all the gods. You, of lovely form, are in the sacrifice the establisher of all treasures. In your sacrificial house, which is spread most widely, may we be free from care; and through friendship with you may we suffer no harm of any kind: favour us thus."

English Translation (as printed)

You brilliant (Agni) are the especial friend of the gods ; you who are graceful in the sacrifice are the confirmer of all riches may we be present in your most spacious chamber of sacrfice [sic]; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.13 (Kannada)

devānām adbhutaḥ mitraḥ asi — "'You are the great friend of all gods': this shows the relationship of Agni with the other gods. Because Agni, by distributing the oblations through the sacrifice to all the gods who long for oblations, is the friend of all of them, and above all the friend who stands in front [the print's last words read as given, doubtful [?]]." Gloss, editorial and tentative: "in you, Agni, all the immortals, free from guile, the gods, eat with the mouth the oblation that has been offered". Gloss, editorial and tentative: "you, Agni, the immortal messenger, bearer of oblations, protector, to be praised, they have set down, age after age; gods and mortals with homage sat down by you, the watchful, the all-pervading, the lord of the clans".

त्वे अग्ने विश्वे अमृतासो अद्रुह आसा देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम् । tve agne viśve amṛtāso adruha āsā devā havir adanty āhutam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-14 as read [?])

त्वां दूतमग्ने अमृतं युगेयुगे हव्यवाहं दधिरे पायुमीड्यम् । देवासश्च मर्त्यासश्च जागृविं विभुं विश्पतिं नमसा नि षेदिरे ॥ tvāṃ dūtam agne amṛtaṃ yuge-yuge havyavāhaṃ dadhire pāyum īḍyam | devāsaś ca martyāsaś ca jāgṛviṃ vibhuṃ viśpatiṃ namasā ni ṣedire ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-8 as read [?])

"In many such contexts, which show the close relationship between Agni and the gods, and that the satisfaction of all the gods is effected through Agni alone, Agni is said to be the friend of all."

original p. 555

vasūnāṃ vasuḥ asi — "'You are the establisher of all treasures.' In mantras such as —"

वसुर्वसूनां क्षयसि त्वमेक इद्यावा च यानि पृथिवी च पुष्यतः । vasur vasūnāṃ kṣayasi tvam eka id dyāvā ca yāni pṛthivī ca puṣyataḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-91-3 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "you alone, the Vasu of the Vasus, rule over those treasures which heaven and earth nourish". "— Agni is praised as the sole lord of every kind of wealth needed for the protection of the heavenly world and the growth of the earth; therefore he is said to be vasūnāṃ vasuḥ asi."

saprathastame — sarvataḥ pṛthutamaḥ: "'extremely extended on all sides', the sense is 'most spread out'. The word in this sense is used in many contexts, such as 3-6-3 [?] and others."

śarman — "'In the sacrificial house.' Since it is read among the twenty-two names of 'house' — gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ, garttaḥ and the rest (Ni. 3-[?] [?]) — the sense here is 'house'. In many contexts the word śarman also has the senses 'protection' and 'refuge'. The Nirukta-author, with the sense of 'refuge, protection', cites the Ṛk —"

यच्छा नः शर्म सप्रथः । yacchā naḥ śarma saprathaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-15 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "grant us a wide refuge". "— and explains the word śarma as śaraṇam, 'refuge'. Thus this word is used abundantly in both senses. Here it means 'in the exceedingly spacious house'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.13 grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 556

asi — root as (being), laṭ second person singular sip following; tāsasty or lopaḥ elides the s of the root; nighāta accent, since it follows a tiṅanta (the print's atijanta). — śarman — a stem in n; the seventh-case ending ṅi following, supāṃ suluk elides it. — syāma — root as (being), adādi; vidhiliṅ, first person plural mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ (Pā. 3-4-99 [?]) elides the s of mas; yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca (Pā. 3-4-103 [?]) gives the augment yāsuṭ; since ṅit-ness is prescribed for it, continues on p. 556

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.13, concluded : syāma — … śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-111 [?]) elides the a of the root; nighāta accent, since it follows a tiṅanta. ‖ 13 ‖ Grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?].

तत्ते भद्रं यत्समिद्धः स्वे दमे सोमाहुतो जरसे मृळयत्तमः । दधासि रत्नं द्रविणं च दाशुषेऽग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ १४ ॥

tat te bhadraṃ yat samiddhaḥ sve dame somāhuto jarase mṛḷayattamaḥ | dadhāsi ratnaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dāśuṣe 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 14 ‖

tat | te | bhadram | yat | sam-iddhaḥ | sve | dame | soma-āhutaḥ | jarase | mṛḷayat-tamaḥ | dadhāsi | ratnam | draviṇam | ca | dāśuṣe | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 14 ‖

हे अग्ने ते त्वत्संबन्धि तत् खलु [?] भद्रं भजनीयं । प्रशस्तमित्यर्थः । किं पुनस्तत् [?] । स्वे दमे स्वकीये उत्तरवेदिलक्षणे निवासस्थाने । तस्यैष स्वो लोको…

he agne te tvatsaṃbandhi tat khalu [?] bhadraṃ bhajanīyaṃ | praśastam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ punas tat [?] | sve dame svakīye uttaravedilakṣaṇe nivāsasthāne | tasyaiṣa svo loko… The line break of the print at "kiṃ puna-" reads "-sthat" [?]; the words yat samiddhaḥ of the Rik are not repeated in the bhāṣya as read; the text continues on p. 557.

original p. 557

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 94.14, continued from p. 556

…यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः । ऐ. ब्रा. १-२९ [?] । इति श्रुतेः । तस्यामुत्तरवेद्यां समिद्धः सम्यग्दीप्तः प्रज्वलितः सोमाहुतो हुतेन सोमरसेन संतर्पितः सन् जरसे । ऋत्विग्भिः स्तूयस इति यदस्ति तद्भद्रमित्यर्थः । एवं प्रशस्तस्त्वं मृळयत्तमोऽतिशयेनास्माकं सुखयिता भूत्वा रत्नं रमणीयं कर्मफलं द्रविणं धनं च दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय दधासि । प्रयच्छसि । अन्यत्समानं ॥ समिद्धः । इन्धी दीप्तौ । कर्मणि निष्ठा । श्वीदितो निष्ठायामिति इट्प्रतिषेधः । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सोमाहुतः । सोमेनाहुतः । तृतीया कर्मणेति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । जरसे । जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा । व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । दधासि । अनुदात्ते चेत्यभ्यस्तस्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

…yad uttaravedī nābhiḥ | ai. brā. 1-29 [?] | iti śruteḥ | tasyām uttaravedyāṃ samiddhaḥ samyagdīptaḥ prajvalitaḥ somāhuto hutena somarasena saṃtarpitaḥ san jarase | ṛtvigbhiḥ stūyasa iti yad asti tad bhadram ity arthaḥ | evaṃ praśastas tvaṃ mṛḷayattamo 'tiśayenāsmākaṃ sukhayitā bhūtvā ratnaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ karmaphalaṃ draviṇaṃ dhanaṃ ca dāśuṣe havirdattavate yajamānāya dadhāsi | prayacchasi | anyat samānaṃ ‖ samiddhaḥ | indhī dīptau | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | śvīdito niṣṭhāyām iti iṭpratiṣedhaḥ | gatir anantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | somāhutaḥ | somenāhutaḥ | tṛtīyā karmaṇeti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | jarase | jaratiḥ stutikarmā | vyatyayena karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | dadhāsi | anudātte cety abhyastasyādyudāttatvaṃ ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "…'the Uttaravedī is the navel' (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, as read 1-29 [?]) — so says the scripture. On that Uttaravedī, kindled, fully blazing, and gratified by the Soma-juice that has been offered, you are praised (jarase) by the priests: whatever there is that is so, is bhadra, to be sought, praiseworthy. Thus praised, being most gladdening, a giver of ease to us, you bestow the delightful fruit of rites (ratna) and wealth (draviṇa) on the worshipper who has given the oblation. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: samiddhaḥ — indhī (shining), past participle in the passive; the iṭ augment forbidden by śvīdito niṣṭhāyām; the gati (sam) retains its natural accent by gatir anantaraḥ; somāhutaḥ — 'offered by Soma', the instrumental determinative, first-member accent by tṛtīyā karmaṇi; jarase — jarati is a verb of praise; the agent suffix in the passive by vyatyaya; no nighāta because of the connexion with yat; dadhāsi — the reduplicate takes the initial acute by anudātte ca.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"agne — O Agni; sve dame — (ordained by the śāstra) in your dwelling-place; samiddhaḥ — well blazing, kindled (and); somāhutaḥ — one to whom the Soma-juice has been offered; jarase — (by the priests) praised; te — your; tat — that kindling and the hymn also; bhadraṃ — (for you) productive of a lovely satisfaction (you, who have obtained such satisfaction); mṛḷayattamaḥ — (us) greatly gladdening; ratnaṃ — the delightful fruit of rites; draviṇaṃ ca — and wealth too; dāśuṣe — to the sacrificer who has offered oblations; dadhāsi — you give; tava — your; sakhye — through friendship; vayaṃ — we; mā riṣāma — may we not suffer harm."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, in your dwelling-place ordained by the śāstra you are well kindled, and after the offering of the Soma-juice you are praised by the priests: that kindling of yours and the hymn are a lovely satisfaction to you. Having obtained such satisfaction, you greatly gladden us, and give the delightful fruit of rites and wealth to the sacrificer who has offered oblations. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

English Translation (as printed)

It is pleasant to you when you are lighted in your own abode and propitiated by libations are praised (by the priests) ; then, much delighted, you give rewards and riches to the worshipper ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

original p. 558

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.14 (Kannada)

sve dame — "gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ, garttaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-two names of 'house' (Ni. 3-13 [?], as read), so dame means 'in the house'. Here sve dame means 'in the dwelling-place, ordained by the śāstra, of Agni'. As described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —"

तस्यैष स्वो लोको यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः । tasyaiṣa svo loko yad uttaravedī nābhiḥ | (Ai. Brā. 1-29 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "this is his own world, the Uttaravedī, the navel". "— the abode in the form of the Uttaravedī is well known as Agni's own house, or the world of heaven."

jarase — "jaratiḥ stutikarmā: since jarati is a verb of praise, jarase means 'to praise the gods', or 'for you to be praised by the priests'."

ratnaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dāśuṣe dadhāsi — "'You give all kinds of wealth to the sacrificer who offers oblations' — so it is said. By vasūnāṃ vasuḥ ['the Vasu of the Vasus'] Agni is said to be both the field of all prosperity and its lord, and in —"

विश्वं सो अग्ने जयति त्वया धनं यस्ते ददाश मर्त्यः । viśvaṃ so agne jayati tvayā dhanaṃ yas te dadāśa martyaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-4 as read [?])

पीपाय स श्रवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्थैः । pīpāya sa śravasā martyeṣu yo agnaye dadāśa vipra ukthaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-[?] [?], numeral read from small figures)

यो अग्निं तन्वो दमे देवं मर्तः सपर्यति । तस्मा इद्दीदयद्वसु ॥ yo agniṃ tanvo dame devaṃ martaḥ saparyati | tasmā id dīdayad vasu ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?] [?], numeral read from small figures)

Glosses, editorial and tentative: "he wins all wealth through you, Agni, the mortal who has given to you"; "he grew in fame among mortals who with hymns, as sage, gave to Agni"; "the mortal who serves the god Agni in his own house — to him he shines forth wealth". "In many such contexts it is described that the sacrificer who offers oblations in the way the śāstra directs obtains every kind of wealth from Agni."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.14 grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 559

samiddhaḥ — root ñi indhī (shining); kta in the passive; since the root is ī-marked, the iṭ augment is not added, by śvīdito niṣṭhāyām (Pā. 7-2-14 [?]); the suffix being kit, the n of the root's penultimate is elided by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-24 [?]); by jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. 8-2-40 [?]) the t of the suffix becomes dh, and by jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi (Pā. 8-4-53 [?]) the preceding dh becomes d; the gati (sam) keeps its natural accent by gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 [?]). — somāhutaḥ — somena āhutaḥ, a third-case tatpuruṣa; the first member keeps its natural accent by tṛtīyā karmaṇi (Pā. 6-2-48 [?]). continues on p. 559

original p. 559

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.14, continued : jarase — root jyaṣ (loss of vigour); since roots have several senses, it is used here in the sense of praise; by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 [?]) the agent suffix occurs in the passive; laṭ second person singular thās, se for thās by thāsaḥ se (Pā. 3-4-80 [?]); śap as vikaraṇa; guṇa of the root's i by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; the form jarase; though yat is separated from it, yadvṛttān nityam (Pā. 8-1-66 [?]) prevents the nighāta, so the root's accent remains. — dadhāsi — root ḍudhāñ (holding, nourishing), juhotyādi; laṭ second person singular sip; ślu by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ (Pā. 2-4-75 [?]); reduplication by ślau (Pā. 6-1-10 [?]); the reduplicate shortened; initial acute of the reduplicate by anudātte ca (Pā. 6-1-190 [?]). — dāśuṣe — root dāśṛ (giving); kvasu in the form dāśvān, irregular (dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca, Pā. 6-1-12 [?]); with the dative ending following, the stem has the bha-designation, so vasoḥ samprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131 [?]) turns the v of vas into u; samprasāraṇāc ca (Pā. 6-1-108 [?]) gives the earlier form; ṣ by śāsi vasi ghasīnāṃ ca (Pā. 8-3-60 [?]); the form dāśuṣe. ‖ 14 ‖

yasmai tvaṃ sudraviṇo dadāśo 'nāgāstvam adite sarvatātā | yaṃ bhadreṇa śavasā codayāsi prajāvatā rādhasā te syāma ‖ 15 ‖ Reading note: the last line is printed …prajāvatā rādha- | sā te syāma, the word broken at the line end; read as rādhasā te syāma, to be checked against the Pada on the next page [?]. yasmai | tvam | su-draviṇaḥ | dadāśaḥ | anāgāḥ-tvam | adite | sarva-tātā | yam | bhadreṇa | śavasā | codayāsi | prajā-vatā | rādhasā | te | syāma ‖ 15 ‖ The Pada, as printed, divides the last line rādhasā | te | syāma, which settles the reading of the Saṃhitā's last line on p. 559: rādhasā te syāma; the print's Pada carries no verse numeral at the end of the page's lines.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.15)

हे सुद्रविणः शोभनधनादितेऽखण्डनीयाग्ने सर्वताता सर्वासु कर्मतितिषु [?] । यद्वा सर्वेषु यज्ञीयेषु वर्तमानाय यस्मै यजमानायानागास्त्वमपापत्वं पापराहित्येन कर्मार्हतां त्वं ददाशः प्रयच्छसि स यजमानः समृद्धो भवति । यं च यजमानं भद्रेण भजनीयेन कल्याणेन शवसा बलेन चोदयासि संयोजयसि सोऽपि समृद्धो भवति । वयं च स्तोतारः प्रजावता प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रैर्युक्तेन ते राधसा त्वया दत्तेन धनेन युक्ताः स्याम । भवेम ॥ सुद्रविणः । शोभनानि द्रविणानि धनानि यस्य । द्रु गतौ । द्रुदक्षिभ्यामिनन् । उ. २-५० [?] । द्रविणशब्दस्यान्ते मकारोपजनश्छन्दसः [?] । ददाशः । दाश्र दाने । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं । सर्वताता । सर्वदेवात्तातिल् इति स्वार्थे तातिल्प्रत्ययः । यास्कपक्षे तु सर्वाः स्तुतयो येषु यागेष्विति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । वर्णव्यापत्त्यात्वं [?] । उभयत्रापि सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या डादेशः । चोदयासि । चुद प्रेरणे । लेट्याडागमः ॥

he sudraviṇaḥ śobhanadhanādite 'khaṇḍanīyāgne sarvatātā sarvāsu karmatatiṣu [?] | yadvā sarveṣu yajñīyeṣu vartamānāya yasmai yajamānāyānāgāstvam apāpatvaṃ pāparāhityena karmārhatāṃ tvaṃ dadāśaḥ prayacchasi sa yajamānaḥ samṛddho bhavati | yaṃ ca yajamānaṃ bhadreṇa bhajanīyena kalyāṇena śavasā balena codayāsi saṃyojayasi so 'pi samṛddho bhavati | vayaṃ ca stotāraḥ prajāvatā prajābhiḥ putrapautrair yuktena te rādhasā tvayā dattena dhanena yuktāḥ syāma | bhavema ‖ sudraviṇaḥ | śobhanāni draviṇāni dhanāni yasya | dru gatau | drudakṣibhyām inan | u. 2-50 [?] | draviṇaśabdasyānte makāropajanaś chandasaḥ [?] | dadāśaḥ | dāśṛ dāne | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvaṃ | sarvatātā | sarvadevāt tātil iti svārthe tātilpratyayaḥ | yāskapakṣe tu sarvāḥ stutayo yeṣu yāgeṣv iti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | varṇavyāpattyātvaṃ [?] | ubhayatrāpi supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā ḍādeśaḥ | codayāsi | cuda preraṇe | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O Agni, you of lovely wealth (sudraviṇaḥ), indivisible, in all the multitudes of rites [karmatatiṣu, the print's word read from p. 562]. Or: to the sacrificer who abides in all the sacrificial acts, you give anāgāstva — freedom from sin, the fitness for rites that comes of sinlessness — and that sacrificer prospers; and whichever sacrificer you rouse with good, desirable strength, he too prospers; and may we, the praisers, be endowed with wealth given by you, accompanied by progeny, sons and grandsons." Grammatical tail: sudraviṇaḥ — from dru (going) with inan (drudakṣibhyām inan, Uṇ. 2-50 [?]); the added m at the end of draviṇa is the Vedic usage [as read, doubtful [?]]; dadāśaḥ — dāśṛ (giving), a leṭ form with the augment aṭ, śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi, initial acute by abhyastānām ādiḥ; sarvatātā — by sarvadevāt tātil the suffix tātil in the same sense; on Yāska's view, a bahuvrīhi 'in which all the praises are', with the first member's natural accent; the ā-ending as the replacement of the locative by supāṃ suluk…; codayāsi — cud (urging), the leṭ augment aṭ. The print's karmatatiṣu on p. 560 is a clotted karmateti-; the words makāropajanaś chandasaḥ and varṇavyāpattyātvaṃ are doubtful [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"sudraviṇaḥ — O one with lovely wealth; adite — O indivisible [Agni]; sarvatātā — in the multitude of all rites, or (in faith) in all sacrifices, [him] who abides in faith; yasmai — to which sacrificer; anāgāstvaṃ — the fitness for rites that is free of sin; tvaṃ — you; dadāśaḥ — you who give (and); yaṃ — whom; bhadreṇa — with the benevolent; śavasā — strength; codayāsi — you join [with] (he prospers, that is certain; may we too); prajāvatā — full of sons, grandsons and the like; te rādhasā — with the wealth given by you; syāma — may we be (united)."

original p. 561

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, possessing lovely wealth and indivisible: the sacrificer to whom, abiding with faith in all sacrificial rites, you give the fitness for rites that is free of sin, and the sacrificer whom you join with strength that does good — he surely prospers. May we too, through your favour, be possessed of wealth together with sons, grandsons and the like."

English Translation (as printed)

Fortunate is the worshipper to whom (assiduous) in all pious works, you possessor of riches, indivisible Agni, grant exemption from sin, whom you associate with auspicious strength, may he be (enriched) by you with wealth that comprehends progeny.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.15 (Kannada)

sudraviṇaḥ — śobhanadhanaḥ: "'one who has lovely wealth', that is, 'one whose wealth is excellent'. In the Ṛksaṃhitā this epithet is used only as a synonym of Agni. In the Ṛk 10-61-21 [?], too, this epithet shows the excellence of Agni's wealth."

adite — "akhaṇḍanīyāgne — 'indivisible Agni'; or aditeḥ putra agne — 'O Agni, son of Aditi': it can be explained in two ways. In the first, aditi is taken to mean 'not poor' (adīnā), that is, 'not wasting away': Agni is said in many places to be free of decay and free of death." Glosses, editorial and tentative: "O Agni, saviour, immortal, worthy of offering, best sacrificer, bearer of oblations"; "never does the immortal, born of strength, fail, when as Hotṛ he became the messenger of Vivasvat".) "In many such contexts Agni is called deathless; so he may be called aditi. In the second sense, aditi is devamātā (Ni. 4-22 [?]), the 'mother of the gods', so Agni too is a son of Aditi; therefore, by adite is to be understood 'O son of Aditi', Skandasvāmin says. Or, since the Nirukta-author says agnir asyāditir ucyate (Ni. 11-23 [?]), aditi is a synonym (paryāya) of Agni;" (continues on p. 562

अग्ने त्रातारममृतं मियेध्य यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन । agne trātāram amṛtaṃ miyedhya yajiṣṭhaṃ havyavāhana | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-5 as read [?])

नू चित्सहोजा अमृतो नि तुन्दते होता यद्दूतो अभवद्विवस्वतः । nū cit sahojā amṛto ni tundate hotā yad dūto abhavad vivasvataḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-58-1 as read [?])

original p. 562

"…he says this, and cites this very Ṛk. adite then means 'O Agni'."

sarvatātā — "The Nirukta-author, citing this very Ṛk when explaining the word sarvatātā, gives the meaning sarvāsu karmatatiṣu, 'in the multitude of all sacrificial acts' (Ni. 11-23 [?]). The word sarvatātā is used generally as a synonym for 'sacrifice'. For example —"

देवानां दूतः पुरुध प्रसूतोऽनागान्नो वोचतु सर्वताता । devānāṃ dūtaḥ purudha prasūto 'nāgān no vocatu sarvatātā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?] [?], numeral as read "४-५४-१८" [?])

शतेतेमं वेश्यं सर्वताता दिवोदासमतिथिग्वं यदावम् । [?] śatetemaṃ veśyaṃ sarvatātā divodāsam atithigvaṃ yad āvam | [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-3 as read [?])

रायो मित्रावरुणा सर्वताता ईळे शोकाय तनयाय शं योः । rāye mitrāvaruṇā sarvatātā īḷe śokāya tanayāya śaṃ yoḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-3 as read [?])

The middle quotation is clotted in the print and the words are read as given, doubtful [?]. Glosses, editorial and tentative, for the first and third: "may he, the messenger of the gods, sent forth in many places, speak for us, sinless, in the rite"; "for riches, Mitra and Varuṇa, I invoke at the sacrifice, for the offspring, for weal and welfare". "In Ṛks like these also, and in 1-[?]-[?]; 2-[?]-[?] and many other Ṛks, the word sarvatātā is used as a synonym of 'sacrifice'. In this context it can be taken to mean 'in the midst of all rites'."

anāgāstvaṃ — "'Freedom from sin', or 'fitness for rites that is free from sin'. From ignorance, through any sort of lapse in the rites or any other kind of deficiency, with the faith 'Agni will release us from this fault', a prayer of this kind is made to Agni at every step. For example —"

यच्चिद्धि ते पुरुषत्रा यविष्ठाचित्तिभिश्चकृमा कच्चिदागः । कृधी ष्वस्माँ अदितेरनागान्व्येनांसि शिश्रथो विष्वगग्ने ॥ yac cid dhi te puruṣatrā yaviṣṭhācittibhiś cakṛmā kac cid āgaḥ | kṛdhī ṣv asmām̐ aditer anāgān vy enāṃsi śiśratho viṣvag agne ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-12-4 as read [?])

यत्क्षीमागश्च कृमा तत्सु मृळ तदर्यमादितिः शिश्रथन्तु । yat kṣīmāgaś ca kṛmā tat su mṛḷa tad aryamāditiḥ śiśrathantu | [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?] [?], numeral as read "२-४१-६" [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative, for the first: "whatever offence, youngest one, we have committed against you among the mortals through our lack of understanding — make us sinless before Aditi, loosen the sins on every side, Agni". The second quotation is clotted and is read as given, doubtful [?]. "In many such contexts the prayer to Agni that all sins be destroyed is made with deep repentance and with faith."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.15 grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 563

sudraviṇaḥ — "he who has lovely wealth": root dru (going); the suffix inan by drudakṣibhyām inan (Uṇ. 2-[?] [?]); after dru the suffix … continues on p. 563

original p. 563

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.15, continued from p. 562

sudraviṇaḥ, concluded: guṇa and av-substitution of the root's vowel through the suffix; since there is an r as cause, the n of the suffix becomes ṇ by aṭkupvāṅ… (Pā. 8-4-2 [?], the sūtra's end clotted); the form draviṇa. In the Saṃhitā an s-augment arises at the end of the word draviṇa in the Vedic manner (so the Kannada page, as read; the bhāṣya says makāropajana, see p. 560 [?]). In the vocative, because of the designation āmantrita, the nighāta accent arises by āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19 [?]). — dadāśaḥ — root dāśṛ (giving); leṭ, second person singular, sip; the i is elided by itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97 [?]); the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 [?]); ślu for śap by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-76 [?]); reduplication of the root by ślau (Pā. 6-1-10 [?]); the reduplicate shortened and beginning with the single consonant by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; in dadāśas the s becomes ru and visarga; initial acute by abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189 [?]); because the word is connected with yat, no nighāta. — sarvatātā — after the word sarva the suffix tātil by sarvadevāt tātil (Pā. 4-4-142 [?]); by liti (Pā. 6-1-193 [?]) the syllable before the suffix is acute. On Yāska's view, the bahuvrīhi sarvāḥ stutayaḥ yeṣu yāgeṣu, 'in which all praises are', sarvatātā; the ā comes by the Vedic substitution of letters, and by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 [?]) the first member keeps its natural accent. On both views ḍā replaces the seventh-case ending by supāṃ suluk… — codayāsi — root cud (urging); leṭ second person singular sip; since it belongs to the curādi class, ṇic in the sense of the root itself by satyāpapāśa… (Pā. 3-1-25 [?]); guṇa of the light penultimate vowel by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. 7-3-86 [?]); the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau; guṇa of the ṇic's i, then ay; because yat stood earlier and is connected with it, the nighāta does not arise; by the suffix accent the ā after the d is acute. — prajāvatā — "they have progeny": prajāvān; the suffix matup by tad asyāsty asminn iti matup (as read), added after a stem ending in a [as read]; m turns to v by mādupadhāyāś ca… (Pā. 8-2-9 [?]); the instrumental singular form. ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.16)

हे देव दानादिगुणयुक्ताग्ने स पूर्वोक्तगुणविशिष्टस्त्वं सौभगत्वस्य सुभगत्वं सौभाग्यं विद्वान् जानन् इहास्मिन् कर्मण्यस्माकमायुः प्र तिर । प्रवर्धय । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः । त्वया प्रवर्धितं नोऽस्माकं तदायुर्मित्रादयः षड्देवता मामहन्ताम् । पूजयन्ताम् । रक्षन्त्वित्यर्थः । मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्राता वरुणोऽनिष्टानां निवारयिता अदितिरदीनाखण्डनीयो वा देवमाता सिन्धुः स्यन्दनशीलोऽवकाशात्मा [?] देवता पृथिवी प्रथिता भूदेवता । उतेति समुच्चये । द्यौः प्रकाशमाना द्युलोकात्मा देवता । एताश्च सर्वा अग्निना प्रवर्धितमायुर्मामहन्तामिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ सौभगत्वस्य । सुभगस्य भावः सौभगं । सुभगान्मन्त्र [?] इत्यादि [?] त्वात्रादिषु पाठाद्वेऽइक् [?] । पुनरपि भावप्रत्ययोत्पत्तिश्छान्दसी । मामहन्ताम् । मह पूजायाम् । भौवादिकः । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् ॥

he deva dānādiguṇayuktāgne sa pūrvoktaguṇaviśiṣṭas tvaṃ saubhagatvasya subhagatvaṃ saubhāgyaṃ vidvān jānan ihāsmin karmaṇy asmākam āyuḥ pra tira | pravardhaya | prapūrvas tiratir vardhanārthaḥ | tvayā pravardhitaṃ no 'smākaṃ tad āyur mitrādayaḥ ṣaḍ devatā māmahantām | pūjayantām | rakṣantv ity arthaḥ | mitraḥ pramīter trātā varuṇo 'niṣṭānāṃ nivārayitā aditir adīnākhaṇḍanīyā vā devamātā sindhuḥ syandanaśīlo 'vakāśātmā [?] devatā pṛthivī prathitā bhūdevatā | uteti samuccaye | dyauḥ prakāśamānā dyulokātmā devatā | etāś ca sarvā agninā pravardhitam āyur māmahantām iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖ saubhagatvasya | subhagasya bhāvaḥ saubhagaṃ | subhagān mantra [?] ity ādi [?] tvātrādiṣu pāṭhād ve 'ik [?] | punar api bhāvapratyayotpattiś chāndasī | māmahantām | maha pūjāyām | bhauvādikaḥ | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | tujāditvād abhyāsasya dīrghatvam ‖

Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed): "O god Agni, endowed with qualities such as generosity, you of the qualities named before, knowing the nature of good fortune (saubhagatva), prolong (pra tira, 'increase': the root tir with pra has the sense of growth) our life in this rite. That life of ours, increased by you, may the six deities, Mitra and the rest, honour (māmahantām) — that is, protect. Mitra is the protector from death; Varuṇa the averter of ills; Aditi the not-poor, the indivisible, the mother of the gods; Sindhu the flowing, of the nature of open space [?], a goddess; Pṛthivī the widely spread, the earth-goddess; uta ('and') is in the sense of joining; Dyaus the shining, the goddess who is the heavenly world. All these are to be construed with 'may they honour the life increased by Agni' in the preceding." Grammatical tail: saubhagatvasya — from subhaga; the printed derivation is clotted and not reproduced [?]; māmahantām — mah (honour), bhvādi; in the imperative śap is elided by bahulaṃ chandasi, and the reduplicate's vowel is lengthened because the root belongs to the tuj-type group. The tail of the bhāṣya on saubhagatvasya is clotted at several words, marked [?].

original p. 565

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"deva — O one endowed with qualities such as giving; agne — O Agni; saḥ — you who are filled with all these qualities; tvaṃ — you; saubhagatvasya — the nature of good fortune; vidvān — knowing; iha — in this sacrificial rite; asmākam āyuḥ — our life; pra tira — increase; naḥ — our; tat — that life; mitraḥ — Mitra the protector; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa (who destroys ills); aditiḥ — the indivisible mother of the gods; sindhuḥ — the flowing river-goddess; pṛthivī — the spacious earth-mother; uta — and; dyauḥ — the shining goddess of the heavenly world; mamahantām — may they protect."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Agni, endowed with qualities such as giving, you are filled with all virtues; knowing the nature of good fortune, increase our life in this sacrificial rite. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the goddess of the flowing waters, the earth-mother, and the goddess of the heavenly world also increase our life and protect it."

English Translation (as printed)

Divine Agni, do you who know what is good fortune on this occasion, prolong our existence, and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi, ocean, earth and heaven preserve it to us.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.16 (Kannada)

sa tvam agne — "Since it is said 'such a one are you', it means: you, endowed with the qualities spoken of before — that is, in the preceding Ṛks —"

देवो देवानामसि मित्रो अद्भुतो वसुर्वसूनामसि चारुरध्वरे । devo devānām asi mitro adbhuto vasur vasūnām asi cārur adhvare | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-13 as read [?])

तत्ते भद्रं यत्समिद्धः स्वे दमे सोमाहुतो जरसे मृळयत्तमः । दधासि रत्नं द्रविणं च दाशुषेऽग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ tat te bhadraṃ yat samiddhaḥ sve dame somāhuto jarase mṛḷayattamaḥ | dadhāsi ratnaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dāśuṣe 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-14 as read [?])

"— and so on: Agni is addressed as the cause of all good fortune, of both the gods and of men." continues on p. 566

original p. 566

Special Topics of Rik 94.16, continued from p. 565 (Kannada)

saubhagatvasya vidvān — subhagasya bhāvaḥ saubhagaṃ | tasya bhāvaḥ |: "That is, one who knows all good fortunes and possessions. Since by epithets such as jātavedāḥ ('knower of all that is born') the omniscience of Agni is described, he knows fully the faith and devotion of the sacrificers, and their diligence in what is to be done, and the fruits proper to their good works, and bestows on them all good fortune and possessions."

asmākam āyuḥ pra tira — "'Make our life grow.' The Nirukta-author explains the words pra tira as pravardhaya, 'increase' (Ni. 10-40 [?], as read), and cites the Ṛk of the Ṛksaṃhitā —"

असुनीते मनो अस्मासु धारय जीवातवे सु प्र तिरा न आयुः । asunīte mano asmāsu dhāraya jīvātave su pra tirā na āyuḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-59-5 as read [?])

Gloss, editorial and tentative: "O Asunīti, set your mind on us; for our living, prolong our life well". "— and so shows it. In many contexts like these the meaning 'increase our life; may we live long' is given. In the same way here, asmākam āyuḥ pra tira means 'make our life grow', that is the sense."

tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ — "In these deities also, by Agni's grace, may they increase our good fortune and possessions, and make [us] honoured [the Kannada word read as pūjyāmānasa, doubtful [?]]; may they make them beneficial to our share. This is the last prayer of this Sūkta. From the beginning of the Sūkta up to here it has had Agni as its deity; but in the last half of the last Ṛk this prayer, addressed to all the gods, in this way, is the peculiarity of the composition of the seer Kutsa. This peculiarity is found also in the compositions of the seers Bharadvāja, Gṛtsamada and the rest. For this there is a well-known technical word, udarka ('closing', 'sequel'). The Bṛhaddevatā describes the udarka of the seer Kutsa in this way:" The three stanzas are transcribed from the Kannada script of the print; several words are clotted and are read as given, doubtful [?]: especially ṣoḷaśarcam, sto 'rdham, vātra ṣaḍbhiḥ prakṛtābhyaḥ, nodhasy agastye and nodarkā. The source gives no translation of the stanzas; the Kannada that follows on p. 567 explains their sense.

इमं कुत्स आङ्गिरसो ददर्श जातवेदस्यं जगाद षोळशर्चम् । पूर्वो देवा इत्यृचो देवदेवास्त्रयः पादा उत्तमायाः स्तोऽर्धम् ॥ imaṃ kutsa āṅgiraso dadarśa jātavedasyaṃ jagāda ṣoḷaśarcam | pūrvo devā ity ṛco devadevās trayaḥ pādā uttamāyāḥ sto 'rdham ‖

तस्यैव वा यस्य तत्पूर्वसूक्तं मित्रादिभ्यो वात्र षड्भिः प्रकृताभ्यः । अन्त्योऽर्धर्चस्तु वा षण्णां स्तुतानां पूर्वो देवाः पादैस्तु द्विभिः स्तुताः ॥ tasyaiva vā yasya tat pūrvasūktaṃ mitrādibhyo vātra ṣaḍbhiḥ prakṛtābhyaḥ | antyo 'rdharcas tu vā ṣaṇṇāṃ stutānāṃ pūrvo devāḥ pādais tu dvibhiḥ stutāḥ ‖

भरद्वाजे गृत्समदे वसिष्ठे नोधस्यगस्त्ये विमदे नभाके । कुत्से नोदर्का बहुदैवतेषु तथा द्विदेवेषु समानधर्मिणः ॥ bharadvāje gṛtsamade vasiṣṭhe nodhasy agastye vimade nabhāke | kutse nodarkā bahudaivateṣu tathā dvideveṣu samānadharmiṇaḥ ‖ (Bṛhaddevatā III. 126–128, as printed in the source in Roman reference)

original p. 567

"The seer Kutsa Āṅgirasa received the vision of this Sūkta (1-94) and hymned it, sixteen Ṛks, as concerned with Jātavedas. The first three pādas of the 8th Ṛk, which begins pūrvo devāḥ, and the latter half of the last Ṛk are addressed to many deities. In the Sūktas of Bharadvāja, Gṛtsamada, Vasiṣṭha, Nodhas, Agastya, Vimada and Nabhāka also, although there are such udarkas, whether they are of many deities or of two deities, they do not have the same characteristic as the refrain (pallavi) in the udarka of the seer Kutsa; thus the peculiarity in the composition of the seer Kutsa is shown."

"Altogether, in the compositions of eight seers such udarkas are found at the ends of Sūktas. In none of them is the last half of the Sūkta addressed to many deities [as read, doubtful [?]]. This matter will be considered in detail, with examples, in the exposition of the next Sūkta."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.16

saubhagatvasya — subhagasya bhāvaḥ saubhagam; because subhagān mantre is read as such in the udgātrādi group (as read), a suffix (the Kannada print gives phiñ [?]) arises in the sense of 'state'; being ñit, it gives vṛddhi of the first vowel. saubhaga itself means 'state' [of being subhaga]; where the sense of 'state' is to be shown again, the suffix tva has to be added to the word saubhaga, in the Vedic manner; by the suffix accent the word is final-acute. — tira — the root tir with the prefix pra, in the sense of increase; loṭ, second person singular; tiṅanta, nighāta accent. — mamahantām [Saṃhitā māmahantām] — root maha (honouring), bhvādi; loṭ, third person plural, jha → anta by jho 'ntaḥ (as read); āmetaḥ (Pā. 3-4-90 [?]) turns the e produced in the loṭ into ām; śap gets ślu by bahulaṃ chandasi; reduplication of the root by ślau; the reduplicate keeps the first consonant by halādiśeṣa; since the root belongs to the tuj-type group, the reduplicate's vowel is lengthened by tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya (Pā. 6-1-7 [?]); nighāta accent, since it follows a tiṅanta. ‖ 16 ‖

Closing line of the print: "94ne sūktavu samāptavāgide" — "The 94th Sūkta is complete." Printed in Kannada after the grammar page of Rik 94.16; a printer's ornament follows. No further colophon, and no closing line for the Sixth Adhyāya, appears in the scan.

16. SOURCE PAGE MISSING: the scan carries printed p. 513 in this place

¶ The page occupying PDF 428 is headed "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 30 [?]" on the left, "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā" in the centre and "513" on the right, with the printer's signature "33 … Volume 7" at the foot. It is a stray page of the commentary on a later Sūkta (the Agni-Sūkta 94: Bṛhaddevatā quotations on jātavedas, the line imaṃ stomaṃ rathām iva saṃ mahema, and tava sakhye vayaṃ mā riṣāma), and the same page appears again at its proper place, PDF 528 = printed p. 513. Printed p. 413 itself — which, by the sequence of the text, should hold the end of the Special Topics of Rik 92.3 and the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of 92.3 — is not in the scan. The signature number confirms the intrusion (signature 33 belongs to printed pp. 513–528, whereas p. 413 would be in signature 27). Nothing of Rik 92.3's remaining commentary can therefore be translated; the page is to be translated at its own place (printed p. 513) when that is reached, and the missing p. 413 is noted as a gap in the source, to be supplied from another copy if the user can provide one.
